The Collaboration on International ICT Policy in East and Southern Africa (CIPESA),

 the Forum on Internet Freedom in Africa 2026 (FIFAfrica26) set to take place on

Over the past decade, the FIFAfrica conference

As open spaces for human rights conversations continue to shrink, convenings such as these are more important than ever.


Access Now has been a key partner of CIPESA and continues to actively participate in FIFAfrica to strengthen our partnership and expand our network within Africa and beyond. We are happy to be part of this year’s FIFAfrica.

author: By Camilla Donzelli, Contributor
title: A Failed Reception System in Crete Turns People on the Move Into Political Targets
content:
Athanatoi, Greece — Residents of a small village in Northern Crete, near Herakleion, are fighting the Greek government’s plan to convert a disused factory into a reception center for people on the move, escalating a monthslong standoff that pits xenophobic backlash against an increasingly securitized European border regime. 


“We’re not staying silent. We’re not backing down. No to the camp.” The slogan, painted in red and black across a large banner, hangs from the gate of a factory facing the Candia-Mires state highway, near the village of Athanatoi in northern Crete. A few yards away, a second banner reads: “No camp — the people have a voice.”


A banner reading “We’re not staying silent. We’re not backing down. No to the camp,” hanging from the gate of a factory opposite the abandoned Skouloudis industrial complex. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Across the road stands the disused Skouloudis industrial complex, recently identified by Greece’s Ministry of Migration and Asylum as a site to be converted into a reception center for migrants crossing the stretch of sea between Libya and Greece and landing on the island’s southern coast. Since Minister Thanos Plevris

announced

 the plan in mid-June 2026, Skouloudis has been at the center of a

bitter standoff

 between authorities and local communities.


The former Skouloudis industrial facility, seen from the Heraklion–Mires state highway. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


The choice of this industrial site, however, is only the latest development in a long and contested decision-making process that began in the summer of 2025, when

arrivals in Crete

 far outpaced those recorded along the Aegean route — the sea passage from Turkey to the Greek islands of Lesbos, Samos and Chios that has long been the country’s primary migration corridor — making the island Greece’s main point of entry.


Against a backdrop of chronic absence of adequate first-reception facilities on the island, the handling of landings has fallen to entirely

unsustainable emergency measures

.


The main temporary holding site in Heraklion remains the former psygeio — a Coast Guard cold-storage building in the port area. Meant to hold just 70 to 80 people, the site held more than 450 in the first months of 2026, forcing men, women and children to sleep on the floor.


The lack of adequate sanitation and ventilation created dire health conditions, while pressure to find an alternative mounted further as the Port Authority pursued legal action to clear the site. Faced with this infrastructural collapse, authorities found themselves forced to publicly propose a solution.


One of the rooms inside the temporary first-reception facility known as Psygeio, in the port of Heraklion, where people are held after their arrival. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Locked Up and Criminalized: People on the Move Face a Broken System on Crete’s Shores


Between Delay and Denial 


In the summer of 2025, the government

announced

 the conversion of several military sites, but that announcement was followed by months of silence and effective inaction. Only in February 2026 did the Greek Parliament approve the opening of

two centers

, without specifying their location or how they would be built.


The first details came only months later: in Chania, authorities settled on retrofitting

Agya

, a former exhibition center already in use as a temporary reception facility; in Heraklion, the disused Skouloudis industrial plant was identified instead.


“These delays and constant changes of plan shouldn’t be read as political strategy, but as failure,” Michalis Markodimitrakis, a member of the Heraklion-based collective Thalassa of Solidarity and a researcher at the Hellenic Mediterranean University, told Unicorn Riot.


“Local communities and representatives of Crete’s tourism and cultural sector are pushing back hard, because they see the presence of migrants as damaging to the island’s image and a threat to their economic interests.”


Michalis Markodimitrakis, member of Thalassa of Solidarity collective


A side view of the former Skouloudis industrial facility, where adaptation works to accommodate people on the move have not yet begun. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Back in July 2025, the day after the first announcement floated the opening of the centers, a network of tourism industry associations sent an

open letter

 to Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and Migration and …

title: Debian Edu goes Lomiri - Freie Tablets für die Schule [24. Kielux 2026]
content:
Ein Vortrag von Mike Gabriel


Dieser Vortrag gibt dir einen kurzen Überblick, was Debian Edu ist und was der aktuelle Status des Projekts ist. Und dieser Vortrag gibt dir in ähnlicher Weise einen kurzen Überblick, was Lomiri ist und was der aktuelle Status von Lomiri in Debian ist (mit einem kleiner 'Rüberspäher auf Ubuntu Touch).


Der Vortrag erzählt dann eine Geschichte über Möglichkeiten, kommerzielle vendor-locked-in Tablet-Lösungen in Klassenzimmern zu ersetzen gegen alternative Ansätze auf Basis von Debian / Debian Edu in Kombination mit Lomiri (die von Ubuntu Touch genutzte Telefon- und Tablet-Bedienoberfläche).


Zusätzlich möchten wir im Rahmen dieses Vortrags Entwickler ermutigen, Apps für Lomiri / Ubuntu Touch / Debian Edu Lomiri Tablets zu entwickeln, die auf Use Cases im Bildungsbereich abzielen. Apps, die in Ubuntu Touch bereitgestellt werden, portieren wir für die Bereitstellung in Debian und laden sie als Pakete nach Debian hoch, um sie dann anschließend im Debian Edu Installer bereitstellen zu können.


In einem unserer gegenwärtigen Projekte bei der Fre(i)e[n] Software GmbH wurde uns über einen Zeitraum von zwei Jahre ausreichend Budget zur Verfügung gestellt, um Lomiri für das Debian 14 (aka forky) Release in die Debian Distribution zu integrieren und einen für Tablets angepassten Installationsmodus innerhalb von Debian Edu zu integrieren. Auch für die Entwicklung von schulgeeigneten Ubuntu Touch / Lomiri Apps steht theoretisch Budget zur Verfügung.


Der Vortrag wurde auf den Kieler Open Source und Linux Tagen im Jahr 2026 gehalten.


Für Inhalt und Richtigkeit sind ausschließlich die jeweiligen Referenten verantwortlich.

author: Devanshi Nishar
title: DraftKings Is Using AI to Supercharge the Harms of Online Behavioral Advertising
content:
Online sports betting company DraftKings is using AI to target customers who are most likely to place losing bets and respond to gambling promotions. This kind of targeting is a form of online behavioral advertising, which is when companies personalize the ads they show you based on the data they’ve collected about you. The more data a company has, the more personalized the ad can be. While DraftKings is using AI to supercharge the harmful effects of online behavioral advertising, EFF has long argued that all behavioral advertising should be banned.

According to the New York Times, DraftKings is using its customers’ betting records to train a machine learning model to find losing gamblers. Once found, DraftKings sends these customers targeted advertising designed to lure them back to the site to place more bets—bets that DraftKings thinks will be losing ones. DraftKings has a business incentive to keep losing gamblers coming back to their site, because these are the users actually making DraftKings money. Unfortunately, those considered “problem gamblers” (people who repeatedly gamble despite harm to themselves, their finances, and their relationships) are highly likely to be targeted by this model. By re-engaging these individuals through targeted promotions aimed at keeping them on the platform, DraftKings is capitalizing on their vulnerability for profit instead of mitigating their risk.

Predatory online behavioral advertising isn’t new, but companies’ use of AI to process data and target customers has magnified its harms. Online behavioral advertising incentivizes the collection of vast quantities of data to power ad tech. Adding AI into the mix means that even more data is collected to train and refine models. Because AI operates as a black box, the humans building the models can rarely predict which data points are the most useful to the AI, driving them to continuously collect more data. AI also allows companies to process enormous data sets much faster, and, as a result, supercharges the harms of online behavioral advertising.

A direct consequence of online behavioral advertising is that it provides the data the surveillance industry needs to run. Data collected for targeted placement of ads is being sold to insurance companies, banks, and state and federal government law enforcement agencies such as CBP. ICE is also taking an interest in the data fueling ad tech: earlier this year, ICE published a Request for Information “seeking information to better understand how the industry’s commercial Big Data and Ad Tech providers can directly support investigations activities.”

DraftKings seems to be using solely “first party data” to target their ads, meaning that they’re using only the data they collect directly from their users and are not buying any additional data from third parties to fuel their machine learning model. This highlights how policy solutions that only limit third-party data sharing and selling would not be enough to prevent these predatory advertisements. Rather, policymakers must ban online behavioral ads.

What DraftKings is doing with their targeted promotions is just one example of how online behavioral advertising causes real harm to real people. But there are ways to take back control over your own data: EFF offers resources such as our Surveillance Self Defense project, along with other tips for how you can protect yourself on mobile apps and on websites.

DraftKings’ use of AI to target losing gamblers illustrates how ad tech evolves and how companies find new ways to use our data against us. This is why EFF believes that all behavioral advertising should be banned. If companies can’t send personalized ads, they’ll have less incentive to collect the behavioral data powering them.

author: Jake Bittle
title: UN passes first declaration on sea level rise, protecting island nations’ sovereignty
content:
President Donald Trump’s second term has been a nightmare for global cooperation on climate change. Trump has yanked the United States from the Paris climate agreement,

attacked

 a global agreement on a carbon tax for cargo ships, and

threatened

 countries with tariffs if they get too vocal about climate. 


This week brought a notable exception. World leaders at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday approved a unanimous resolution on how to handle sea level rise, and the United States did not block it from moving forward. The passage of the accord represents a rare win for multilateralism, made all the more notable by the fact that the agreement includes references to climate change and climate aid for developing countries. 


The declaration could bring new momentum to efforts to help small island states, said Philip Davis, the prime minister of the Bahamas, in an interview with Grist.


“Our landmass is less than three meters above sea level, we are already seeing our land being swallowed by water, and the global effort to stem the carbon footprint has stalled,” he said. “I think this declaration will perhaps heighten the flow of action.”


For many low-lying countries, the implications of this agreement could be profound. Some island nations, like Tuvalu and

the Marshall Islands

, face almost total inundation over the next century as rising temperatures melt the world’s ice sheets and glaciers. It had never been clear what would happen to those sovereign nations. Under the agreement, those states will continue to exist as political actors even if their landmass disappears. They’ll also retain control over their old maritime borders, the stretch of sea extending from the coastline over which a country has exclusive control for fishing, energy development, and other military and economic activity. 


An aerial view of a strip of land between the Pacific Ocean and a lagoon in Funafuti, Tuvalu. The island nation of around 11,000 people is facing total inundation as sea levels rise.


Photo by Mario Tama / Getty Images


The declaration is the result of a campaign by the Alliance of Small Island States, an influential bloc of low-lying island nations. Recent rulings from international legal bodies have helped affirm countries’ continued rights in the face of sea level rise, but the world’s leaders had never endorsed those rulings. 


“What was long treated as a legal ‘presumption’ is now an affirmation,” said Kamal Amakrane, the managing director of the Global Center for Climate Mobility and the climate envoy for Trinidad and Tobago, which helped initiate talks toward a global declaration. He noted that the world has agreed to preserve small islands “by consensus, in a year when consensus has been hard to come by.”


The document enshrines strong protections for states at risk of losing land. It holds that countries “can … maintain their maritime zones in the face of physical changes resulting from sea level rise,” a principle that the document calls a “presumption in favor of continued statehood.” That echoes a

landmark climate ruling

 from the International Court of Justice last year, which held that “once a State is established, the disappearance of one of its constituent elements would not necessarily entail the loss of its statehood,” and which affirmed that international law requires countries to respect one another’s established borders.


The declaration will go a long way toward helping secure the future of small island states. For the Bahamas, protecting pristine ocean territory is essential to its tourism-driven economy. Davis said that the legal protections will safeguard his country and others against efforts to claim ocean territory for industries like

deep-sea mining

.


“This cannot be a free-for-all,” he said. “This cannot be might is right, and might takes what is there.”


The agreement also includes strong language recognizing that developed countries and historic emitters have an “urgent” obligation to provide “expanded access” to adaptation funds for small island states. This money could build sea walls or restore mangrove forests to protect coastlines from rising water, or it could help relocate populations from floodprone areas. 


Prime Minister Philip Davis of the Bahamas addresses the United Nations General Assembly in September 2025. The Bahamas is seeking to protect its ocean territory from exploitation as its land disappears.


Photo by Charly Triballeau / AFP via …

author: Paul Prescod
title: Philadelphia Orchestra Musicians Protect Their Hearing and Their Craft
content:
Philadelphia Orchestra musicians have won first-in-the-nation protections against hearing loss. The groundbreaking provisions, which could serve as a model for other orchestras, are part of a contract just ratified by Musicians (AFM) Local 77-274.


They also secured a raise of almost 13 percent over three years, which will help keep pace with inflation and attract high-quality artists. But for the musicians, the most important gains related to their working conditions and artistic integrity.


The orchestra usually performs classical music without amplification, but sometimes plays in a supporting role to pop artists who use large sound systems. During one such performance last year, the musicians were seated right next to unbearably loud speakers, with no way to address the situation.


“Our phones were blowing up about it afterwards, and we knew this had to be a priority,” said Local 77-274 Vice President Marjorie Goldberg.


STOP THE CONCERT


The issue goes beyond discomfort. Hearing loss can impact a musician’s career, especially one who performs very precise classical music in an ensemble.


Under the new contract, decibel meters will be placed onstage during rehearsals and performances. If the sound levels get too high for too long, musicians can remove themselves or even stop the concert.


Artists performing with the orchestra will be required to attend rehearsals to ensure that sound details are worked out in advance. And management will provide a $150 allowance for musicians to buy professional-level hearing protection.


The union also proposed, and management agreed, to open up unlimited opportunities for students of all ages to attend dress rehearsals and sometimes meet with members of the orchestra. Experiences like these can spark a lifelong interest in the arts.


“It’s very important for developing the next generation of musicians and music-lovers,” said violinist Dara Morales, a member of the bargaining committee.


In addition, management will be required to meet at least quarterly with the musicians’ education committee to discuss ways to improve outreach.


Increasingly, the orchestra has been asked to do concerts where they perform the soundtrack while a movie is shown. But a movie soundtrack is written to be recorded in small chunks in a recording studio, not for hours at a time.


Playing it all straight through, live, can be very physically demanding and even put the musician at risk of long-term physical injury due to repetitive motion. For brass players, these scores often call for sustained playing of loud and high notes in a way that’s not common in symphonic pieces.


Now the orchestra has a limit of two film programs per subscription season. This also provides opportunities for other orchestras that are more used to playing that type of program, such as the Philly Pops.


STARTED EARLY


The orchestra’s last contract fight was much more contentious and almost led to a strike. This go-round, the union started laying the groundwork earlier, beginning with a detailed survey on priorities. Substitutes and extras were surveyed as well.


“This time we were very prepared,” said Local 77-274 President Ellen Trainer.


Though management didn’t push back as hard as it did three years ago, members still had to organize pressure. When CEO Ryan Fleur stopped showing up to bargaining sessions, the union launched a petition demanding he be present. Every single orchestra member signed. Fleur started appearing again.


After one concert, musicians passed out flyers thanking the audience for supporting classical music. During movie-soundtrack concerts, they wore their union T-shirts.


Principal players—the section leaders for each group of instruments—signed a petition demanding that substitute players receive pension contributions, which had been eliminated for them when the orchestra declared bankruptcy in 2012. Now substitutes will receive a 5 percent pension contribution starting in year three of the contract.


The bargaining committee used a phone tree to keep in touch with members and coordinate actions. Once the committee met for two hours after a concert that ended at 11 p.m.


A UNION FAMILY


The contract reflects years of bottom-up organizing to transform the local.


A slate of reform leaders won office in 2019. They ran to rebuild a union they saw as stagnant and unresponsive. Before, “people didn’t feel like the union did anything except take dues,” Trainer said.


Freelancers worked …

author: unoffensiveadmin
title: GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT AUGUST ROUND UP
content:
There’s been some huge wins for the grassroots animal rights space in August.


Right at the start of the month, Southampton Animal Action convinced Brittany Ferries to end the live export of farmed animals from Ireland to France.


They protested and disrupted ports, offices, and shareholders across the South Coast and London for a year. Concerned the protests might escalate to demonstrations at sea, Brittany Ferries’ CEO gave them his personal WhatsApp number, arranged a series of meetings, and agreed to end the vile trade! The win has sent the Irish farming sector into crisis mode, and they are warning that if a replacement isn’t found soon. All eyes are now on Irish Ferries, the only remaining live exporter for the Irish farming industry. This is an incredible opportunity for our grassroots movement to strike a powerful blow against the dairy industry.


More incredible news from Scotland as grassroots activists and national organisation Protect the Wild have just saved 4,000 lives!


Following a sustained campaign against the Guga Hunt, which sees ten men from the Scottish island of Lewis bludgeon baby gannets to death for a local delicacy, the hunt’s licence has been revoked! In support of the Protect the Wild campaign, grassroots activists smashed windows, painted buildings, and occupied rooftops. The licence will not be issued for 2026, and the licensing body, NatureScot, has indicated this will continue through 2027. Gannets are an endangered species, and the licence is allowed only because of a deliberate loophole in the law. Campaigners are now pushing to close this loophole and make the hunt permanently illegal.


MBR Acres, the notorious puppy factory that breeds dogs for research, continues to sink into shit. Quite literally, it turns out, as their waste management company pulled out, leaving them stacking tonnes of dog poo in rubble sacks behind their buildings. The MBR Suppliers campaign (www.mbrsuppliers.is or MBR Suppliers on FB) is impressively deconstructing the company, leaving them with no working toilets (for the last year!), no gardeners (their security have to trim the hedges to allow lorries in), at risk of being delisted from Companies House, and their £250,000 office building remains unfinished because no one wants to build it.


The National Animal Rights March saw thousands of people marching for animal freedom in London. This is the fifth month in a row that activists have taken to the UK streets en masse for the animals! The Animal Freedom Network has announced that 25 local animal rights communities have formed as part of their efforts to help support and grow the grassroots space. An exciting initiative that is already seeing great results! Their national gathering is on September 25-27 – more info at www.animalfreedom.org.uk.

title: La répression continue : 8 nouvelles interpellations dans l'affaire Deranque
content:
La répression judiciaire sur les antifascistes lyonnais continue. Après quelques mois de silence, le travail de la Sous-direction anti-terroriste (

SDAT

), associée au dossier depuis le mois de mars a fini par payer et a mené à l'arrestation de 8 nouvelles personnes, dont 5 ont été mises en examen pour "association de malfaiteurs".


Entre le 17 et le 18 février, le parquet de Lyon et le procureur Thierry Dran avaient déjà fait arrêter 11 personnes sur la qualification lunaire d' «

 

homicide volontaire

 

», suivant complètement le narratif médiatique de l'extrême-droite. Quelques jours plus tard, on apprenait la confirmation par des témoins dans divers articles de presse que la bagarre de rue était en réalité un guet-apens raté mis en place par les fafs en coordination avec le collectif Némésis. Le 4 mars, 2 nouvelles personnes étaient interpellées par la Direction de la Criminalité Territoriale (

DCT

) dans le Rhône et dans l'Aube. Sur ces 13 premières interpellations, 9 personnes demeuraient mises en examen et incarcérée ce mois de septembre.


On apprend aujourd'hui dans le Progrès, qui cite carrément que ses sources viennent du torchon fasciste Boulevard Voltaire, que 8 nouvelles personnes ont été interpellées le jeudi 24 septembre. 5 personnes au total ont été mises en examen pour "associationde malfaiteur, 4 également pour "violences aggravées par trois circonstances (avec usage ou menace d'une arme, en réunion et en dissimulant volontairement tout ou partie du visage afin de ne pas être identifiées)". Trois ont été placées en détention provisoire et deux en contrôle judicaire.


L'affaire constitue une réelle aubaine pour la répression de s'acharner sur les milieux antifascistes dans un contexte de fascisation évident. Ces arrestations au compte-goutte, outre que de légitimer la fiction libérale de justice démocratique qui veillerait à éliminer les éléments "violents" du paysage républicain, ont clairement pour but de terroriser la mobilisation antifasciste et plus largement le mouvement social qui s'opposent à la vague réactionnaire nationale et internationale.


Continuons à garder la ligne et à faire front contre la répression qui touche ces camarades en leur apportant toute la solidarité possible, à l'intérieur des murs et à l'extérieur.


À jamais antifascistes.

title: Netanyahu BM kürsüsüne çıkarken onlarca ülke temsilcisi Genel Kurulu terk etti
content:
İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu, Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) 81. Genel Kurulu'nda konuşmak üzere 24 Eylül Perşembe günü kürsüye çıktığında onlarca ülkenin diplomatik temsilcisi ayağa kalkarak Genel Kurul salonunu terk etti.


Netanyahu konuşmaya başlayınca salonda yuhalama sesleri yükseldi. İsrail heyeti ve galerideki Netanyahu destekçileri ise ayağa kalkarak alkışladı ve İbranice sloganlar attı. Oturum başkanı salondakileri düzeni korumaya çağırdı. 


Netanyahu protestoya kürsüden karşılık verdi:


“Bu salondan henüz çıkmamış başka ahlaki korkaklar varsa, lütfen şimdi ayrılsınlar.”


Filistin heyeti toplu çıkış çağrısı yaptı


Genel Kurul'daki protesto öncesinde Filistin heyeti BM'deki diplomatik misyonlara gönderdiği notta, Netanyahu'nun konuşması sırasında salonu terk etmeleri çağrısında bulunmuştu. Çağrıda, eylemle İsrail hükümetinin Gazze'de yürüttüğü savaşa ve Batı Şeria'daki politikalarına yönelik bir ortak diplomatik mesaj verilmesi önerilmişti. 


Reuters'in geçtiği görüntülerde Netanyahu kürsüye gelirken delegelerin gruplar halinde çıkışlara yöneldiği ve İsrail Başbakanı'nın hemen hemen boş bir Genel Kurul salonuna hitaben konuştuğu görüldü.


Netanyahu: "İran'a saldırmak en kolay kararlarımdan biriydi"


Netanyahu konuşmasının ağırlık merkezinde Gazze'nin yanı sıra İran'la savaş ve İsrail'in bölgedeki askeri operasyonlarının savunulmasını yerleştirmişti. İsrail Başbakanı İran'a saldırma kararı için “Hayatımda verdiğim en kolay kararlardan biriydi” dedi. 


Netanyahu, konuşmasında İran'a yönelik saldırılarını da savundu; İran yönetiminin sonunda kendi halkı tarafından devrileceğini ileri sürdü ve İsrail'in yürüttüğü savaşların, ülkesinin varlığını korumak açısından zorunlu olduğunu savundu.


Konuşma, Gazze'deki savaş dolayısıyla Netanyahu üzerindeki uluslararası baskının arttığı, Batı Şeria'daki yerleşimlerin genişletilmesine karşı yeni yaptırım girişimlerinin gündeme geldiği ve İsrail'in geleneksel müttefikleri arasında da Netanyahu hükümetine verilen desteğin azaldığı bir dönemde gerçekleşti. 


BM Genel Kurulu dışında da protesto 


Netanyahu'ya yönelik protestolar BM Genel Kurulu'yla sınırlı kalmadı. Konuşması sürerken BM binası çevresinde yüzlerce Filistinli, Yahudi, İranlı ve Lübnanlı New York sakiniyle birlikte savaş karşıtı göstericiler toplandı. Göstericiler “Yaşasın Gazze” ve “Bütün dünya izliyor” sloganları attı; bazıları “İnsanları finanse edin, bombaları değil” yazan tişörtlerle yürüdü. 


Göstericilerin bir bölümü BM Genel Merkezi yakınındaki yollarda yaklaşık bir saat boyunca oturma eylemi yaparak trafiği engelledi. Resmî konvoyların güzergâhları değiştirildi.


Polis oturma eylemine müdahale ederek göstericileri gözaltına aldı. Düzenleyiciler, aralarında Hannah Einbinder ve Susan Sarandon gibi sinema oyuncularının da bulunduğu 100'ü aşkın kişinin gözaltına alındığını bildirdi. 


“ABD hükümeti İsrail'i finanse etmeyi bıraksın”


Eylemin düzenleyicileri arasında Barış Eylemi İçin Yahudi Sesi (Jewish Voice for Peace Action-JVP Action) hareketi de vardı. Örgütün siyasal yöneticisi Beth Miller, Netanyahu'nun New York ziyaretine karşı gösterilerin yalnızca Filistin dayanışma hareketinin değil, Yahudi Amerikalılar arasındaki muhalefetin de büyüdüğünü gösterdiğini söyledi.


ABD'nin İsrail'e askeri desteğinin sona erdirilmesini isteyen oyuncu Hannah Einbinder protestoya katılma gerekçesini şöyle açıkladı:


“Bir Yahudi, bir Amerikalı ve bir insan olarak konuşmak ve ABD'nin bunu finanse etmeyi bırakmasını istemek ahlaki yükümlülüğüm.”


New York Belediye Başkanı da Netanyahu'ya karşı


Netanyahu'nun BM ziyareti, New York Belediye Başkanı Zohran Mamdani ve İsrail Başbakanı arasındaki sert siyasi çatışma sürerken gerçekleşti.


Mamdani daha önce Netanyahu'yu “savaş suçlusu” olarak nitelemiş ve New York'ta istenmediğini söylemişti. Seçim kampanyasında Netanyahu New York'a gelirse tutuklanması gerektiğini savunan Mamdani, tutuklama emri verme yetkisinin bulunmadığını kabul etmiş ve sorumluluğun federal makamlarda olduğunu belirtmişti.


Netanyahu ise BM konuşmasında Mamdani'yi de hedef aldı ve New York Belediye Başkanı'nı İsrail'in Gazze'deki eylemleri konusunda “yalanlar yaymakla” suçladı.


Mamdani protestolardan önce yaptığı açıklamada gösterilere katılmayacağını ancak New Yorkluların protesto hakkının korunacağını söyledi


“Onlara her zaman söylediğim şey, bu kentte protesto etme haklarının olduğudur.”


Netanyahu Genel Kurul'da üçünü kez protesto ediliyor

author: nublogs.org
title: They tried to bury us, but didn’t know we are seeds! Neues Archiv mit allen Noblogsseiten eröffnet!
content:
Ihr könnt alle alten noblogs.org-Seiten wie xy.noblogs.org jetzt unter xy.nUblogs.org finden.


Ende August hat die US-Regierung Autistici/Inventati (A/I), und damit auch die Blogs von Noblogs, in die Knie gezwungen. (Mehr Infos dazu:

https://de.indymedia.org/node/859454

 und

https://unicornriot.ninja/2026/activist-blogging-platform-shuts-down-after-terrorism-designation/

)


In einem Statement von A/I heißt es danach:


„Geht also hin und vermehrt euch. Kopiert uns. Kopiert, was wir getan haben. Kopiert den Code, den wir verwendet haben. Kopiert die Idee, der wir Gestalt zu geben versucht haben. Oder nehmt einfach, was ihr von uns braucht, und remixt es. Wenn es etwas gibt, das unsere Gegner fürchten und verabscheuen – jetzt, in der Vergangenheit und für immer –, dann ist es unsere Fähigkeit, den Virus der Selbstverwaltung und Selbstbestimmung zu verbreiten und Infrastrukturen des Widerstands fraktal zu replizieren.


Autistici/Inventati, das sind nicht nur wir. Autistici/Inventati mag sterben, aber Tausende sind bereits geboren worden und Tausende weitere werden entstehen.“


Wir haben heute einen ersten Schritt getan. Nun könnt ihr alle früheren Noblogsseiten unter .nublogs.org erreichen! Schreibt dafür einfach den Namen der Website (was bisher [Name].noblogs.org war) vor .nublogs.org. Leider ist das Ganze ein Archiv und es können keine neuen Artikel aufgenommen werden.


Helft euch gegenseitig und baut neue Server auf!


 


Quelle:

https://nublogs.org/


 


passiert am 18.09.2026

title: Суд признал нарушенными права Азата Мифтахова в связи с недопуском его супруги в качестве защитницы в ИК: новый сбор на поддержку политзаключённого
content:
Однако при этом суд в Лабытнанги (ЯНАО), проходивший 24 сентября, отказался считать сотрудников колонии нарушителями, а ещё УФСИН не нашёл нарушений в прогулке во дворике, ставшем бассейном, передаёт RusNews. Супруга Азата Елена Горбань и его представитель участвовали в заседании по ВКС из Троицкого суда (Новая Москва).

Ранее, 22 сентября, супруге Азата и его представителю не дали даже заслушать решение суда. Суд в Лабытнанги удалился для принятия решения, а Троицкий суд сразу отключил ВКС со словами, что у них следующее заседание и вообще они рассчитывали только на час. Защита Азата тогда отказалась участвовать в заседании из-за того, что им не слышно суд по ВКС, а сам политзек отказался отвечать на вопросы без представителя.

Все 4 раза, когда Елену не пустили в ИК, признали незаконными. А вот действия полковника и подполковника внутренней службы Пилипчика и Цыбульского нарушениями не признали. Присудить денежную компенсацию за нарушение условий содержания Азата суд тоже отказался.

Также Елена получила отписку от УФСИН по поводу случая, когда Азата вывели гулять в сильный ливень во дворик без стока для воды. Он рассказал, что, захлопывая дверь, сотрудник сказал: «Надеюсь, ты умеешь плавать». Азату пришлось залезть ногами на скамейку и час ждать, когда за ним придут.

«Мифтахов был заранее предупреждён, что на улице сыро. Вопросов о умении его плавать осуждённому не задавались», — ответили в ведомстве. Там добавили, что «на дуплексную связь поступил звонок от Мифтахова с обращением к сотруднику по факту нахождения в прогулочном дворике сырости, где данному осуждённому было разъяснено, что в других двориках аналогичная ситуация».

Группа поддержки Азата объявила новый сбор на его защиту и бытовые нужды.

«После того, как применение пыток к Азату в «Полярной сове» в Харпе в начале мая получило огласку, - пишет группа поддержки. - Нам в рамках объявленного сбора средств — на работу адвокатов и сопутствующие траты — набежала достаточно крупная сумма денег.

Благодаря финансовой свободе у нас была возможность обеспечить визиты к Азату адвоката из Харпа и поездки к нему за Полярный круг защитников: адвоката Светланы Сидоркиной и жены Елены.

Кроме того, с мая по настоящий день прошло не менее 10 судебных заседаний, связанных с нарушениями, допущенными колонией в адрес Азата, а также с попытками не дать замять ситуацию с пытками.

Мы добились нескольких важных побед. А что самое главное — обеспечили некоторую безопасность Азату в колонии в тысячах километров от Москвы благодаря «руке на пульсе». Но все это стоило нам больших денежных вложений.

Спустя пять месяцев со страшных событий, полных скурпулёзной борьбы с бюрократически-репрессивной системой, наш горшочек с золотом прохудился. Это вынуждает нас объявить новый сбор».

author: Redazione_web
title: Attacco omofobo in Turchia
content:
Pubblichiamo la traduzione del comunicato di Kaos GL, una delle principali organizzazioni LGBTI+ della Turchia, che arriva nel quadro della repressione, attuata in questi giorni, contro organizzazioni, attivistə e difensorə dei diritti LGBTI+ in Turchia.


Nella notte tra il 12 e il 13 settembre, la polizia ha fatto irruzione nelle abitazioni di attiviste LGBTI+ e HIV e negli uffici di organizzazioni LGBTI+ e di prevenzione HIV in tutta la Turchia, fermando almeno 30 persone. Il numero continua a salire. Tra le persone fermate ci sono membr dei consigli direttivi e revisor di associazioni regolarmente registrate, tra cui Kaos GL, Muamma, 7 Renk, SPoD, HEVİ, Lambda, LİSTAG, Pozitif Yaşam e Pozitif-iz.


Kaos GL è da tempo direttamente colpita da provvedimenti repressivi e censori e il suo sito risulta bloccato in Turchia!


Il 16 settembre 2026 Kaos GL ha diffuso un comunicato sulla situazione delle persone arrestate nell’ambito della recente operazione contro associazioni e attivist LGBTI+.


Le persone incarcerate sono state trasferite in diverse carceri di Sincan.


Questo il comunicato in traduzione


KaosGL: «Temiamo per la sicurezza delle persone incarcerate. Devono essere liberate immediatamente»


16 settembre 2026


Chiediamo l’immediata liberazione dellə nostrə amicə, ingiustamente e illegalmente incarceratə dopo essere statə colpitə da false accuse e sottopostə a un’intensa campagna diffamatoria.


Vogliamo che l’opinione pubblica sappia che ciò che sta accadendo non è un procedimento giudiziario, ma un’aperta operazione politica che prende di mira diritti e libertà fondamentali. Questo processo deve essere riconosciuto per ciò che è: un tentativo di intimidazione.


Come conseguenza di questa operazione politica, lə nostrə amicə sono statə trasferitə in diverse carceri di Sincan. Siamo profondamente preoccupatə che possano subire maltrattamenti a porte chiuse e nelle condizioni della detenzione carceraria, e temiamo per la loro sicurezza.


Per garantire la loro incolumità e prevenire possibili violazioni dei diritti, è fondamentale che lə nostrə amicə detenutə nella stessa prigione non vengano poste in isolamento e rimangano insieme in ogni momento.


Vogliamo ricordare con chiarezza alle autorità competenti e all’opinione pubblica che la responsabilità di garantire la sicurezza e l’integrità fisica e psicologica di tuttə lə nostrə amicə attualmente in carcere ricade interamente sulle amministrazioni penitenziarie, sul Ministero della Giustizia e su tutte le istituzioni statali competenti.


Nei prossimi giorni pubblicheremo un ulteriore comunicato complessivo sui dettagli di questa operazione illegale e politica e sull’intero procedimento.


Pressioni, complotti politici, false dichiarazioni e accuse prive di fondamento non riusciranno a spezzare la nostra determinazione.


Come Kaos GL continueremo con ancora maggiore determinazione la nostra lotta per i diritti, l’uguaglianza e la libertà.


Lə nostrə amicə non sono sole!

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[1] https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cattle-sheep-and-pig-slaughter

[2] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12431619/Animal-Rising-protesters-charged-stealing-Kings-sheep-royal-Sandringham-Estate-driving-away-animals.html

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

[3] https://www.cambsnews.co.uk/peterborough-court-acquittal-animal-rescue-beagles/

[4] https://www.animalrising.org/post/not-guilty-verdict-for-beagle-puppy-rescuers-in-landmark-legal-case

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

title: Konseya Sendikayên Cîhanî: Êrişên li dijî LGBTÎ+yan nayên qebûlkirin
content:
Konseya Sendikayên Cîhanî (CGU) derbarê operasyonên li dijî LGBTÎ+yan ên bi navê “Malbata min di ewlehiyê de ye” yên li Turkiyeyê daxuyaniyek belav kir.


Di daxuyaniya ku di 23yê Îlonê de hatiye weşandin de Konseyê diyar kir ku ew bi rêxistinên LGBTI+yan, aktivîst, endamên sendikayan û parêzvanên mafên mirovan re di nav hevgirtinê de ne.


Konseyê bi bîr xist ku di çarçoveya operasyonan de derbarê 9 komele û 13 kargeh û zêdetirî 160 kesan de lêpirsîn hatiye dest pê kirin.


Konseyê diyar kir ku tevî rêxistinên LGBTÎ+yan, malper û hesabên medyaya civakî yên saziyên medyaya serbixwe, komên xwendekaran, parêzvanên mafên mirovan û aktivîstan hatine astengkirin û bal kişand ku di serdegirtinan de dest danîne ser materyalên dîjîtal jî.


Operasyon li dijî saziyên ku di qada HIVê de dixebitin jî hat kirin


Di daxuyaniyê de hat destnîşankirin ku operasyon şeva yekem de li 15 bajaran belav bûne û cîhên kar û qadên civakî jî hatine armancgirtin.

Konseyê rexne li wê yekê kir ku saziyên li Stenbolê yên ku piştevaniya kesên bi HIVê ketine dikin, xistine nav operasyonan û weha got:


“Tevlîkirina saziyên piştgiriyê didin kesên bi HIVê re dijîn di nav van operasyonên li dijî rêxistinên LGBT+yan de û metirsiya wê heye ku statuya HIVê û nasnameya LGBT+yan bi awayekî zirarbar û şaş tevlihev bike û dibe ku bibe sedem ku kes ji lêgerîna dermankirin û piştevaniyê paşde bisekinin.”


“Rîska sînordarkirina qada sivîl heye”


Konseyê diyar kir ku her çiqas operasyonên “Malbata min di ewlehiyê de ye” wekî tedbîrek ji bo parastina malbatan hatibin nîşandan jî, ew bi fikar in ku ev hincet ji bo rewakirina cihêkarî û cudakarîya li dijî LGBTI+yan bê bikaranîn.

Di daxuyaniyê de bal kişandin ser berpirsiyariya sendikayan a ji bo parastina azadiya rêxistinbûn û derbirîn û mafên demokratîk:


Êrişên li dijî rêxistinên civaka sivîl û parêzvanên mafên mirovan van prensîban lawaz dikin û qada demokratîk a ku mafên karkeran li ser ava bûne dixin xeteriyê. Bêdengmana li hemberî zextên bi vê rengî, dikare tenê berpirsiyaran wêrektir bike.


“Kesên hatine desteserkirin divê demildest serbest bên berdan”


Hevserokên Komîteya LGBT+yan ya Konseya Sendikayên Cîhanî Jeffrey Boyd û Darienne Flemington jî daxwaz kirin ku operasyon bi dawî bibin.


Boyd û Flemington di daxuyaniya xwe ya hevpar de wiha gotin:


“Êrişên dubare û armancgir ên li dijî civak û rêxistinên LGBT+yan nayên qebûlkirin. Em daxwaz dikin ku her kesê/a ku tenê ji ber bikaranîna mafên xwe yên bingehîn ên wekî avakirina komeleyan, azadiya derbirînê û parêzvaniya aştiyane hatine desteserkirin demildest serbest bên berdan. Em bang dikin ku dawî li desteserkirin û kiryarên din ên çavtirsandinê yên ku xebatên rewa yên civaka sivîl armanc digirin bê anîn.”


NÖ/AY

author: EDRi
title: Simplification for whom? Open letter to EU Member States to uphold GDPR protections in Digital Omnibus on Data
content:
Over the past months, the European Commission's Digital Omnibus on Data has turned into a wider discussion about how much protection the data – and with it, the rights – of people in the EU should receive in the name of AI, innovation and competitiveness. That discussion has now reached a critical stage in the Council.

EU governments are now discussing critical issues like whether data should sometimes fall outside the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) depending on who holds the data, whether AI deserves special treatment when companies want to reuse personal data, and whether people should receive less information about how their data are used. The Irish Presidency’s compromise of 3 September has raised serious concerns across the board. A revised text circulated on 21 September seemingly attempted at improving some parts of it, but leaves the most fundamental questions unresolved. Just as the Commission’s Proposal, this is deregulation of substance, not simply less paperwork, it is happening very quickly, and the legal drafting is quite worrying.

The Council has stepped back from directly rewriting the GDPR’s definition of ‘personal data,’ and this may sound reassuring. But it is not: the new Article 25a and the accompanying Recitals 27 still risk changing the answer to the same basic question: when does the GDPR apply?

To understand why, it helps to distinguish pseudonymisation from anonymisation. Pseudonymisation means replacing obvious identifiers, such as a name, with something else, like a code or an ID number. That can make data safer, because the information linking the code back to the person is kept separately. But the person is still there behind the code, and the data, together with the rights attached to them, are still meant to remain protected.

This is not an abstract scenario. Much of today’s online tracking already works through pseudonymous identifiers rather than people’s names. Cookie IDs, advertising IDs, device identifiers and similar codes are used to recognise people over time, link their behaviour across services, build profiles and decide what content, prices or adverts they see. In many contexts, knowing that someone is ‘User 15051948’ is actually more useful for tracking and targeting them than knowing their name.

Anonymisation is different. Data are anonymous only when a person can no longer realistically be identified from them, including by combining them with other information that is reasonably available. Anonymous data fall outside the GDPR. Pseudonymised data do not simply become anonymous because one company cannot immediately put a name to the person.

The Council’s approach risks blurring exactly that line, between data that are still being used to single out and act on a person, and data that are genuinely anonymous. Under Article 25a, the same pseudonymised data could be treated as personal data for one actor but as non-personal data for another if that actor is considered unable to identify the person. In practice, this can produce something very close to narrowing the definition of personal data itself. That creates two problems.

The first issue is about rights. If a company treats the data as outside the GDPR, many of the protections attached to the GDPR may disappear with it: the duty to keep data secure, people’s right to know how data are used, the right to access or correct them, or to object to certain uses.

The second is about legal certainty. Digital data rarely sit with one company. They move through long chains of service providers, advertisers, analytics companies, cloud providers and data brokers that disproportionately depend on distributed data processing: different actors hold different pieces of information (all of them surely pseudonymised) and have different technical capabilities. So the legal status of the same dataset will change depending on who is holding it at a given moment. That means companies, regulators and individuals may first have to work out who can identify whom, with which data and at which point in the chain, before they can even answer the basic question of whether the GDPR applies. And there is an obvious incentive problem here: actors already argue that they are not responsible because they cannot themselves identify the person behind an identifier, or because another actor in the chain holds the information needed to do so. Article 25a risks giving those arguments considerably more legal weight.

For a law supposedly …

author: Unknown
title: Interview de Daniel Carreno, militant syndical à SUD PTT
content:
Daniel Carreno, militant Sud

PTT

, est décédé le 31 juillet 2018.


Militant

SUD


PTT

, il donnait en novembre 2006 une interview à la revue «

 

Partisan

 

» de l'

OCML

 - Voie Prolétarienne dans laquelle il faisait part de ses réflexions et critiques sur

SUD

 et le syndicalisme en général. La voici sans retouche.


L'activité


Problème du dépassement de forfait sur mon portable perso pour cause d'activité syndicale. (De l'ordre de 100 à 120 € par mois, pendant un an et demi).


Depuis juillet, j'ai un portable payé par le syndicat sur justificatif.


J'ai dû changer de position sur le sujet


Auparavant, j'étais contre l'attribution de portable au permanent. J'ai posé le problème parce que cela devenait financièrement invivable. Le problème se posera aussi pour mon successeur qui n'a pas un gros salaire.


Le syndicat a donc voté l'attribution d'un portable mais aussi un remboursement des frais précédents, ce que j'ai refusé par principe (faute de justificatifs et de contrôle possible) et j'ai reversé la somme au syndicat.


Je justifiais la position précédente (pas de portable) au nom du fait que la permanence ne doit pas être quelque chose de confortable pour le permanent.


V : Je rends compte d'une anecdote sur l'élection des chefs de tribus indiennes du Chiapas rapportée par Traven.


Il y a un manque de volontaire pour me succéder a la permanence.


Il y a néanmoins un jeune de 24 ans, habitant Montgeron.

II

 a une conscience de classe.


Les vieux, eux, ne veulent plus. Parce que la place n'est pas confortable

 

; parce qu'ils m'ont vu agir et que c'est repoussoir, parce que pour certains, leur base syndicale est faible et disparaîtrait s'ils en partaient.


V : J'expose la démarche de l'interview

 

; un interview non pas pour Partisan (ce qui avait été évoqué par des camarades), mais pour Voie Prolétarienne, pour alimenter notre réflexion sur le syndicalisme et ses rapports avec la construction de l'organisation communiste. On verra éventuellement si on peut extraire des articles de l'interview.


V : Pourquoi, toi qui est basiste, tu es devenu permanent

 

?


Le mandat est électif, d'un an, renouvelable par élection deux fois. Soit 3 ans maximum.


Après un certain nombre de critiques que j'avais dirigées (dont une motion de 8 pages de la section de Créteil), les camarades ont pensé que c'était mon tour. «

 

Tu penses savoir comment faire, prouve-le

 

!

 

». J'ai reculé puis, après un temps, j'ai pensé effectivement que c'était mon tour.


J'ai trouvé aussi que c'était logique par rapport à l'organisation du tri trois secteurs Courrier, Courrier International et Colis. Cette dernière division est une grosse direction, avec plein de problèmes (de répression entre autres). Il fallait quelqu'un venant du Colis.


Je me suis demandé comment faire. Puis j'ai décidé. Ce que je faisais sur une section (Créteil), j'allais le faire sur 30.


J'ai été sur tous les sites, au service des travailleurs, en essayant d'organiser partout des sections et de les coordonner. Gros investissement contesté par certains de mon syndicat qui trouvaient que j'en faisais trop.


La sauce a pris dans des sites qui étaient des déserts syndicaux (et où on fait maintenant 70% aux élections)


La journée commençait généralement par une diffusion de tracts à 6h quelque part en région parisienne (St-Denis, Montgeron, Bondy etc.). Voir les gens pendant la diffusion, les voir après en salle de repos à la pause. Puis, s'il y avait lieu

AG

 du personnel. Sur certains problèmes, cela se poursuivait par une délégation.


C'est comme ça que l'agence colis-poste d'Argenteuil s'est trouvée en grève un 4 août.


[Avant, tout était ensemble à la Poste. Maintenant les bureaux de Poste sont vides de facteurs. Il y a séparation]


A 9h, habituellement, mon intervention sur site était terminée. A 10h j'étais rue des Envierges, au bureau du syndicat, et je rédigeais des tracts centraux ou locaux à partir d'informations données par les camarades.


Au bureau, c'était beaucoup de téléphone : renseignement, assistance par rapport à la répression. Beaucoup de camarades téléphonaient chaque jour pour faire le point. Souvent des camarades inexpérimentés demandaient un avis. Ce que je donnais. Il me demandaient aussi une décision, ce que je ne donnais pas. Je concluais «

 

Vous faites ce que vous voulez en fonction de notre conversation

 

». Obligés de trancher eux-mêmes, ils prenaient la décision.


Tout ça était entrecoupé d'un …

author: Hassan Alnaser
title: After seizing Tigray airports, TPLF announces ‘defensive war’ against Ethiopian govt
content:
The confrontation between the Tigray regional government and the Ethiopian federal government entered a new phase on Wednesday when Tigrayan forces seized control of the

Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports.

 


Clashes broke out at several locations in the restive northern state, the site of a two-year civil war that concluded in 2022, and in the neighboring

Afar

 region — a development that has pushed the Ethiopian conflict back toward open warfare, four years after the signing of the

Pretoria Agreement

 that ended the previous war between the

Tigray People’s Liberation Front

and federal forces.


A source in the Tigray regional administration told Mada Masr that the seizure of the airports was part of a military redeployment that began in the early hours of Wednesday, with Tigrayan forces

using

the airports as facilities of operational importance amid the expanding scope of the fighting.


In the wake of the TPLF takeover, Ethiopian Airlines

announced

 the suspension of flights to the three airports due to the “current situation” in the Tigray region.

 


A Tigrayan military source noted that Wednesday’s developments followed months of troop buildup and limited skirmishes along the front lines, describing Wednesday’s events as a shift from a phase of mutual pressure to direct confrontation.

He added that Tigrayan forces

view

 federal movements as an attempt to alter the military landscape established since the Pretoria Agreement and believe

that

seizing certain vital sites could prevent federal forces from utilizing the region’s civilian and military infrastructure during ongoing operations.


The federal government framed Wednesday’s events differently. A former security source in Addis Ababa described the movements by the TPLF as a “full-scale attack” on government positions in Afar and Amhara.


While seizing airports does not in itself decide the outcome of the battle, it signals a shift in the nature of operations, a security source in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr.

Mekelle

 serves as the region’s political and administrative hub, while the airports at Axum and Shire provide crucial links to northern and western Tigray.

 Consequently, placing airports under the control of regional forces strains the federal government’s ability to manage its presence within the region and gives Tigrayan forces a strategic advantage in any future negotiations, the source said.


The security source added that any operation to retake the airports would require careful calculation due to the presence of civilians in the cities, and because the use of air power and artillery in urban areas would heighten humanitarian risks.


In its first official comment on Wednesday’s escalation, the Ethiopian military

said

 it had repelled attacks from Tigrayan forces and their allies in parts of northern Ethiopia, adding that hostilities began in an area of the Amhara region close to the border with Tigray.


The military

added

 that it had killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 in a counteroffensive in the Amhara region.


Wednesday’s escalation in the long simmering tension between the TPLF and federal government immediately follows a series of airstrikes that targeted areas in Tigray over the past few days. In Alamata, located in southern Tigray, an attack on Tuesday left 14 civilians dead and 22 injured, a local media source told Mada Masr.


Aftermath of a drone strike on a humanitarian aid truck in northwestern Tigray, September 22. Photo: @JoeTseGy on X.


The source stated that more than six drones and three fighter jets carried out over 21 raids, beginning around 3:30 am, adding that the strikes hit civilian educational facilities, including a secondary school.


The media source noted that the area has recently seen an increase in military activity and troop movements involving both federal and Tigrayan forces.


The TPLF is increasingly worried about drone strikes, a senior official in the front told Mada Masr, saying that many top officials are limiting their movements to avoid being targeted by federal forces. 


For the security source in Addis Ababa, the broader concern for the federal government is that the conflict will quickly extend beyond Tigray.

Wednesday’s clashes broke out just as the TPLF — alongside six other armed groups — announced the formation of the

Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival.


This alliance includes the Fano militia in Amhara, the

Oromo Liberation Army,
