author: Emma Jacobs
title: What the climate movement can learn from organized labor
content:
This article

What the climate movement can learn from organized labor

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Climate activists engaged in nonviolent direct action are used to the rinse and repeat of arrest: handcuffs, short trip to jail, a misdemeanor charge and then release to friends for a post-action pizza dinner. Show up at court a few weeks later for a brief arraignment and wait for the case to be dismissed. Low drama.


That’s changed under Trump. From the

Declare Emergency activists charged with felonies

 (for applying washable paint to the protective case around a Degas sculpture) to the

Extinction Rebellion activists under investigation by an FBI terrorism task force

 (for undisclosed reasons), activists can no longer depend on walking away unscathed from direct actions.

Multiple states have passed anti-protest laws

 since Trump was elected, increasing penalties imposed on activists. Grassroots action has a higher cost now. 


Simultaneously, with the gutting of the Inflation Reduction Act and its attendant tax credits for clean energy investment, the federal path to climate action is blocked. And local wins, while important, cannot surmount the incredible rollbacks happening at the federal level, as Sunrise Movement Executive Director Aru Shiney-Ajay

recently pointed out

. 


Indeed, the U.S. climate movement is in

deep trouble

. If all that weren’t enough, the climate crisis is no longer top of mind for many on the left, especially with the rising authoritarian threat and the focus on affordability. With civil disobedience demanding greater risk, traditional policy advocacy for climate action at the federal level closed off and public attention turned elsewhere, what tactics do we in the climate movement have left?


What’s left is deep engagement with the labor movement — its members and its tactics. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Organized labor has a broad base, a track record of major wins and the power to shut down the economy. And make no mistake: Economic leverage is a necessary ingredient in the struggle to bring down companies as profitable as those in the fossil fuel industry. 


Climate activists have relied heavily on tactics of protest and persuasion (see Gene Sharp’s

categories

), underinvesting in tactics of economic noncooperation. While the environmental movement has a history of consumer boycotts, there have been fewer instances of work stoppages or rent strikes. The climate groups that do engage in symbolic work and school stoppages (most famously, Fridays for the Future), have mostly been confined to students and are largely to make a political statement rather than a strategic attempt to gain concrete concessions from a specific target. 


Strategically aligning workers with a rapid energy transition not only broadens the coalition needed to win durable policy victories, but builds power with a movement versed in strikes, walkouts, slowdowns and other forms of economic disruption. (Not to mention a bevy of tools like

community benefit agreements

 and

co-enforcement

 to promote follow-through on corporate environmental promises.)


Labor-climate alliances go back decades (see Blue Green Alliance, Climate Jobs National Resource Center and Labor Network for Sustainability), and unions have long advocated for a

just transition

 that supports workers employed in polluting industries. But in the current political environment, we need these relationships to be stronger than ever.  


One major opportunity for the climate movement is the May Day Strong coalition, which brings labor and community groups together to organize mass strikes and make big demands for systemic change. The coalition’s demands don’t yet include climate, but the climate movement can still organize with them to learn nonparticipation tactics and build solidarity toward a broad base that sees climate, anti-authoritarianism and affordability as one united fight. 


Lessons from labor

 


Think about the situation at your job. Workplaces are pretty authoritarian: the leader doesn’t care much for the input of the people on the shop floor, and what the leader says goes. If someone gets hurt, let the government step in to help them. As unions teach us, for a group of workers to extract real concessions from a profit-maximizing boss requires building enough power among workers to shut the workplace down (or at least threaten to do so) …

author: Santana Dreaver
title: After more than a century, this Salish woolly dog pelt has returned to ‘B.C.’
content:
Only known pelt of the extinct woolly dog. Photo by Brittany M. Hance, courtesy of Division of Mammals, Smithsonian

Institution


This story is co-published

with the Narwhal

 as part of their

2026 Indigenous journalism fellowship


Coming face to face with the pelt of a now-extinct Salish woolly dog was an emotional experience for Jordan Wilson.


The curator from xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam Indian Band) attended an unveiling at the Museum of Anthropology in “Vancouver” as the ancestor was welcomed back to its home territories earlier this month.


The pelt is on loan from the Smithsonian institution, where it was in storage for more than a century — it was sent to the “American” museum in 1859. It will be at MOA until August of 2027. 


Belonging to a dog from Stó:lō territories known as Mutton, it’s the only known Salish woolly dog pelt in existence.


As the pelt was unveiled to its Salish relatives on Sept. 4, Wilson attended along with other Salish community members from “Vancouver Island” and the “Fraser Valley.”


“For me personally, I was caught off guard at the emotional quality of it,” Wilson said.


“Seeing this pelt in person, seeing its little paws and seeing its little nose, realizing that this was a living being that was alive 160 years ago.”


A reconstruction of the Coast Salish dog with sketches of Arctic dogs and spitz breeds in the background for comparison. Illustration by Karen Carr


Renowned Musqueam weaver Debra Sparrow was there with her daughter and grandson.


“You watch as they unveil it, pieces of the wood come off, and then the containers open, and there he is. There’s a sense of welcome you feel instinctively,” she said.


“It’s historical that the woolly dog arrived back home.”


Once ubiquitous among Indigenous communities in the Pacific Northwest, Salish woolly dogs went

extinct

 during the late 1800s, as settlers arrived on the coast. Through storytelling, oral history, literature and artwork, woolly dogs have

remained a sacred part of Coast and Interior Salish culture

. 


The pelt came to “B.C.” from Seattle, where it was on loan from the Smithsonian and temporarily exhibited for the first time.


Indigenous people travelled from up and down the Salish Sea to spend time with the woolly dog pelt at MOA before it became open to be viewed by the public.


“They were very important to every village, all through the territory of Salish people,” Sparrow said about the dogs. Their traditional

territory

 spans from southwestern “B.C.,” into “Washington State” and “Oregon.”


“People will come to feel connected to it. It’s amazing how one little pelt can bring all the people back together.”


Dog’s genetic makeup confirms Salish oral history 


This specific dog, with Stó:lō roots from the Chilliwack area, belonged to an American naturalist George Gibbs, who named the dog “Mutton.” 


Because of specific storage requirements, the pelt is being hosted at MOA, on Musqueam territory,

at the request

 of Stó:lō leaders.


It’s a caretaking responsibility that museum curator Wilson takes seriously. He began working on the

Pacific Northwest and contemporary Indigenous art

 exhibit, where the pelt is being shown, last year.


“This is the highlight of the work that I do … being able to help facilitate things like this,” he said.


“This specific breed dates back thousands of years,” he added. “That goes to show how important this breed was to our ancestors.”


Sparrow recalled that, as settlers arrived in “British Columbia,” “the first thing many of the European sailors said was that the people have these little dogs with them in their canoes.” 


Combined with mountain goat wool, Salish woolly dog fur was spun into a weaving fibre, used to make clothes, blankets, regalia and other textiles. 


The woolly relatives were fed a rich salmon and elk diet to keep their coats soft and shiny, and in exchange providing Salish communities with safety, companionship and fluffy white hair. 


But the deep connection between Salish people and the woolly dog was severed as the important animal went extinct.


Kwulasultun, Eliot White-Hill, an artist from Snuneymuxw First Nation, said he never heard about the Salish woolly dog while he was growing up.


Once he became an artist and started asking Elders in his community questions, knowledge and stories about them began resurfacing.


“It’s profoundly meaningful to have that woolly dog come back to this part of the world, to be able to reconnect with …

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Straightwashed Its Lesbian but Maisie Williams Played Her Gay Anyway
content:
Leading up to the release of Practical Magic 2, we were all hoping this witchy sequel would be even gayer than the gay undertones of the first because, in the source material, Sally Owens’ daughter Antonia is a lesbian. And while there were potentially versions of the movie that expressed that, the final edit left Antonia’s sexuality undetermined. However, Maisie Williams has been sure to tell everyone on the press tour that she knew the source material and regardless of what the final edit revealed, she played Antonia as a “sapphic icon” and that it brought some nuance to certain scenes since it meant Antonia had a different perspective on men than the other women in her family.

This is a shame and not the first time queerness in a book has been watered down or erased altogether in their adaptations. To name a few: Fried Green Tomatoes, The Color Purple, and don’t even get me started on comic book characters that are queer on the page but straight on screen. Studios are cowards and it’s the same reason queer storylines are often cut from animated films, or even single lines in big box office hits that would mean a lot to the queer community but scare the money men. This feels especially egregious in a movie franchise like this, because witches have such a rich queer history and having a film (as so few are) jam-packed with women and to have all of them be straight feels like a waste.

It’s disappointing to say the least, especially in the year 2026, but at least we have people like Maisie making sure we know that SHE knows that the character should have been queer, and that it was unfortunately out of her hands in the end.

Sandra Bullock has said there could be a third Practical Magic in the future, centering on Antonia and Joey King’s Kylie, so fingers crossed the queer lines and scenes don’t end up on the cutting room floor of that one.

author: Admin100
title: One Million Hands Flourishing: Nicaragua and the Neverending Task of Planting
content:
By Tamaya F.C.


The indigenous neighborhood of Monimbo in Masaya, Nicaragua has a long legacy of resistance. Masaya is located less than an hour Southeast of the capital, Managua. In 1978, the people of Monimbo barricaded themselves, used makeshift weapons and prevented the National Guard from coming into the city, winning the first major victory for the Sandinistas as they were able to take control of an urban city. Forty years later, the people of Monimbo barricaded themselves with paving stones and were able to prevent riot police from entering. The next day however, they had lost most of the city to riot police. Masaya, the city where I am from, has become a battlefield where police attack citizens.


The Unrest


The latest civil unrest has had many university students from across the capital city of Managua protesting against the government’s social security reforms this past week. These students hail from various universities like the Universidad Centroamericana (UCA), Universidad Nacional de Ingenieria (UNI), Universidad Nacional Agraria (UNA), Universidad Autónoma Nacional de Nicaragua – Managua (UNAN)

,

and Universidad Politécnica de Nicaragua (UPOLI). The  proposal was to increase social security contribution from both workers and employers and

reduce retiree benefits

 by 5%.


Last week, students barricaded the Metropolitan Cathedral in Managua which serves as a refuge for protesters. There, they collected donations and distributed provisions such as water and had student doctors help tend to the wounded. Police and pro-government Sandinista youth eventually surrounded the cathedral and held them hostage until prominent Catholic church official, Monsignor Silvio Jóse Báez, who has been critical of Ortega and supportive of protesters, aided and helped assure the release of the students.


Sandinista Legacy


When the Sandinistas (FSLN) overthrew the Somoza regime in July 1979, they had to work toward reconstructing the social, political and economic structure of the country. They implemented

agrarian reforms

 for redistribution of land, launched

 vaccination campaigns

 to open access to healthcare and created

literacy campaigns

 that reduced illiteracy from 80 percent to 12 percent, among other reforms. This was only possible because of the work everyday people put in day after day.


Over the last five days, more than 30 people have died, many of them students as well as a journalist. Over 100 are being held prisoner, around 50 remain missing and the overall count of those injured is unknown.


On April 22nd, Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, who rose to power as a prominent leader of the Sandinistas, revoked the proposed changes to social security. After he pulled the reforms, riot police entered a prominent symbol of the student resistance, UPOLI, which students had barricaded. Five students were shot in the process and two were killed. Ortega also attacked the student movement as “delinquents” who were backed by right-wing parties and funded by the CIA. The student movement does not allow

political parties to participate

 though. But many Nicaraguans know this is an issue greater than social security. They are tired of corrupt governments and want the current government out.


I am an anarchist. So w

hen I say “I am a Sandinista” to me it means I believe in the popular movement that rose up to overthrow capitalist imperialism. The movement that fought for freedom. The movement that dared to dream of bringing a just and equitable society.


The current government of Ortega does not represent the values of Sandino nor of the Sandinistas who spilled blood to break free from their chains in previous decades. The Sandinista Youth of today is not the same one that my mother joined many years ago. It is not the one that participated in literacy campaigns to teach the people to read and write, nor is it the one she joined to help pick coffee and rebuild Nicaragua.


The Demands of the Students


The future is uncertain and it is unclear where this is all heading but there is much work to be done on the ground. Today, students from the

Movimiento 19 de Abril

, who embody the spirit of liberation are undertaking the never ending task of building a new world, one from the bottom up. Approximately 500 students continue their barricaded occupation of UPOLI and their organizing against Ortega. They are currently working on establishing a coordinating body to represent students from different …

author: Daron Letts
title: Free breakfasts to continue for students across Kivalliq and Kitikmeot
content:
Approximately 5,000 students at 22 schools across the Kivalliq and Kitikmeot regions will continue to have access to free breakfasts through 2031, thanks to $5 million from Agnico

 Eagle Mines Ltd.


The breakfast program, dubbed the Inunnguiniq Project, is administered by Breakfast Club of Canada, a Quebec-based charity that leads initiatives to address food security across the country.


“We’ve seen how this program is important for students, for families, and for communities,” said

Marc-Olivier Vachon, general manager of Agnico Eagle’s Meliadine mine, Wednesday evening during

his keynote speech at the

Kivalliq Trade Show gala.


Agnico Eagle announced the first round of $2.5 million in funding for the program at the same trade show event in 2023.


Inunnguiniq is an Inuktitut term taken from Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, or traditional Inuit knowledge, that refers to the process of becoming a capable human being.


— With files from Corey Larocque

author: Gladys Stagno
title: ¿Macro ordenada?
content:
La OCDE mejoró su previsión global para 2026, pero bajó su perspectiva de crecimiento para Argentina, y hasta JP Morgan advierte que el buen desempeño del sector energético no alcanza para sostener “un país para todos”. ¿Qué números mira el Gobierno?


Ilustración: Marcelo Spotti


Por Gladys Stagno


Si uno quisiera sintetizar el modelo económico de Javier Milei, podría decir que se empeña en tener un Excel prolijo. Así, de la mano de un crecimiento sostenido (impulsado por agro y energéticas), un dólar planchado (gracias al cuantioso ingreso de divisas que garantizas ambos sectores) y un ajuste perpetuo del gasto público, los números dan.


Obnubilado por la macro y el mantra del equilibrio fiscal, el Gobierno ha podido —a lo largo de casi tres años— despreciar la micro. Y con ello hablamos de cualquier indicador de la economía doméstica que titile en el tablero. Pero, al parecer, para quienes juzgan desde afuera no es un suficiente.


Todos crecen menos vos


En su

Informe Interino de Perspectivas Económicas

, la Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE) acaba de actualizar las proyecciones anuales de PBI e inflación de 2026 para los países del G20, Argentina entre ellos.


Según sus estimaciones, la OCDE considera que la economía global crecerá 2,9%, lo que significa una mejora de una décima en relación a su último informe trimestral. La explicación radica en el que el impacto sobre precios del conflicto en Medio Oriente será en gran parte compensado por una rigurosa política fiscal aplicada a las tarifas energéticas y por las inversiones que tracciona la inteligencia artificial. “El crecimiento económico mundial se ha desacelerado, pero se ha mantenido resiliente”, sintetizó la institución.


En cambio, para la Argentina, ajustó su proyección anterior a la baja. Esta vez, consideró que el crecimiento de nuestro país será de 2,6% en 2026. Se trata de una reducción de 0,2 puntos porcentuales respecto de su informe previo, y de una desaceleración importante en relación con el 4,5% de crecimiento de 2025.


El organismo tuvo en cuenta la amenaza del fenómeno meteorológico conocido como El Niño, que afectará a toda la región, lo que potencialmente reducirá “la producción agrícola en las economías más expuestas de América Latina, África y la región de Asia-Pacífico”. Otras economías de estas latitudes, como México y Brasil, no se verán tan perjudicadas.


Hasta JP Morgan lo dice


El pronóstico de la OCDE no se condice con el optimismo del Gobierno,

que proyectó en el Presupuesto 2027 un crecimiento del PBI del 4% para el año que viene.

 Pero sí con la mirada de, por ejemplo, JP Morgan, una de las entidades financieras más grandes del mundo.


En una nota con Bloomberg Línea, el CEO de JP Morgan para la Argentina, Facundo Gómez Minujín, advirtió: “No basta con que a mineras y petroleras les vaya muy bien”


“También tenés que tener un país para todos, donde la gente pueda consumir, haya crecimiento de la empleabilidad, bajar la informalidad, extender la tributación al resto de la población y lograr bajar los impuestos”, agregó Minujín. Y detalló que hay compañías que están “recontra mal” a causa de la carga tributaria, los costos financieros y, sobre todo, de la caída del consumo y la apertura de importaciones.


Según señala Tiempo, Gómez Minujín fue el anfitrión de la reunión con banqueros que Luis “Toto” Caputo mantuvo el lunes en Nueva York, que no fue informada por el Ministerio de Economía. Llamativamente, el martes después de la reunión, los ADRs (acciones y bonos argentinos que cotizan en Wall Street), sufrieron pronunciadas caídas y el riesgo país escaló a los 555 puntos.


Ilustración: Marcelo Spotti


La entrada

¿Macro ordenada?

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Por la salud y la vida del compañero Juan Aliste Vega. En el marco de una nueva conmemoración del 11 de septiembre
content:
Por la salud y la vida del compañero Juan Aliste Vega

En una noche de memoria, a 53 años de la barbarie dictatorial. Seguimos recordando a cada compañerx asesinadx, torturadx o desaparecidx, tanto en dictadura como en democracia. No desde la memoria pasiva, sino desde la acción subversiva, recordamos el pasado para cargarnos de aprendizajes y repensar el antagonismo del mañana.

Frente a un enemigo que precariza nuestras vidas, impone impunidad, miseria y devasta el mundo con guerras, ecocidios y genocidios. La propuesta desde el anarquismo organizado ha sido jamás dejar de resistir. Nos hemos abocado fervientemente a estar en la construcción de movimientos sociales y de organización popular. Siempre dotando de características anarquistas cada una de las trincheras de las que somos parte. Es decir, de autonomía, acción directa, horizontalidad y apoyo mutuo. A eso nos debemos compañeras/os, a dejar de poner la otra mejilla, organizarse y arrojarse al incomodo pero provechoso y necesario camino revolucionario para construir el mundo nuevo que queremos vivir.

Siempre sabiendo que el único poder capaz de hacer justicia a nuestro pueblo es el propio pueblo organizado.

Y particularmente también, considerando la urgente situación del compañero subversivo Juan Aliste, que afectado por los largos años de prisión, las duras condiciones de reclusión y las sistemáticas negligencias medicas-carcelarias hoy enfrenta nuevamente al estado, que en un afán vengativo niega otorgar cualquier beneficio, régimen alternativo o excarcelación, convirtiendo su enfermedad en prisión en una condena a muerte. Aún así, Juan Aliste Vega, sigue dando la pelea, enviando ánimos de resistencia y fortaleza, de lucha y dignidad. Ese es precisamente el ejemplo de coherencia del compañero, además de la de un hermano, amigo, expropiador, revolucionario, anticapitalista, padre e hijo; el de un combatiente contra la dictadura y su continuidad democrática, luchando dentro y fuera de la prisión, hasta las ultimas consecuencias. Desde esta perspectiva, efectivamente, la lucha por la salud, la vida y la liberación del prisionero subversivo Juan Aliste debe convocar nuestra más profunda atención.

Hasta el triunfo de la revolución social.

Porque nada ha acabado, nada ni nadie está olvidado.

Nuestro mejor homenaje es seguir combatiendo.

Muerte al Estado y que viva la anarquía.

author: Thiago Müller
title: Zucco destinou emenda pix para evento evangélico liderado por pastor bolsonarista
content:
O político do Partido Liberal (PL) de Santa Maria, Jader Maretoli, se intitula como um apóstolo. Foi com essa autodenominação que ele coordenou um evento gospel realizado no final do ano passado. No encerramento do Dia da Família, em 7 de dezembro, o pastor da Jesus Church pediu bênçãos para o padrinho do evento, o tenente-coronel Luciano Zucco, então deputado federal bolsonarista.


“Nós precisamos honrar quem merece honra. A Bíblia nos diz isso. Se tem alguém que nos ajudou muito, que é o grande padrinho deste evento, é o tenente-coronel Zucco”, disse aos fiéis presentes. “Eu quero que você, nas suas orações, nessa noite, ore pela vida dele, porque, com certeza, Deus vai o abençoar muito mais, para que ele continue nos abençoando e sendo canal de Deus nos próximos anos aqui na nossa cidade, na nossa região.”


Zucco não estava presente no evento, mas destinou R$ 200 mil para custear o Dia da Família de 5 a 7 de dezembro. O evento, que reuniu de motoqueiros a fiéis evangélicos, incluiu também a contratação de um cantor gospel sem licitação. O repasse destoa do perfil das emendas pix enviadas pelo então deputado federal e atual candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul e foi a única ocasião em que Zucco destinou a eventos. 


Uma análise feita pela Matinal das emendas pix enviadas por Zucco entre 2024 e 2026, com base no

Emendômetro

, mostra que a maior parte dos R$ 5,6 milhões foi destinada à educação e segurança pública. Quase não há detalhamento de onde foi parar o dinheiro enviado a escolas. No que tange à segurança pública, os recursos foram aplicados na compra de veículos, armas e outros materiais para guardas municipais, Polícia Militar e delegacias.


Apesar de Maretoli ter homenageado Zucco como padrinho do evento, a equipe de comunicação do candidato do PL disse à Matinal que a demanda partiu do próprio município. “O mandato recebe solicitações apresentadas por prefeituras, câmaras de vereadores, entidades, associações, representantes municipais e também por cidadãos”, informou. 


Com base nestas demandas, a comunicação do candidato especificou que são considerados critérios técnicos e legais como “relevância e o interesse público, a pertinência para o município, a possibilidade legal de atendimento, a adequação do objeto à modalidade do recurso, a disponibilidade orçamentária e a viabilidade de execução”. Após a resposta, questionamos qual seria a relevância social e a pertinência do Dia da Família, mas a comunicação do candidato disse que não ia prestar novos esclarecimentos. Disse ter atendido às demandas do veículo e que o questionamento sobre o destino da emenda está ligado ao alinhamento editorial do veículo.


Nas respostas enviadas, Zucco e sua equipe afirmam zelar pela correta destinação das emendas parlamentares. “Caso seja identificado qualquer indício de irregularidade na aplicação dos recursos, o mandato exerce sua prerrogativa de fiscalização e adota as providências cabíveis perante os órgãos competentes”, diz a nota. O deputado também enviou ofício à Controladoria Geral da União solicitando fiscalização das emendas parlamentares individuais indicadas por ele no exercício de 2025, visando a lisura e transparência na execução.


Porém, disse também que, durante a indicação da emenda parlamentar para o evento em Santa Maria, o mandato só tinha conhecimento de que a ocasião denominava-se “Marcha da Família” e nada mais (

confira as respostas na íntegra

).


A reportagem entrou em contato com o pastor Jader Maretoli quatro vezes, sem sucesso. No último contato, ele comprometeu-se a prestar esclarecimentos, e pediu que as perguntas fossem enviadas por mensagem de WhatsApp, mas, até o momento, não houve resposta.


Além de apóstolo da Jesus Church de Santa Maria e organizador do Dia da Família, Maretoli é vereador suplente e concorreu pelo PL em 2024. De 2019 a 2020, enquanto filiado ao Republicanos, Maretoli ocupou o cargo de secretário-adjunto da Secretaria Estadual do Esporte e Lazer do governo Eduardo Leite (PSDB). 


Ele se apresenta, no Instagram, como o 12º vereador mais votado na cidade, apesar de não ter sido eleito. Hoje, pouco menos de 12 meses depois do evento, atua como cabo eleitoral de Zucco e dos candidatos ao Senado, Marcel Van Hattem (Novo) e Sanderson (PL). 


O sogro de Maretoli, o pastor Oséas Costa, concorre ao cargo de deputado estadual pelo Republicanos. No Dia da Família, Costa figurou como

atração.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Perseguir y censurar a la ciencia: el INTA echa y exonera a su mayor investigadora en agrotóxicos
content:
Por Darío Aranda


El INTA tiene un largo historial de persecuciones, censuras, precarización y maltrato laboral, pero dio un paso extremo y está a punto de cometer

el hecho más grave desde la vuelta a la democracia: el despido y exoneración de Virginia Aparicio

, la mayor investigadora de agrotóxicos en la institución. ¿El motivo? Haber realizado su trabajo:

analizó y confirmó los efectos terribles del modelo de agronegocio

 en la salud de la población y en el ambiente. La exoneración implica que nunca más podrá ser contratada por el Estado.


Los responsables directos de la censura y persecución: las autoridades del INTA, funcionarios del Gobierno, aliados de la Mesa de Enlace, Aapresid y de las empresas de transgénicos y agrotóxicos.


Pruebas contundentes


Con 22 años de carrera dentro del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA), Aparicio tiene larga experiencia en la detección de agrotóxicos en el ambiente. Cuenta con publicaciones científicas, participó de libros y

fue perito en causas judiciales sobre pueblos fumigados

. Siempre cumplió un rol científico-técnico y no silenció los resultados, aunque sabía que eran incómodos para el

INTA, reconocida institución al servicio del agronegocio.


Pero el quiebre fue un

proyecto internacional llamado Sprint

 ("Transición Sostenible de Protección Vegetal"), realizado durante cinco años por académicos de once países y que

detalló el grave impacto del modelo agroindustrial

. Los países con población estudiada fueron Argentina, Francia, España, Portugal, Italia, Países Bajos, Suiza, Dinamarca, República Checa, Croacia y Eslovenia.


Aprobado por los distintos eslabones burocráticos y jefes del INTA, Aparicio participó del proyecto que incluía análisis de 27 personas de la provincia de Buenos Aires, tanto del ámbito rural como urbano.


Los resultados de Argentina fueron lapidarios, como contaron

Cecilia Gárgan

o

 y

Anabel Pomar en Tierra Viva

:


Todas las personas testeadas tenían glifosato en su cuerpo

.


Los


suelos y el agua bonaerense tienen una concentración de agrotóxicos

 más alta que en los países Europeos.


Se confirmo presencia abrumadora de

glifosato, 2-4D, atrazina, clorpirifos, fipronil,


imidacloprid y cipermetrina, entre otros.


El total de participantes argentinos (27) presentó un rango


de 6 a 13 plaguicidas en orina, de 2 a 10 plaguicidas en sangre y hasta 18 plaguicidas en materia fecal.


Agua superficial se encontraron entre 10 a 28 plaguicidas.


Los resultados finales fueron presentados en Bélgica en una

conferencia pública

.


Los resultados de

Argentina lo ubican como el país con mayor cantidad de peligrosos plaguicidas


como el glifosato y el clorpirifos

.


Y, lejos de tomar medidas para proteger a la población, en Argentina sobrevino la censura.


El Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria

abandonó la investigación en 2023

 mediante la Resolución 2023-399-APN-INTA, sin comunicar jamás los hallazgos de agrotóxicos en las personas y en el ambiente.


Los responsables directos:

Mariano Garmendia

 y

Nacira


Belén Muñoz

, presidente y vice del INTA en ese momento, y el Director Nacional (

Carlos Parera

). El INTA prohibió que se hable del tema. Y apuntó las "culpas" a la reconocida y experimentada científica Virginia Aparicio, del INTA Balcarce.


Insólito: Garmendia y Muñoz participan de sindicatos (el primero en Ate, la segunda en Apinta), que tienen como regla principal defender a los trabajadores.


Era el año 2023. Gobernaba el peronismo de Alberto Fernández.


Persecución y maltrato


No conforme con censurar la investigación Sprint, desde las autoridades del INTA iniciaron un proceso de maltratos de diverso tipo sobre Aparicio. En las evaluaciones institucionales comenzó un sostenido descenso en el ítem "integración" (de 100 puntos pasó a 80 y luego a 60), le cambiaron de funciones a un técnico de su equipo sin siquiera avisarle (mucho menos consultarla), y los profesionales de agronomía no le dejaban participar de reuniones del área ni del grupo de WhatsApp,.


Cuando solicitó utilizar un equipo nuevo para medir plaguicidas (cromatógrafo de alta resolución), las autoridades del Ipads (instituto del INTA-Conicet par el agro) le negaron el permiso y no le permitieron integrar el grupo de trabajo (pese a tratarse de una línea de investigación que desarrolló durante años).


En 2025 se redujo, unilateralmente, la interlocución con el el Director del INTA Balcarce (

Facundo José Quiroz …

author: anred
title: Agrotóxicos, censura y persecución política: ¿qué pasó con la investigación sobre plaguicidas de Virginia Aparicio en el INTA?
content:
Foto de la científica Virginia Aparicio en el campus de la Estación Experimental Agropecuaria Balcarce. Imagen: Agencia Tierra Viva.


Virginia Aparicio, ingeniera agrónoma del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA) e investigadora del Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (CONICET), enfrenta un sumario administrativo cuyo expediente propone su exoneración, la sanción más grave dentro del régimen del empleo público nacional. El proceso se vincula con su participación como coordinadora argentina del proyecto internacional SPRINT, una investigación financiada por la Unión Europea y difundida institucionalmente por el propio INTA, que estudió la presencia de plaguicidas en muestras ambientales, animales, vegetales y humanas.

En junio de 2023, cuando Aparicio iba a presentar los resultados argentinos del estudio, el INTA ordenó suspender la difusión pública de esa información. Seis meses después, el organismo resolvió retirarse del consorcio, con la firma del entonces presidente Mariano Garmendia. Ahora, tres años más tarde, la investigadora podría ser exonerada por su participación en aquel proyecto. En este marco, organizaciones de pueblos fumigados, asambleas ambientales y entidades vinculadas a la defensa de la investigación científica impulsan actualmente una campaña para reclamar su no exoneración.

Por ANRed.


La investigadora

Virginia Aparicio

, ingeniera agrónoma del

Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA)

 e investigadora del

Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (CONICET)

, enfrenta un

sumario administrativo relacionado con su participación como coordinadora argentina del proyecto SPRINT

, una investigación internacional financiada por el programa

Horizon 2020 de la Unión Europea

. Según su abogado, el expediente propone su exoneración,

una sanción que implicaría la pérdida del cargo y la imposibilidad de volver a desempeñarse en organismos estatales

.


El proyecto «

Sustainable Plant Protection Transition: A Global Health Approach» (SPRINT)

 se desarrolló entre 2020 y febrero de 2026 y tuvo a la Argentina como uno de sus once sitios de estudio. El dossier documental reconstruido sobre el proyecto señala que

el INTA figuró como beneficiario argentino del convenio europeo

 y que, durante los primeros años,

la propia institución difundió sus objetivos, resultados y la participación de Aparicio

.


Infografía de los países participante del proyecto Sustaninble Plant Protectcion Transition (SPRINT)


El proyecto buscó estudiar la

presencia de plaguicidas en distintas matrices ambientales y biológicas

. Según la gacetilla difundida en respaldo de Aparicio,

en 2021 se analizaron 4.573 muestras correspondientes a suelo, agua, sedimentos, aire, cultivos, animales y personas

. Allí se afirma: «los resultados fueron más que contundentes, ya que

se encontraron entre 2 y 10 plaguicidas en sangre, de 6 a 13 en orina, hasta 18 en materia fecal y entre 7 y 53 en el aire respirado. Se detectaron agrotóxicos incluso en personas que viven lejos de las fumigaciones, y también en alimentos, polvo del hogar, granos, animales, suelos y agua».


La presentación pública de los resultados argentinos estaba prevista para junio de 2023

. Sin embargo, el INTA instruyó a Aparicio a suspender la misma, en una decisión que fue comunicada el 15 de junio, pocos días antes de la actividad, según reconstruyó el medio

Tierra Viva

, y que el organismo sostuvo que los estudios “exceden la incumbencia institucional”.


El dossier difundido por la campaña por la no exoneración de la investigadora señala que, pocos meses después de aquella suspensión, las autoridades institucionales comunicaron a la coordinación del proyecto su intención de retirarse del consorcio. De esta manera, el 7 de diciembre de 2023,

el entonces presidente del INTA Mariano Garmendia firmó la Resolución 1081/2023 para formalizar la salida

. Al mismo tiempo, el propio registro documental del proyecto muestra que Aparicio continuó vinculada a publicaciones científicas derivadas de SPRINT durante los años siguientes.


Foto: INTA Informa


Ahora, en 2026, la disputa volvió al centro de la escena. Medios que reconstruyeron el expediente señalan que el sumario comenzó a avanzar entre fines de 2024 y comienzos de 2025 y que entre los cargos atribuidos a Aparicio figura un

supuesto perjuicio material a la administración pública

. Mientras que su abogado cuestiona esa acusación y …

author: Comunizar
title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

title: Aufruf zu einem Informationstreffen über die Reise-Umarmung für die Sucher*innen,  Dezember 2026 – Januar 2027
content:
Comisión Sexta Zapatista. Mexiko.

Die Comisión Sexta Zapatista lädt Einzelpersonen, Gruppen, Colectivos, Colectivas, Bewegungen und Organisationen – Anhänger*innen der Sexta und der Erklärung für das Leben – sowie alle ehrlichen Menschen guten Herzens ein

zum Informationstreffen über die Reise einer zapatistischen Delegation nach Mexiko-Stadt, die Treffen mit den Sucher*innen und die kollektive Umarmung für diejenigen, welche Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit für ihre Vermissten suchen.

Dieses wird am 2., 3. und 4. Oktober 2026 im CIDECI in San Cristóbal de Las Casas, Chiapas, Mexiko stattfinden – gemäß folgendem Vorschlag:

.- Ankunft am Freitag, den 2. Oktober.

.- Informationstreffen am Samstag, den 3. Oktober.

Unter Beteiligung von Personen, welche die Sucher*innen-Gruppen, die an den Treffen [in Mexiko-Stadt] teilnehmen möchten, über die Fortschritte informieren werden (Menschenrechtszentrum Fray Bartolomé de Las Casas); [die] über die Finanzen für die Reise [informieren werden] (colectivo »Llegó la Hora«); die Unterkunft und Verpflegung der zapatistischen Delegation und der Gruppen der Sucher*innen (Casa Samir Flores Soberanes); die künstlerischen Kampagnen, die durchgeführt werden, um Fonds zu sammeln; die registrierten Vorschläge zu Aktivitäten innerhalb der Landesmitte im Dezember 2026-Januar 2027 (colectivo Red Universitaria Anticapitalista – RUA); die Aktivitäten, welche verschiedene Musikgruppen, Otroas-AndEre, Stadtteile, Tänzer*innen, Universitätsleute bereits umsetzen (na klar, ohne KI); sowie die Teilnahme der Comisioń Sexta Zapatista, die die Ziele der Initial-Reise der Rundreise für das Leben, Kapitel Mexiko, präzisieren wird (Comisioń Sexta Zapatista).

.- Rückfahrt am Sonntag, den 4. Oktober.

Die Informationstreffen werden im Livestream übertragen. Da es Kosten bedeutet und wegen möglicher ökonomischer, gesundheitlicher und/oder familiärer Probleme oder wegen der Arbeit – wird empfohlen, dass nicht alle kommen, sondern dass Ihr welche schickt, die Euch die detaillierten Informationen übermitteln. Oder dass Ihr welche, die kommen werden, bittet, Euch die Information weiterzugeben sowie während der Pausen Eure Zweifel und Fragen entgegenzunehmen, um diese dann im Präsenztreffen einzubringen.

Nun, es wird ein hybrides Treffen sein: in Präsenz sowie virtuell.

Demnächst werden wir den Link für den Livestream bekanntgeben.

Es ist nicht notwendig, sich zuvor für das Präsenztreffen zu registrieren. Bei der Ankunft im CIDECI kann sich registriert werden.

Aus den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos.

Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés. Mexiko, September 2026.

title: Se profundiza la crisis industrial: vuelve a cerrar Dánica
content:
La planta ya tuvo un cierre a fines de 2024 y una reapertura parcial en febrero de 2025, tras gestiones gremiales y la asistencia económica del gobierno bonaerense. Ahora el Grupo Beltrán, actual propietario de la firma, anunció que clausura definitivamente las operaciones en el establecimiento a partir del 30 de septiembre.


Foto: SOEIA


Dorada S.A., la empresa antes denominada Flora Dánica y que produce la conocida marca de margarina, confirmó el cierre definitivo de su planta de Llavallol, en el conurbano bonaerense, a través de un cartel que la propia firma colocó en la puerta del establecimiento. El aviso, que los trabajadores del turno sabatino encontraron al llegar a las 6 de la mañana sin poder ingresar, fija el fin de la actividad industrial para el próximo 30 de septiembre.


Hace poco menos de dos años atrás la empresa ya pasó por un proceso similar, señalaron desde el Sindicato Aceitero de Capital y GBA (SOEIA), y tras la intervención gremial, se logró que la planta volviera a funcionar en febrero de 2025. “Esas gestiones incluyeron meses de duras negociaciones y gestiones para incorporar a Dorada S.A. al programa PREBA del gobierno bonaerense”, apuntaron.


En esa reapertura parcial, reingresaron a sus puestos de trabajo unos 30 obreros aceiteros, y el plan era ir expandiendo los sectores que volverían a operar. No ocurrió.


Foto: SOEIA


“Hoy nos encontramos ante esta noticia aberrante de que la empresa quiere cerrar nuevamente, echándole la culpa al consumo y a cuestiones operativas”, señalaron desde el gremio, que conduce Ezequiel Roldán, y agregaron: “rechazamos que el costo lo tengan que pagar siempre los trabajadores. Desde el Sindicato y junto a los compañeros trabajadores aceiteros tenemos la firme decisión de seguir defendiendo los puestos de trabajo, el salario y el Convenio Colectivo de Trabajo 420/05 aceitero”.


“Desde el gremio ratificamos la postura de defender los puestos de trabajo, y vamos a seguir haciéndolo hasta las últimas consecuencias”, reafirmaron.


Por su parte, Daniel Yofra, Secretario General de la Federación Aceitera y Desmotadora a nivel nacional, advirtió que el cierre de Dánica es consecuencia de un deterioro más amplio del empleo y la actividad económica: “El país está dinamitado con el tema de los despidos, hay más de 350.000 trabajadores y trabajadoras en la calle, más de 30.000 empresas cerradas”, aseguró en declaraciones a AM750.


Además, el dirigente sindical criticó las políticas del Gobierno nacional al expresar que “no hay créditos blandos, hay una libre importación que hace que no se pueda competir con lo que viene del extranjero”. Para Yofra “el problema es la concepción que tiene un gobierno que claramente quiere vaciar el Estado y que cada uno se arregle como pueda”.


Foto: SOEIA


“Las consecuencias, obviamente, no las pagan los que más tienen, no las paga la casta, como decían ellos, sino los más vulnerables, los jubilados, los trabajadores, los desocupados”, afirmó.


“Ante la pasividad que hay en la sociedad de soportar los embates que tiene un gobierno que claramente desprecia a los más vulnerables, las consecuencias son estas”, cerró.


Foto: SOEIA

title: Cem veículos digitais disseram não às propagandas de Bets
content:
Uma iniciativa capitaneada pela

Agência Pública

 e outros veículos digitais reuniu mais de 100 veículos em editorial conjunto. Lançada em 21 de julho, a iniciativa “Aqui não tem propaganda de bets” procurou pautar o debate dentro da imprensa a respeito da responsabilidade do jornalismo sobre os anúncios que veicula. De início, 15 veículos – Agência Lupa, Agência Pública, Alma Preta, Amado Mundo, Aos Fatos, Manual do Usuário, Matinal, Meio, Mobile Time, My News, Notícia Preta, NeoFeed, Plural, Portal IMPRENSA e Reset – assinaram o editorial conjunto, chamando outros sites a participarem. 


Até o início de setembro, mais de 100 veículos de todo o Brasil aderiram à iniciativa. Entre eles estão os sites Conexão Planeta, Finsiders Brasil, Falando de Tech, Central do Varejo, Click Guarulhos e Portal Meu Amazonas. 


Segundo o editorial conjunto, “o jornalismo, que deve ser, antes de tudo, comprometido com o interesse público”. 


E segue: “Nosso papel é o da defesa da sociedade e, portanto, o de investigar, denunciar com independência o poder indevido do setor e exigir das autoridades regras mais estritas às propagandas e à atuação das bets. Ao aceitar propagandear os jogos online, consideramos que estaríamos contradizendo informações apuradas com rigor pelas nossas equipes”. 


“A seriedade da atual epidemia que tem vulnerabilizado, sobretudo, os mais pobres, não pode ser relativizada por conta de interesses comerciais, sob pena de minar a credibilidade do jornalismo” conclui.


Em meio à campanha eleitoral, o governo Lula prepara uma MP para proibir as bets no País. A medida deve ser assinada nessa sexta-feira, segundo informações da coluna da Alicia Klein no UOL. 


Liberado em 2018 e regulamentado em 2023, durante o atual governo, o setor de apostas online chegou a retirar R$ 62,5 bilhões do orçamento das famílias brasileiras em 2025, segundo um estudo do Comitê Nacional de Secretários de Fazenda dos Estados e do Distrito Federal (Comsefaz).


No mesmo ano, o governo federal arrecadou R$ 9,16 bilhões em impostos. 


Veículos que fazem parte desta iniciativa:

 Agência Lupa, Agência Pública, Alma Preta, Amado Mundo, Aos Fatos, Manual do Usuário, Matinal, Meio, Mobile Time, My News, Notícia Preta, NeoFeed, Plural, Portal IMPRENSA e Reset.

title: KCK commemorates Rıza Altun and the victims of the Diyarbakır Prison massacre
content:
The Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) commemorated Rıza Altun and his comrades, who lost their lives in an airstrike in 2019, as well as ten political prisoners who were killed in the E-Type Prison in Diyarbakır (Amed) on September 24, 1996, on the anniversaries of their deaths.


In a statement, the Co-Presidency of the KCK Executive Council paid tribute to Altun’s role within the Kurdish freedom movement and recalled his political journey from Ankara and North Kurdistan, through Turkey’s prisons, to the movement’s diplomatic work.


The KCK statement on Thursday reads as follows:


“On September 24, 1996, ten of our comrades were brutally killed with nail-studded wooden planks in the E-Type Prison in Diyarbakır. On September 25, 2019, our comrade Rıza Altun, one of the leading cadres of our party, was killed together with our comrades Baz and Garzan in an airstrike. On the anniversaries of their deaths, we commemorate our comrades with respect, love, and gratitude, and renew our promise to fulfill their aspirations.


Our comrade Rıza Altun joined our group together with numerous friends from the Tuzluçayır neighborhood when the Apoist movement first began among university students in Ankara. They significantly strengthened our group. Rıza Altun was among the leading revolutionaries of the period when Tuzluçayır was known as ‘Little Moscow.’ At the time, the neighborhood was strongly shaped by socialist revolutionaries. Not only young socialist militants, but also the people of Tuzluçayır took part in socialist organizing and political struggle.


While our comrade Rıza Altun was active within the Apoist movement in Ankara, he went to Kurdistan in 1976 and became involved in the work in Antep. There, he stood on the front lines of the struggle against fascists while also playing an important role in organizing the youth and the population. During the fighting in Hilvan and Siverek, he served on the Military Council together with Mehmet Karasungur. In this way, he took his place in history as one of the first military commanders of our struggle.


He was among the leading figures of the resistance in Diyarbakır Prison No. 5 and, in every prison to which he was subsequently transferred, worked to establish and uphold the line of that resistance. After his release, he reached Abdullah Öcalan within twenty days. From that point until his death, he assumed leading responsibilities in every sphere of our struggle.


He assumed responsibilities both in Europe and in all parts of Kurdistan. Until his death, he was responsible for the diplomatic work of our freedom movement. He involved not only himself and his friends from Tuzluçayır in this struggle, but also his siblings, nieces and nephews, and thus his entire family. In this respect as well, he took an exemplary place in our freedom struggle. Our comrade Rıza Altun will always be remembered for his distinctive personality within this struggle. His militant spirit will live on in our struggle.


Commemoration of those killed in the prison massacre


Our comrades who were brutally killed in Diyarbakır Prison on September 24, 1996, will never be forgotten. They are among the comrades who were murdered in the most brutal manner in the history of our struggle. Their deaths are concrete testimony to the extremely difficult conditions under which we carried out our resistance. This massacre demonstrated how hostility toward the Kurdish people manifested itself in the reality of the Turkish state.


Their memory is a call for us to intensify the struggle and achieve a free and democratic life for the Kurdish people. They cannot be forgotten. To deserve and attain a free and democratic life means intensifying the struggle to fulfill their aspirations.


With the fighting spirit of our comrade Rıza Altun and our comrades who were brutally killed, we will fulfill their aspirations. To this end, we will keep them alive in our struggle in every sphere. In order to fulfill their aspirations, we will intensify the struggle to successfully bring the Peace and Democratic Society Process to its intended goal.”

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Company seeks to evict Sebaring IP residents
content:
By Aurelia Solaba


The homes of the Cuyonon, Kagayanen, and Palaw’an indigenous residents of Barangay Sebaring, Bugsuk Island, Palawan have been at the mercy of changing tides not just from the flow of the seawater but also from the whims of a powerful company. 


Just like their neighbors in

Sitio Marihangin

, the community is facing displacement because of ecotourism plans in the area. Unlike Sitio Marihangin, however,

San Miguel Corporation

 has no direct involvement. 


Barangay Sebaring’s opponent is an entirely different enterprise, the Normal Holdings and Development Corporation.


Cycle of relocation


In 2018, the company purchased the mother title of Barangay Sebaring from the Gabinete family. The deal did not include the islanders’ homes but the corporation wants their land anyway.


Alex (not their real name), an ally of the islanders, said that the residents’ part of the barangay exists because

“umurong yung dagat”

(the sea receded) and the shoreline expanded. The newly formed beachfront was beyond their original ancestral domain which was the titled property of Honorio Gabinete and Pedro Gabinete. 


As a result, the community relocated to excess land now known as Lots 4625, 4626, and 4628.


“When the island got bigger, the [Gabinete heirs] subdivided it and sold it to us so that we would have a place to live because the Gabinetes just let us stay here,” Hannah (not her real name), an indigenous Kagayanen resident of Barangay Sebaring, said. She added that the sale occurred in 2002.


Eight years later, the community is once again facing relocation. Only this time it is paired with repeated incidents of harassment and allegations of administrative abuse. 


Never free


On January 27, 2025, the community received Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) notifications that Patricia Bianca Chio, Weizenfluh Navarro, and Genevieve See applied for

free patents

 over the lots they call home. 


Hannah and other legal documents mentioned Rodrigo Salo-Ay as Navarro’s co-claimant, however his name is absent from the Notices of Application.


Notices of Application for Free Patent to claim Lots 4625, 4626, and 4628 that were distributed to indigenous residents of Brgy. Sebaring. | Contributed Photographs


According to Romilano Calo, chairperson of the Sambilog – Balik Bugsuk Movement that has been assisting the residents, the four individuals are supposed affiliates of Normal Holdings and Development Corporation. 


If recognized, the free patents will give legal titles for Lots 4625, 4626, and 4628 to the four individuals without need for payment. However, a prerequisite for a free patent is that claimants have freely and openly occupied an area for at least 10 years. 


Until now, Hannah said that nobody in Barangay Sebaring has ever seen Chio, Navarro, Salo-Ay, or See.


Barangay Certificate of Non-Residency that shows Chio, Navarro, Salo-Ay, and See are not recorded inhabitants of Brgy. Sebaring. | Contributed Photographs


Hannah and her community refused to accept the sudden loss of their homes to outsiders. Within 15 days, on February 11, 2025, they filed their first verified protest against the Notices of Application at the Brooke’s Point Office of the DENR. 


The case was rejected. 


“The DENR Brooke’s Point [office] denied [our protest] because they said that we need a [Certificate of] File Action that would be provided by our barangay. We called… our attorney [from Sambilog] and they said, we don’t need a File Action because those who applied [for Free Patents] are not really from Barangay Sebaring,” Hannah said. 


Emboldened by their attorney’s advice, they filed a new protest on March 28, 2025, where the DENR required them to prove their occupation of the disputed lots. For Alex, the barangay’s denial of Certificates of Residency to some community members of Barangay Sebaring complicated the issue.


Hannah and Calo opined that the Sebaring barangay office has allied itself with Normal Holdings and Development Corporation.


“We don’t have direct evidence to show that the barangay captain is directly involved in this [land dispute issue],” Alex said. “But what we do know is there is a refusal to perform the duties of the barangay itself.” 


Cost


Despite the lack of official support, the community continues to exhaust administrative remedies for addressing the dispute.


Without proper funding from the barangay, the residents scrape together money to cover fuel …

author: groundxero
title: ‘They Knew He Wanted to Kill Me’: 17y/o Survivor of Near Fatal Acid Attack in Bhiwani Exposes Rural Haryana’s Cultures of Silence and Inaction
content:
[

21 September 2026, New Delhi:

 More than a year after the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) took Suo motu cognizance of a heinous case of a father’s attempt to murder and assault with acid his own teenage daughter in a small village in Haryana’s Bhiwani district, local police have still not fulfilled their directive of investigating the case and ensuring relief for the survivor.


 


The alleged crime took place on 3rd August 2025. The latest order to the Bhiwani Police, issued by the NHRC on 18 March 2026 (yet another in an allegedly long line of directives for an urgent Action Taken Report (ATR) to be filed along-with a call for additional information) has long passed its two-week deadline.


 


“This matter has been with us for over a year,” the NHRC told

GroundXero

 on Monday, 21 September 2026. “The latest order was issued in March demanding the submission of additional information regarding the victim’s rehabilitation and financial compensation according to the Women and Child Development Department’s Scheme for Relief and Rehabilitation of Women Acid Victims, but has received no response.” The NHRC declined to comment on their further plan of action.


 


Such orders have been issued repeatedly to the Bhiwani Police since a former member of Haryana’s State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR) complained to the NHRC regarding the police’s inaction on 7 August 2025, just as they have been repeatedly ignored. No further action has been taken in the matter since the first week of April, when the latest call for ATR was due.


 


We are publishing a year-old investigative report into the incident by

MOULI SHARMA

and

 VISHNU KHANAWALIA

]


 


‘They Knew He Wanted to Kill Me’: 17y/o Survivor of Near Fatal Acid Attack in Bhiwani Exposes Rural Haryana’s Cultures of Silence and Inaction


 


On 3rd of August 2025, 17-year-old Monica from Ghuskani—a small village in Haryana’s Bhiwani district—survived not only an acid attack and horrifying murder attempt by her own father, but also a centuries long culture of silence where familial secrecy and honour codes disguise a long legacy of controlled—and legalised—violence. One that dictates women’s lives, and so too their brutal, quiet deaths. Monica’s assault was far from the sensational, freak incident local news made it out to be, but a consequence of systematic cover-up of serial abuse and violent crime. Now, she wants justice; who will make sure she gets it?


 


Rear side of the house of Monica, Mangal and Satyavaan. Monica’s screams were reportedly heard up to this location. August 2025/MOULI SHARMA


 


21st August 2025, Ghuskani, Haryana:

 Sunday morning, on the 3rd of August, seventeen-year-old Monica woke up to a slow day in her home in Haryana’s Bhiwani district. Her father, Satyavaan, wasn’t home very often from his full-time job at the local nursery—and he wasn’t very nice when he was.


 


“He didn’t much like me. He used to like my brother before, but since he began siding with me more and more often, even he got into his bad books,” Monica tells

Himal

.


 


On Sunday, her brother was going to return from a few days away at an aunt’s home in another village, and Monica felt lighter. She had a cup of tea, scrolled through the apps on her phone, completed the chores around the house and fell asleep, looking forward to a good day after a long week.


 


She turned out to be very, very wrong.


 


“I woke up to fire all over my face and body. My father had thrown acid in my face, and then tried to kill me,” Monica says.


 


3 days after the assault, an anonymous phone call to a social activist sent the matter to the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), with allegations of serial murder added to the mix of titillating family crime. Monica’s case became not only the first of an acid-attack in her village, but the beginning of something huge; unbeknownst to her, she had survived not only a particularly bad day, but a history of quiet killings and corruption in her family as well as her culture going back at least fourteen years.


 


A Particularly Bad Day


 


After attacking her with acid while she was sleeping, accused father Satyavaan Dalaal unsuccessfully attempted to kill Monica, who goes by her first name.


 


“I ran to save my life, screaming,” she says, but running away from one’s assailant becomes considerably trickier with acid working its way into one’s eyes.

author: Joseph Bognot at Ara Jane Credo
title: Mula Martial Law hanggang ngayon, nagpapatuloy ang laban para sa tahanan at kabuhayan
content:
Hindi lamang alaala ng nakaraan ang bitbit ng mga lumahok sa malawakang kilos-protesta noong Setyembre 21.

Para sa mga nagprotesta, ang mga aral at pakikibaka noong diktadurang Marcos Sr. ay hindi iba sa kalagayan sa ilalim naman ngayon ng administrasyong Marcos Jr. kung saan nagpapatuloy ang kalbaryo ng maralita para sa tirahan, kabuhayan at karapatan.

Kasabay ng paggunita sa ika-54 na anibersaryo ng deklarasyon ng Martial Law, inilabas ng mga maralita sa lansangan ang mga suliraning kinakaharap nila sa araw-araw partikular sa banta ng demolisyon, kawalan ng katiyakan sa tirahan, pagbaha sa mga komunidad, at patuloy na pagtaas ng presyo ng pagkain at iba pang batayang serbisyo.

Hindi na bago sa mga maralita ang pangambang mawalan ng tirahan bunsod ng mga proyektong pangkaunlaran.

Ilang araw matapos ang deklarasyon ng Martial Law noong Setyembre 1972 sa ilalim ng diktadurang Marcos Sr., nilagdaan ang Letter of Instruction No. 19 na nag-utos sa pagpapaalis ng mga itinuturing na “illegal structures” sa mga lugar gaya ng mga pampang ng ilog at kanal, riles ng tren, at iba pang pampubliko at pribadong lupain.

Sa Tondo, nagkaroon ng kaliwa’t kanang demolisyon sa mga komunidad sa Tondo Foreshore. Kabilang sa mga lugar na naapektuhan ang mga komunidad sa paligid ng Parola at iba pang bahagi ng Tondo na saklaw ng mga planong pagpapaunlad sa North Harbor at Tondo Foreshore.

Noong 1974, nilikha naman sa pamamagitan ng Presidential Decree No. 570 ang Tondo Foreshore Development Authority upang ipatupad ang mga programa sa pagpapaunlad ng lugar. Sa mga sumunod na taon, isinulong ng administrasyong Marcos Sr. ang Tondo Foreshore-Dagat-Dagatan Urban Development Project, na kinapapalooban ng pagpapaunlad ng lugar, land tenure at relokasyon ng mga residenteng maaapektuhan.

Makalipas ang mahigit limang dekada, muling humaharap ang mga maralita sa Tondo at Port Area ng pangamba sa katiyakan sa paninirahan kaugnay ng itinatayong North-South Harbor Bridge (NSHB), isang malaking proyektong pang-imprastraktura sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos Jr.

Para kay Julia Barquin, lider-kababaihan sa Baseco, hindi lamang pagkawala ng tahanan ang nakataya sa proyekto kundi pati ang kabuhayang matagal nang nakaugat sa kanilang komunidad.

“Mawawalan kami ng pamumuhay. Madaling maghanap ng kabuhayan sa Maynila, katulad ng pagbabalat ng bawang, pagtitinda ng mga kakanin at street food. Hindi katulad ng mga lilipatan na walang hanapbuhay, umpisa na naman,” ani Barquin.

“Kaya nandito kami ngayon at sumama sa pagkilos na ito dahil ipinapanawagan namin yung karapatan namin bilang mga naninirahan sa komunidad ng Tondo. Huwag naman kaming i-demolish bilang inyong nasasakupan at kilalanin yung karapatan namin bilang naninirahan sa komunidad,” dagdag pa niya.

Makasaysayan na rin ang pakikibaka ng mga maralita sa Tondo Foreshore laban sa demolisyon, harassment at iba pang usapin hinggil sa katiyakan sa paninirahan. Noong 1970, bago pa ideklara ang Martial Law, itinatag ng mga residente ang Samahan ng Mamamayan-Zone One Tondo (SM-ZOTO), na naglunsad ng iba’t ibang kampanya at paglaban sa banta ng demolisyon. Sa kasalukuyan, iba’t ibang samahan at grupo ng mga residente ang tumitindig kaugnay ng nagpapatuloy nilang kalbaryo sa paninirahan.

Kasabay nito, inalala ni Barquin ang sunod-sunod na sunog na tumama sa mga komunidad sa Tondo Foreshore, partikular sa Parola at Baseco, ngayong taon.

Noong Marso 6, isang sunog sa Parola ang nag-iwan ng 349 pamilyang nawalan ng tirahan. Hindi pa man nakakabangon ang komunidad mula sa trahedya, muling nilamon ng apoy ang Parola noong Mayo 23, na nakaapekto sa mahigit 7,000 indibidwal o 2,134 pamilya.

Ilang araw lamang ang lumipas, sumiklab naman ang sunog sa bahagi ng Gasangan, Baseco noong Mayo 30, na nakaapekto sa higit 85 pamilya o 340 indibidwal. Isang menor de edad ang nasawi sa insidente.

Sa gitna ng magkakasunod na sunog, isinagawa naman noong Mayo 20 ang groundbreaking ceremony para sa NSHB sa Baseco.

Sa Baseco at Parola, nakatakdang dumaan ang 2.026-kilometrong tulay na mag-uugnay sa Parola sa North Harbor at Baseco sa South Harbor. Nauna nang inaprubahan ang NSHB sa ilalim ng administrasyong Duterte at iginawad ang kontrata sa China Road and Bridge Corporation.

Ipinagpatuloy naman ito sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos Jr. bilang bahagi ng infrastructure flagship projects sa ilalim ng Build Better More program na nagkakahalagang P6.753 bilyon.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: ‘Human rights reparation starts with justice’
content:
Portraits of enforced disappearance victims. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

MANILA – All human rights violation victims should receive reparation consistent with domestic laws and international obligations.

“From a victim-oriented perspective, the State must recognize that different human rights violations may require various kinds of reparations based on the demands of the victims, their families, and communities which they belong to, to correct the wrongs and achieve healing,” the 2026 Commission on Human Rights (CHR) position paper stated. “Essentially, reparation should be proportional to the gravity of the violations committed and the extent of harm suffered.”

“When my daughter was killed, we received no single assistance nor investigation from the authorities. Not the barangay, not the police. Not one from the government offered help,” Sally Ramos told Bulatlat. Her daughter was killed in 2017 by four unidentified men at the height of the anti-drug campaign.

She said, “We are poor, I do not have a job. My daughter who was killed had a job before she was killed. She supported us for our daily needs and in taking care of my two grandchildren. That is why it was hard for me to accept her passing.”

Read: Ten years on, Duterte’s kill order strikes deep

While it supports the passage of Human Rights Violations Victims Compensations Act (House Bill No. 580), CHR recommends a harmonized definition of victims of human rights violations as persons whose human rights were violated by persons acting in an official capacity and by agents of the State, as well as due to the State’s failure to perform its obligations to prevent, investigate, punish, and redress the private actors’ abuse.

However, human rights group Karapatan disagreed with the bill’s definition that human rights violations are committed by “State or Non-State actors.”

“States are duty-bearers of rights and as such have obligations under international human rights law far greater than non-State actors, and thus the term ‘human rights violations’ should pertain to those committed by State actors. Meanwhile, those allegedly committed by Non-State actors are considered offenses against persons and as such are covered by provisions under criminal and civil laws,” Karapatan Secretary-General Cristina Palabay said.

The existing Victims Compensation Program under Republic Act 7309 provides reparation for martial law victims-survivors. The proposed bill complements this, covering cases and victims that fall outside the scope of RA 7309, particularly those involving indirect State responsibility, non-state actors, or failures of State protection.

“Acknowledging the HRVs committed against the victims is an essential step toward healing, community reconciliation, and justice. This measure will not only affirm the rights of the victims, but will also ensure that acts of grave injustice and abuse will be legally penalized and no victims, regardless of the nature of the violation, will be left disregarded,” the CHR said.

“Compensation could be a big help for the victims’ families, especially if those killed or disappeared were the breadwinners of their families” Cora Jazmines said. Her husband James, a labor rights defender, was forcibly disappeared on August 23, 2024 around 10 p.m., after celebrating the birthday of his friend, Felix Salaveria, Jr. It was Salaveria who reported James’ disappearance. Five days later, Salaveria was also abducted. Both of them remain missing.

Jazmines was among the signatories of a letter to the Supreme Court, urging them to review the writs of amparo and habeas data this August 2026. The court granted the petition for writ of amparo but it has not yielded positive results for their search.

Read: Not one surfaced despite court orders, families demand review of legal remedies

“The majority of Filipino families struggle to make ends meet. As a result, many of the issues raised by HRV victims center on advancing and protecting the basic rights of citizens, including access to adequate food, decent wages and livelihoods, quality education, housing, and healthcare services,” Jazmines said, stressing that if the primary breadwinner of the family was subjected to state violence, the family left behind can be pushed even deeper into poverty.

The bill has been pending with the House Committee on Human Rights since July 29, 2025. The State’s duty to provide reparation is also stated in the International Covenant on Civil and …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Will Kuai Kuai Workers Strike?
content:
WORKERS AT ONE of Taiwan’s best-known snack companies, Kuai Kuai, have voted in favor of a strike.

The strike authorization takes place after an announcement by the company that it would be selling the land on which its existing factory sits on in Zhongli and moving to Hsinchu. The two sites are 39 kilometers from each other, meaning that the move is untenable for many workers.

In particular, workers were only informed of the land scale on September 1st. According to the Ministry of Labor, the move was not expected for another two years. The factory has operated in Zhongli since 1968, and 1/3rd of workers at Kuai Kuai have worked there for more than thirty years, despite the fact that their wages are near minimum wage.

The land sale is ironic. Namely, the land will be sold to Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc. At a time when the semiconductor sector is dominant, as fueled by the AI boom, this has led to significant land acquisitions by semiconductor companies.

Yet Kuai Kuai is an iconic snack in the technology industry. Namely, it is a common superstition in Taiwan that bags of Kuai Kuai can prevent machines and equipment from malfunctioning. It is ironic that Kuai Kuai workers are being thrown under the bus by the very industry the snack is associated with.

Workers have accused the San-Ti Group that owns Kuai Kuai of perhaps having only acquired the company with an eye on selling its land. Kuai Kuai workers were only offered a 5% pay increase and verbal assurances that they would be relocated to the new factory.

In response, however, Kuai Kuai workers have voted by 149 “yes” votes to 2 “no” votes and one abstention to authorize a strike if their demands are not met. Kuai Kuai workers call for the monthly salaries of workers to be increased by 10,000 NT, as well as for the company to share its AI windfall with workers. This is to be codified in writing, while workers who do not relocate are to be provided with severance packages. Kuai Kuai workers have criticized the company’s offer of a 5% pay increase as only in line with government-mandated increases to minimum wage.

It is to be seen how Kuai Kuai’s management will respond. For its part, the company management has expressed disappointment in workers, and may decide to contest workers. In the meantime, it is to be seen how workers at one of Taiwan’s best-known snack companies engage with the public if they launch a strike–given the iconic nature of Kuai Kuai, a potential strike is likely to be one of the more visible labor actions in Taiwan in recent years.

author: rti_admin
title: AI for Humanity: A Buddhist Ethical Framework for the Age of Artificial Intelligence
content:
Artificial Intelligence is rapidly becoming one of the most transformative technologies in human history. In a remarkably short period, AI has moved from a specialised computational technology to a general-purpose tool capable of writing, designing, analysing, reasoning, generating images and video, assisting scientific research, and increasingly performing tasks once considered uniquely human.

This extraordinary development has produced two contrasting visions of the future. One imagines AI ushering in an age of unprecedented abundance, where machines perform much of the world’s intellectual and physical labour and humanity is liberated from scarcity. The other warns that increasingly autonomous and powerful AI systems could become difficult to control and, in an extreme scenario, pose an existential threat to humanity.

Both possibilities deserve serious consideration.

The crucial question, therefore, is not simply how intelligent AI can become, but what values will guide that intelligence.

Intelligence without wisdom can become dangerous. Power without character can become destructive. Knowledge without compassion can become indifferent to human suffering. And technological progress without concern for society’s welfare can increase inequality rather than reduce it.

This is where an ancient ethical tradition offers a remarkably relevant perspective.

The Buddhist concepts of Prajñā (wisdom), Śīla (ethical conduct or character), Karuṇā (compassion), and Bahujan Hitāya–Bahujan Sukhāya (for the welfare and happiness of the many) can provide a useful philosophical framework for thinking about the future of Artificial Intelligence.

Intelligence Is Not the Same as Wisdom

Modern AI is fundamentally an achievement of intelligence: the ability to process enormous quantities of information, recognise patterns, generate responses, optimise objectives and increasingly perform complex reasoning.

But intelligence and wisdom are not synonymous.

A system can be extraordinarily capable at achieving an objective while having no intrinsic understanding of whether that objective is morally desirable. An AI system may be able to determine the most efficient way of achieving a goal, but efficiency does not answer the question: Should that goal be pursued in the first place?

This distinction is central to the future of AI.

Human civilisation has repeatedly demonstrated that technological capability does not automatically produce moral progress. The same scientific knowledge that gives us medicine can also produce devastating weapons. The same communication technologies that connect billions of people can also facilitate manipulation and hatred.

Therefore, as AI becomes more powerful, humanity needs something beyond greater computational intelligence.

In the Buddhist intellectual tradition, Prajñā is associated with deeper understanding and discernment: the capacity to see reality clearly rather than merely accumulate information. Applied to AI governance, this suggests that every major AI decision should involve a fundamental question:

Is this action merely possible, or is it wise?

An AI system may be capable of doing something. A corporation may find it profitable. A government may find it strategically advantageous. But none of these facts establishes that it should be done.

Prajñā introduces the missing dimension of judgement.

Śīla: Intelligence Must Operate Within Ethical Boundaries

The second principle is Śīla, broadly understood as ethical conduct, discipline, and moral character.

One of the central challenges of advanced AI is that systems are increasingly capable of operating autonomously. They can make recommendations, execute tasks, interact with other systems, and potentially influence decisions affecting millions of people.

The greater the autonomy, the greater the importance of ethical constraints.

An AI system should not be designed merely to maximise whatever metric its creator specifies. A recommendation algorithm designed exclusively to maximise engagement, for example, may discover that outrage, addiction or sensationalism produces better engagement than balanced information.

The algorithm may be performing exactly as designed.

The problem is the design objective.

Śīla therefore suggests a deeper principle:

The means by which AI achieves its objectives must be subject to ethical constraints, not merely judged by the outcome.

AI systems should be designed around principles such as honesty …

author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)
