author: Andrea DiP
title: Governadora de Pernambuco sugere laqueadura forçada: por que certas mulheres não importam?
content:
Raquel Lyra, governadora de Pernambuco e candidata à reeleição pelo PSD, aparece em um vídeo divulgado pelo portal Metrópoles no último domingo (20), sugerindo que uma mulher seja esterilizada sem seu conhecimento.

 O episódio aconteceu em 2025, quando Lyra visitava o Hospital Regional Dom Moura, em Garanhuns.

No vídeo

, uma mulher, provavelmente funcionária do hospital, gesticula com as mãos ao falar sobre a barriga de uma paciente que não aparece nas imagens. “Chega assim, ó, gestante, desse tamanho, com sete ‘menino’ na barriga”. Ao que a governadora responde: “Aí tem que fazer laqueadura, visse? A gente bota na fila da laqueadura”. Alguém diz algo ininteligível e ela acrescenta: “Mas faz sem ela saber”.


O vídeo viralizou, e a governadora assumiu a fala, pediu desculpas,

 mas em nota ao Metrópoles, terminou dizendo que a “eleição deve ser decidida na apresentação de propostas, não na fabricação de ataques”

e que


a divulgação do vídeo “trata-se de mais uma tentativa de desviar o foco do que realmente importa, que é Pernambuco”. 


Esse “o que realmente importa”, pra mim, aponta o cerne da questão: a de que

algumas mulheres não importam, ou umas importam mais do que outras. E alguns úteros podem ser mais tutelados – pelo Estado, pela religião, pela medicina, pela política

, dentro de uma visão eugenista, racista e misógina. O Brasil tem uma longa história com isso.


A laqueadura é um procedimento cirúrgico de esterilização que tem como objetivo impedir a gravidez. Faz-se um corte na ligação entre os ovários e o útero, que é feita por meio das trompas.

E fazer uma laqueadura sem informar ou ter o consentimento da mulher é crime no Brasil, com pena de até oito anos de prisão e multa.


Em 2018,

a

Agência Pública

 contou a história de Janaína

, uma mulher de 35 anos do interior de São Paulo que, em situação de vulnerabilidade, teve uma laqueadura determinada pela Justiça. A reportagem conta que o Ministério Público determinou um prazo para que a prefeitura esterilizasse Janaina, sob a alegação de que ela era “pessoa hipossuficiente, apresenta grave quadro de dependência química, sendo usuária contumaz de substâncias entorpecentes, além de ser mãe de cinco filhos” e de que “não tem condições financeiras de arcar com os correspondentes custos”. Pouco antes de a decisão ser emitida, foi anexada ao processo uma certidão firmada em cartório, em que Janaina concordava com a realização da laqueadura. Mas em entrevista à

Pública

, ela disse não saber ler ou escrever e afirmou ter assinado o documento sem saber do que se tratava.


Janaína foi esterilizada à força, e apenas anos depois recebeu uma compensação do Estado por essa violência. 


Mas dá pra ir além.

Nos anos 1990, uma CPMI da laqueadura involuntária foi instaurada, presidida pela deputada Benedita da Silva, para investigar a incidência de esterilização em massa de mulheres no Brasil. Números do IBGE apontavam que 45% das mulheres em idade fértil estavam esterilizadas na época, índices muito superiores aos de outros países.

 E o

relatório final

 da CPMI dizia: “É sintomático constatar que o maior percentual de esterilizadas encontra-se exatamente nos Estados e regiões que concentram os maiores índices de miséria e pobreza do nosso país e onde a composição populacional aponta para uma maioria negra, como por exemplo o Nordeste e o Centro-Oeste. Por outro lado, em Estados de maioria branca, como por exemplo o Rio Grande do Sul, o índice de mulheres esterilizadas fica abaixo da média nacional”.

A CPMI concluiu que as mulheres passavam pelos procedimentos sem o devido conhecimento necessário, imediatamente após cesarianas, que laqueaduras eram oferecidas como escambo eleitoral ou como único método contraceptivo disponível. Apontava ainda que “havia um claro interesse internacional no controle demográfico no Brasil”.


Uma

reportagem

 do Intercept, também de 2018, lembrou o que foi esse interesse estrangeiro: “Esses programas eram capitaneados por entidades que, segundo diversos depoimentos, seguiam orientações que constam no chamado Relatório Kissinger, documento norte-americano classificado como sigiloso (…). O Relatório Kissinger foi adotado como política oficial pelo presidente Gerald Ford em 1975 e defendia que o crescimento populacional dos países menos desenvolvidos era uma ameaça para a segurança nacional americana, pois geraria riscos de distúrbios civis e instabilidade política. Para conter o avanço demográfico, o relatório defendia a …

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Tenemos solamente a un acusado en el banquillo, pero sabemos que hay más civiles responsables de las desapariciones de nuestros compañeros”
content:
Ante el Tribunal Oral Federal 2 de La Plata, el pasado 10 de septiembre comenzó el juicio por crímenes de lesa humanidad en la causa Molinos Río de La Plata contra Emilio Parodi, quien fue jefe de personal de la planta de Avellaneda desde octubre de 1975 hasta 1979, por el secuestro de tres trabajadores de la empresa. “Él fue quien daba las listas de los compañeros militantes que trabajaban en ese entonces en la planta”, señaló Ezequiel Roldán, el secretario general del Sindicato de Aceiteros de CABA y Gran Buenos Aires y secretario gremial de la Federación Aceitera.


Por Christian Madia para Agencia Andar


El Gremio de Aceiteros es uno de los querellantes en la causa Molinos Río de La Plata, pero el derrotero para llegar a este juicio se remonta a 2013. “Una de las primeras personas que comenzó con esto hace 13 años fue Ceferino Mataboni, hijo de Rubén Mataboni, a quien apodaban “el Verdura”, un delegado gremial de Molinos Río de la Plata que fue secuestrado el 3 de diciembre de 1976. Ceferino se presentó en el sindicato a pedir toda la documentación que teníamos de aquellos años. Más tarde, una vez que nosotros pudimos sacar a la burocracia sindical, contactamos a Ceferino y construimos una linda relación. Le entregamos todo lo que teníamos a disposición, tanto en el propio sindicato como en la federación. A partir de ahí, en 2013, arranca la causa judicial. Y, en 2015, nosotros nos presentarnos como querellantes”.


La empresa Molinos Río de La Plata pertenecía por entonces al grupo Bunge & Born, y fue en la planta ubicada en la localidad de Avellaneda donde se produjeron los secuestros y desapariciones de trabajadores. Hoy, tres de esos casos forman parte de la causa: Francisco Fernández, un mecánico que había ingresado a trabajar a Molinos en 1973, fue secuestrado cuando fue a buscar su tarjeta de ingreso a la oficina de vigilancia. Iba dispuesto a iniciar su turno y, cuando estaba por marcar tarjeta, se lo llevaron unos hombres vestidos de traje. El segundo caso es el de Santos Ojeda, que pertenecía a la sección expedición y se lo llevaron a la salida de la fábrica después de su jornada laboral, a las 5 de la mañana. Los testimonios indicaron que fue detenido por integrantes de Coordinación Federal. Gregoria Figueredo de Segovia, tía de Ojeda, denunció ante la CONADEP que supo por un compañero de trabajo de su sobrino que los hombres que lo secuestraron se habían presentado ante el jefe de Personal de la planta (Emilio Parodi) y le habían pedido que identificara a Ojeda. El tercer caso es el de Roberto José Rivolta Bonino: trabajaba en la fábrica desde 1974 y pertenecía al sector administrativo. Lo secuestraron a las ocho de la mañana cuando llegó para comenzar su jornada laboral. Todos estos casos ocurrieron el miércoles 7 de julio de 1976.


“Nosotros sabemos que Emilio Parodi, que era el gerente general de Bunge & Born y jefe de Recursos Humanos de Molinos Río de la Plata, fue cómplice de estos secuestros. Él fue quien daba las listas de los compañeros militantes que trabajaban en ese entonces en la planta”, afirma Roldán.


Pero Molinos Río de La Plata tuvo más trabajadores desaparecidos, un total de 26: Francisco Fernández, Rubén Mataboni, Eduardo Rosen, Roberto Rivolta, Héctor Vidal y su esposa María Inés Ávila, Humberto Dippólito, Juan Carlos Pasquarrosa, José Jacinto Pasquarrosa, Héctor Dadin Vasere, Avelino Freitas, José Luis Salazar, Carlos Robles, Alfredo Patiño, Carlos de Jesús Espíndola, Santos Ojeda, Ricardo Avelino Almaraz y su esposa Celia Arzamendia, Graciela Vitale, Juan Omar Durante, José Vega, Marcos Augusto Vázquez, Jorge Luis Gurrea, René Albornoz, su esposa Elba Noemí Musacchio y Paula Noemí Albornoz Musacchio, hija de ambos y apropiada luego de la desaparición de sus padres cuando tenía seis meses.


Roldán comenta la importancia del avance de la causa y lograr la condena de los responsables empresariales: “lo fundamental es que hayamos llegado a esta instancia de juicio, es algo histórico para nosotros que se enjuicie a civiles que fueron parte de la dictadura cívico-militar. Vale aclarar que no vamos a quedarnos únicamente con esto, también exigimos saber dónde están los demás cómplices, porque no fue sólo Parodi. Y al mismo tiempo, aunque hoy la causa sea por tres compañeros, también vamos a pedir justicia por todos los desaparecidos de Molinos”.


La labor sobre derechos humanos que viene llevando adelante el Sindicato Aceitero no es nueva. Han logrado que los propios trabajadores …

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit council rejects renaming sewage lagoon ‘Trump Lake’
content:
A call to rename Iqaluit’s sewage lagoon Trump Lake died without a vote after no one seconded deputy Mayor Kim Smith’s motion during Tuesday night’s council meeting.


“I figure if (U.S. President Donald Trump) can rename landmarks, then so can we — and we can share a very polite Canadian giggle while we do,” Smith said as she presented her motion, adding no sign would be erected nor any public funds used if the lagoon were to be “symbolically renamed.”


Trump has signed executive orders to rename two bodies of water — the Gulf of Mexico in February 2025 and Lake Ontario in August. The new names, Gulf of America and Lake America respectively, are officially changed in the U.S. government’s Geographic Names Information System, and all federal departments and agencies must follow suit.

But the change does not apply outside the United States.


In her roughly three-minute pitch, Smith expressed her opposition to several of Trump’s actions, including his threats to take over Greenland, the Iran war, and the ongoing trade war with Canada.


The U.S. president has repeatedly mused, joked and threatened to make Canada the “51st state,” and his aggressive use of tariffs has caused economic uncertainty across the nation.


Coun. Kyle Sheppard was the only other councillor to speak to the motion.


He said that while he shares Smith’s “disdain for the current U.S. administration,” he embraced a sentiment expressed in a 2016 campaign speech by former First Lady Michelle Obama: “When they go low, we go high.”


Smith told Nunatsiaq News after the meeting she regarded her act “a success” despite the result.


“My goal at the end of the day was to let residents know that I am all too aware that they are feeling the squeeze, and to give them something to laugh at when they drive down the causeway,” she said.

author: Unknown
title: Torino è contro il riarmo: un inizio di mobilitazione verso e oltre il corteo contro il riarmo del 24 ottobre
content:
Ripubblichiamo il resoconto della due giorni del 19-20 settembre tenutasi a Torino contro il riarmo uscito dalle varie realtà che portano avanti il coordinamento cittadino.


Due giorni ricchi di contenuti, dibattito e socialità. Abbiamo condiviso ragionamenti che vengono direttamente dalle lotte portate avanti in città con l’obiettivo di elaborare una strategia collettiva capace di opporsi al riarmo a partire dalla nostra città. 


Sabato 19 settembre con Elena Basile e Giorgio Monestarolo abbiamo condiviso un’analisi sulle responsabilità delle élite europee e del nostro governo nella guerra in Europa, della crisi profonda che viviamo e della assurda posizione suicida di questi governi nel voler protrarre la guerra in Ucraina e prepararsi alla guerra alla Russia, giustificandolo con il mantra della “difesa”. In tutto questo il genocidio a Gaza va avanti, ma la Palestina ci ha insegnato a lottare anche qui da noi. Non sarà trasformando Torino, né qualsiasi altro territorio, in hub del riarmo che si uscirà da questa crisi. 


Abbiamo bisogno di maggiore coordinamento, abbiamo bisogno di mezzi informativi capaci di portare il nostro discorso chiaro in tutti gli ambiti in cui viviamo e lottiamo. La giornata di domenica 20 settembre è stata un primo tentativo di risposta a questo interrogativo: come contrapporci a tutto questo? A partire dal territorio, passando per la formazione e la sanità, sino al lavoro è fondamentale individuare le contraddizioni che nella nostra città e nella nostra regione vediamo in modo da aprire spazi di contrapposizione alla deriva bellica. Solo unendo le nostre intelligenze, capacità e punti di vista possiamo farlo.


Per continuare questo lavoro ci incontreremo ancora in un tour di assemblee in vari luoghi della città: lo faremo per approfondire il discorso che vogliamo costruire e per coinvolgere sempre più persone in questa mobilitazione. Il 24 ottobre il corteo contro il riarmo sarà un’ulteriore tappa, già raccolta dalle scuole, dai comitati e dalle università. 


Due giorni passati insieme sotto gli alberi dei giardini Pozzo, accompagnati da ottima musica grazie a @omini, @giorgio nieloud e @murubutu special Guest. Grazie a chi ha cucinato la polentata popolare, a chi ha spostato panche, a chi ha ascoltato, a chi ha dato fiducia a una nuova possibilità. 


A presto per il calendario con il tour di assemblee e le prossime tappe di avvicinamento!


Torino è partigiana!

author: Corey Larocque
title: NTI president extols the power of an ‘informed Inuk’ at Kivalliq Trade Show
content:
The world is changing fast, as are interests in the North. There’s pressure to mine Nunavut’s natural resources and to develop infrastructure projects that support Arctic security and sovereignty.


That’s why Inuit need to listen to each other, to their communities and to their youth, says Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. president Gloria Uluqsi.


Big decisions lie ahead about the impacts of future economic activity.


“An informed Inuk is much harder to leave out of a decision that affects them,” Uluqsi said Tuesday in a speech to the Kivalliq Trade Show in Rankin Inlet this week.


She didn’t mention any projects by name. But there has been talk at the trade show about Agnico Eagle Mines’ gold mining and exploration, as well as the four nation-building projects going through the federal government’s Major Projects Office.


Those projects are the Kivalliq Hydro-Fibre Project, the Grays Bay Road and Port Project, a hydroelectricity generator near Iqaluit, and a deepsea port in Qikiqtarjuaq.


Uluqsi leaned into the trade show’s theme — Naalagit, or “Listen” in English. She spoke about what it means to listen and what it means to be heard.


As projects move forward, Inuit need to be heard by government and developers, she said. It has to be a true consultation.


“We need to be involved early enough to really help define the problem, identify the opportunities, consider the risk, and shape the options,” said Uluqsi, a former Government of Nunavut public servant who won the NTI presidency in a May byelection.


“Being asked what we think after the decisions have been made is not meaningful participation.”


NTI advocates for the rights Nunavut Inuit are entitled to under the Nunavut Agreement, and Uluqsi said her organization has a responsibility to ensure Inuit beneficiaries understand those rights.


She also talked about the importance of encouraging young people to have confidence in themselves and about inspiriting Nunavut’s Inuit.


Trade shows are traditionally where businesspeople come together with a goal of making deals with each other. But Uluqsi encouraged participants to do more than exchange business cards and contracts.


She called on participants to exchange knowledge and ideas.


Listening doesn’t always mean agreeing or being liked. But it leads to a better understanding.


“If I understand why you hold your position, and you understand why I hold mine, we have a much better place to begin. That is how relationships are built. That is how trust is built, and that is how better decisions are made.”


The Kivalliq Trade Show ends Wednesday.

author: Joseph Lee
title: As climate disasters multiply, Indigenous governance offers a way forward
content:
Indigenous lands from Canada to Ecuador to Nepal are increasingly being hit by catastrophic storms, fires, and floods. Worse, these climate disasters often come one after the other as overlapping crises rather than isolated incidents. Still, despite the ongoing destruction, Indigenous peoples continue to prove that they have the knowledge and skills to respond, if only global powers will let them. 


Even amid growing recognition by scientists and policymakers of the power of Indigenous expertise to respond to climate change, the key role that Indigenous governance plays in those knowledge systems has not received as much respect.


That’s according to a new report from

Land Is Life

 that highlights the global success of Indigenous climate adaptation and resilience amid escalating crises. The report also says supporting Indigenous governance through legal recognition, financing, and partnerships — none of which are occurring on a large scale — is the best way to reduce climate disaster risk worldwide. 


“We show that it’s not that they are only the most impacted, but they are already implementing effective solutions,” said Luisa Castañeda Quintana, the executive director of Land Is Life, a global nonprofit dedicated to Indigenous self-determination. “When it comes to adaptation, we don’t really need to create new structures or systems. We just need to see what is working.”


The report adds to an expansive body of research showing that Indigenous self-determination, land stewardship, and cultural knowledge and practices are proven climate solutions. The report, released today, offers dozens of examples. In Kenya, Indigenous Endorois and Tugen women cultivated drought-resistant varieties of sorghum, millet, and other key foods that provided some of the region’s only harvests in years with severe drought. In Brazil, Coordination of Indigenous Organizations of the Brazilian Amazon — the nation’s largest regional Indigenous network — helps organize fire management and response. It also provides training and mobilizes response teams. 


The report is based on detailed case studies and more than 200 survey responses from 46 countries spanning six ecosystems: forests, mountains, drylands, freshwater systems, grasslands, and coastal. Castañeda Quintana said a broad global study was essential to show climate change and environmental disasters are not limited by national or even ecological boundaries, and responses to them must transcend borders. It also is essential to recognize that disasters do not arrive one at a time. More than 80 percent of survey respondents said that

they face two or more at once

, and over 90 percent reported rising frequency. 


For example, in 2019, the Kichwa People of Sarayaku in the Ecuadorian Amazon faced devastating floods along the Bobonaza River, destroying crops and homes. Daniel Santi, who is the president of the community, which numbers roughly 1,600 and inhabits more than 500 square miles, said that his people were able to respond effectively because of their strong governance structures that were already in place. In other words, self-determination and governance allowed them to decide how best to prepare for, and respond to, a crisis. “This organization makes it possible to confront any problem and any threat,” Santi said. 


The report argues that the combination of Indigenous governance and knowledge is what makes these adaptation strategies so effective. Knowledge rooted in the land can be put into action immediately. Sarayaku elders, for example, noticed rain and lightning patterns at the river’s headwaters that signaled possible flooding and were then able to warn the community. Sarayaku structure includes clear decision-making processes, mechanisms to address the most urgent needs like housing for families with destroyed homes, and dedicated representatives to communicate status updates and needs with external authorities. According to Santi, these responses are guided by

minga

, a Kichwa term for solidarity and collective responsibility. 


But many countries do not legally recognize Indigenous peoples or their governments,

refuse to use Indigenous languages

 for emergency alerts, and continue to criminalize Indigenous culture. Those conditions can weaken the impact of Indigenous knowledge and governance. 


Read Next


As climate change threatens their lands, Indigenous nations demand more power at the UN


Dionne Phillips


Santi believes Indigenous peoples have a lot …

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Pro-Palestine Activist ‘Close to Death’ on Hunger Strike in Tunisian Prison
content:
The leader of the Global Sumud Flotilla is in a semi-comatose condition and close to death as he enters the 39th day of his hunger strike inside Tunisia’s Mornaguia Prison, the organisation has confirmed to Novara Media.


Wael Naouar, a father of two who was detained in March alongside three other Flotilla organisers, Ghassan Henchiri, Ghassan Boughdiri and Nabil Chennoufi, initiated his hunger strike in protest of the prolonged detention the Sumud 4 have endured without trial. 


In a press release shared on Tuesday, the Global Sumud Flotilla said Naouar is facing organ failure, and experiencing hallucinations and severe heart, chest and stomach pain. He is described as barely able to see or hear, and “wishes to lose consciousness only to escape the agony”.


After a visit to his son this week, Naouar’s father said: “Wael is on the brink of death.”


Henchiri, Boughdiri and Chennoufi also began their hunger strikes a little over two weeks ago. The Flotilla described Henchiri as “bedridden, in severe pain and denied basic medical care”.


The activists were initially arrested over allegations of financial violations in March. This triggered an investigation into each of the men, and they have remained imprisoned by Tunisian authorities while they await trial. 


A trial date has yet to be set, and their pre-trial detention was

extended by four months

on 11 September. 


Hundreds of protestors took to the streets in Tunis this weekend demanding freedom for the Sumud 4. 

Around

15 people were reportedly arrested

 after the march, a move condemned by two Tunisian political parties and the Tunisian League for Human Rights which called for the immediate release of those detained. 


The Global Sumud Flotilla slammed the Tunisian government for holding the Sumud 4 on “fabricated financial charges designed to criminalise their solidarity” with “no credible evidence” and said it holds state authorities fully responsible for their fate. 


It is calling for the activists’ immediate release, all charges against them to be dropped, emergency hospital care for the hunger strikers, and the release of “every activist detained for standing with them”. 


During their six months incarcerated, the Sumud 4 have endured brutal prison conditions including extreme heat, water shortages and a denial of healthcare, according to the Flotilla.

author: Redazione_web
title: Corri viva, corri veloce!
content:
Lucia Sanchez Saornil è stata una compagna anarchica spagnola attiva tra gli anni 20 e la fine degli anni 30 del Novecento. Operaia del settore telefonico, anarco sindacalista, anarco femminista, lesbica, segretaria di redazione della CNT, cofondatrice della rivista Mujeres Libres, attiva nella rivoluzione antifranchista, Lucia è stata molte cose, anche e soprattutto artista e poeta.


Quello che segue è un suo testo poetico dedicato all’assassinio della giovane Maria Silva Cruz. Nel 1933 alcuni braccianti del villaggio andaluso di Casas Viejas affiliati alla CNT insorsero, proclamando il comunismo libertario, e contro di loro si scatenò la repressione della Guardia Civil, che massacrò 26 persone del villaggio. Alcuni si rifugiarono nell’abitazione dell’anarchico Cruz Seisdedos e la Guardia Civil dette fuoco alla casa uccidendo le 10 persone che si trovavano all’interno. Solo Maria Silva, la nipote sedicenne di Seisdedos, riuscì a scappare e successivamente partecipò alle giornate del luglio del ‘36 a Madrid. In seguito fu arrestata dai franchisti e assassinata in un luogo imprecisato fra Medina e Jerez.


Patrizia Nesti


ROMANCE DE “LA LIBERTARIA”


María Silva por nombre


ya era un romance certero.


María Silva traía


los grandes ojos ardiendo,


muda su lengua andaluza,


pálido el rostro moreno


y un espasmo de terror


por las entrañas adentro.


Estampa de noche trágica.


Benalup, en su recuerdo


raía como una lima


la carne de su cerebro;


cerebro de niña pobre,


sin pan, sin libro y sin credo.


En una disputa trágica


gritan la llama y el viento;


rayan la noche fusiles


con resplandores siniestros


buscando al hombre en el monte


como el lobo carnicero.


Dieciséis años tenía


María Silva incompletos.


¡Ay, María Silva Cruz,


nieta del bravo “Seisdedos”,…


tus piernas de corza joven


hacen competencia al viento!


¡Corre hacia los negros campos;


corre viva, corre presto;


salva tus dieciséis años,


tu vida en flor, que aún es tiempo!


Salta las tapias enanas,


busca refugio en los cerros;


chacales con voz humana


siguen tu rastro sangriento.


¡Corre, María Silva, corre!


Y el sol la alumbró corriendo


por caminos de Jerez,


duros de noche y de invierno.


¡A la zaga iba el destino


como una fiera al acecho!


En cárceles tenebrosas


–Cádiz, Sevilla– murieron


como dieciséis jazmines


dieciséis años parleros.


Alguaciles y escribanos


–jeta asquerosa de puercos–


olisqueaban tu carne


y tu pobreza, sabiendo


que el hambre es la celestina


mejor de sus trapicheos.


¡Pecado tus ojos grandes,


aún abrasados de incendio,


tu dulce lengua andaluza,


tu labio tímido y fresco!


¡Pecado con que soñaban


sus apetitos sin freno!


Un incentivo, tu llanto,


mejor que un dique a su sueño


Y la flor de tu inocencia,


aguijón de su deseo.


Fuera botín descontado


tu carne, carne del pueblo,


si en la sombra no velaran


como dos puntas de acero


–carne de tu misma carne–


un afán con ojos negros.


Quebró el destino su vara


y te miró con respeto.


¡Ay, María Silva Cruz,


(“Libertaria”, por tu abuelo),


qué poco dura la dicha!


¡qué poco dura!, ¡ay! El tiempo


mide con varas distintas


una alegría y un duelo.


Apenas tuviste un dulce


collar de brazos morenos,


roncos cañones tronaron


sus tempestades de hierro;


Atila picó de espuelas


su raudo potro siniestro;


sobre los campos de España


la sal del odio vertieron,


porque no dieran más pan


que el pan de su privilegio.


Se desbordaron de sangre


el Guadalquivir y el Ebro;


torrentes rojos teñían


montes, collados y oteros;


y a la luna subió el grito


de guerra del pueblo ibero.


–¡A las armas!, camaradas,


¡a las armas!, que los perros


han quebrado sus carlancas.


¡A las armas! ¡Rompan fuego!


Lucha cruel han trabado


la aristocracia y el pueblo


y en un revuelto amasijo


de carnes rotas y nervios,


rugen por tierras de España


cada uno de sus fueros.


–¡Camaradas, a las armas!


¡El grito deshizo el cerco


adorable de los brazos


y quebró desnudo el cuello!


Sola, no, que ya reclinas


un sueño de oro en tu pecho;


aún tienes una sonrisa


que devuelve tu reflejo.


¡”Libertaria”, has de ser fuerte!


María Silva, ¡de hierro!


Pedazos de tus entrañas


necesitan tu alientos.


Látigos hienden la noche.


–Corazón mío, es el viento…


Y María Silva canta:


–“Duerme…, nanita…, arrapiezo.”


Puños de gigante baten


la puerta del aposento


y la noche entra de pronto …

author: David Swanson
title: Quiz: Are You a Foreign Policy and History Genius?
content:
Culture of Peace, North America, World

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, September 23, 2026

1. The grandfather of the current leader of North Korea, the guy who ruled over North Korea from 1945 to 1994, was more of a Presbyterian than a Communist. Kim Il Sung was raised in a Christian community created by U.S. missionaries, was a Sunday School teacher and church organist, and leader of a Christian youth group. Kim Il Sung did not turn against Christianity so much as choose to himself play the role of Jesus in the story. He changed his name to take the name of a mythical messiah figure (Kim Il Sung), beating out Sun Myung Moon who had the same idea. Kim Il Sung encouraged beliefs in his supernatural powers. He was said to have performed miracles, to have known more as a child than the scholars, to heal with the touch of his hands, and to be especially fond of fishermen. He set aside a Sabbath-like day for worshipping him and learning his words as gospel. One could not take his name in vain or mistreat any image of him. Christian-like hymns praised his glory. Instead of 10 commandments, there were now 10 principles which included effectively that one would have no other gods besides Kim Il Sung. His mother became a Marylike figure. And, like at least one Trump staffer, some of Kim Il Sung’s family was said to have the power to teleport.

2. The nation far and away most often referred to as the richest country in the world, the United States, is not, and for a very long time has not been, and for the foreseeable future will not be the richest country in the world.

3. It was March 23, 1775, and a wealthy, white man who owned many people as slaves was giving a speech in a church in Richmond, Virginia. What he said was not recorded, but we know that he spoke critically of rule by England. An account just the next week by a man who had attended the speech tells us that the speaker called King George III, “a Tyrant, a fool, a puppet, and a tool.” This orator may have merely hinted at revolution, as on other occasions, or he may have openly advocated it. He also probably spoke on this day, as he did on others before and after, of the need to militarily suppress slave revolts and to resist any British efforts to free people from slavery, as well as of the need to attack Native Americans to the west, where this man was making a fortune on land speculation. Forty-two years later, a supposed text of the speech was published, having been concocted from decades-old memories solicited second-hand and probably some sheer invention. The original speaker had long since died. But now we learned that he had spoken against a metaphorical enslavement to England, and possibly even acted out liberating himself from invisible bondage. Words put into his mouth included these: “I know not what course others may take; but as for me, give me liberty, or give me death.” He, Patrick Henry, may or may not have actually said that, but there is no record of Patrick Henry subsequently risking death; he saw no combat action. He did, however, campaign against ratification of the U.S. Constitution. His rallying cry popularizing a war theretofore desired mostly by elites, is sufficient, however, to rank him as a heroic Founding Father of the United States of America. It is reported that in 1800 an enslaved man in Virginia named Gabriel, leading Gabriel’s Rebellion, at least planned to create a banner reading “death or liberty.” This is widely described as a reference to Patrick Henry’s speech even though it reverses the phrase, happened long before the speech was published, and involved someone actually in need of liberty and actually risking death. Gabriel has not been made into a founding father, but was hung by the neck.

4. Weeks before the first nuclear bomb was dropped on Japan, on July 13, 1945, Japan had sent a telegram to the Soviet Union expressing its desire to surrender and end the war. The United States had broken Japan’s codes and read the telegram. President Truman referred in his diary to “the telegram from Jap Emperor asking for peace.” Truman had already been informed through Swiss and Portuguese channels of Japanese peace overtures as early as three months before Hiroshima. Japan objected only to surrendering unconditionally and giving up its emperor, but the United States insisted on those terms until after the bombs had been dropped, at which point it allowed Japan to keep its emperor. title: "Secretary of Measlesland": Dr. Paul Offit Slams RFK Jr.'s Handling of Deadly Measles Outbreak
content:
2026 is already the deadliest year for measles in the United States since the virus was declared eliminated in 2000. Four people died over the last month in Pennsylvania amid an ongoing outbreak in the state, which had not seen a measles-related death in at least 35 years. All four victims, including two infants, were unvaccinated (children do not receive their first dose of the measles vaccine until they have reached a year old). The deaths come as President Trump and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. continue to defund public vaccination programs and push debunked claims that vaccines cause autism.


Pediatrician and vaccine expert Dr. Paul Offit warns that the four reported measles deaths — which were reported by Pennsylvania health officials but have not yet been acknowledged by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — are likely a vast undercount. He estimates that there could be “closer to 4,000” cases in the Pennsylvania outbreak. “I don’t think people realize how contagious this virus is,” Offit says. “You don’t have to have direct contact with somebody who has measles. You just have to be within their airspace within two hours of them being there.”


We also speak to Offit about the

COVID

-19 virus, which he says is now affecting the United States “like flu” by causing “hundreds of thousands of people to be hospitalized and tens of thousands to die, just like influenza does, every year.” Yearly flu and

COVID

-19 vaccinations, he explains, are “effective at keeping people out of the hospital, effective at keeping them out of the intensive care unit, and effective at keeping them out of the morgue.”

title: Kurdish writer Suzan Samancı detained upon entering Turkey, placed under a travel ban
content:
Kurdish writer Suzan Samancı was detained on Tuesday at Istanbul Airport while entering Turkey. The author, who has been living in Switzerland for 18 years, is under investigation on allegations of “propaganda for a terrorist organization.” Following her statement, she was released under judicial supervision and placed under a travel ban.


Her detention was made public by lawyer and human rights activist Eren Keskin. “Kurdish writer Suzan Samancı, who has been living in Switzerland for 18 years, returned to Turkey today. She was detained at Istanbul Airport on allegations of ‘propaganda for an organization,’” Keskin stated.


After her questioning was completed, Samancı was first referred to the prosecutor’s office and then brought before a judge. Via videoconference, the 64-year-old writer was connected to the competent court in Amed (Diyarbakır). The court imposed a travel ban as a judicial control measure and ordered Samancı’s release.


From Turkish-language literature to writing in Kurdish


Suzan Samancı is from Amed and has been part of the Kurdish literary scene for decades. She began her literary career with poetry before turning primarily to short stories and novels. She also wrote for newspapers including Demokrasi, Gündem, and Özgür Politika. She is a member of the writers’ association PEN.


Her well-known works include the short story collections

Eriyip Gidiyor Gece, Reçine Kokuyordu Helin, Kıraç Dağlar Kar Tuttu,

 and

Suskunun Gölgesinde

. In 1997, she received second prize in the Orhan Kemal Short Story Competition for

Kıraç Dağlar Kar Tuttu

. Her works have been translated into several languages.


After initially writing in Turkish, Samancı published

Ew Jin û Mêrê Bi Maske

 in 2015, her first short story collection written in her native Kurdish. In 2019, she published

Mirzayê Reben

, her first Kurdish-language novel. Most recently, in 2024, she published

Payiz an jî Ziyab

, another novel written in Kurdish.

title: "New Low in U.N. History": Trita Parsi on Trump's Threat to Annihilate Iran at General Assembly
content: The annual meeting of the United Nations General Assembly opened this week in New York City. On its opening day, President Trump in his address to all 193 U.N. member states threatened to annihilate Iran. “This is probably a new low in U.N. history,” says Trita Parsi of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, joining us in our New York City studio ahead of the second day of the General Assembly. As Trump pushes for even more sanctions on Iran, “what you’re most likely to see in that scenario is that the Iranians will counter-escalate” in what threatens to become an “endless war.” Parsi also comments on the U.S. military’s growing reliance on artificial intelligence for strategic and targeting decisions, Trump’s upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and the Trump administration’s flouting of international law.

title: Mansur Yavaş’ın ardından CHP’de iki istifa daha: Beypazarı ve Kalecik belediye başkanları partiden ayrıldı
content:
Beypazarı Belediye Başkanı Özer Kasap | Kalecik Belediye Başkanı Satılmış Karakoç

Ankara Büyükşehir Belediye (ABB) Başkanı Mansur Yavaş’ın CHP üyeliğinden istifa ederek siyasi yoluna bağımsız olarak devam edeceğini açıklamasının ardından iki ilçe belediye başkanı daha CHP’den ayrıldı.

Beypazarı Belediye Başkanı Özer Kasap ve Kalecik Belediye Başkanı Satılmış Karakoç, sosyal medya hesaplarından yaptıkları açıklamalarla CHP üyeliğinden istifa ettiklerini ve belediye başkanlığı görevlerini bağımsız olarak sürdüreceklerini bildirdi.

Kalecik Belediye Başkanı Satılmış Karakoç, CHP üyeliğinden ayrılarak görevini bağımsız sürdüreceğini açıkladı.

Karakoç, “İçinden geçtiğimiz süreç ve yaşanan gelişmeler doğrultusunda, Cumhuriyet Halk Partisi üyeliğimden ayrılarak Belediye Başkanlığı görevime bağımsız olarak devam etme kararı aldım” dedi.

Mansur Yavaş’la birlikte hareket etmeyi sürdüreceğini belirten Karakoç, “Mansur Yavaş Başkanımızla çıktığımız yolun temelinde de aynı anlayış vardı: İnsanları siyasi kimlikleriyle değil, insan oldukları için kucaklamak; ayrıştırmadan, adaletle ve halkın emanetine sahip çıkarak hizmet etmek. Bugün de kendisiyle çıktığımız bu yolda, Mansur Başkanımızın yanında yürümeye devam edeceğim” ifadelerini kullandı.

Beypazarı Belediye Başkanı Özer Kasap da sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamayla CHP’den ayrıldığını bildirdi.

Kasap, “Bugün geldiğimiz noktada, Cumhuriyet Halk Partisi üyeliğimden ayrılıyor, siyasi yoluma bağımsız olarak devam etme kararı aldığımı kamuoyunun takdirine sunuyorum” dedi.

Mansur Yavaş’la birlikte çıktıkları yola vurgu yapan Kasap, “Mansur Yavaş Başkanımızla çıktığımız bu yolda, bana güvenen ve destek veren hemşehrilerime verdiğim sözlerin arkasındayım” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Pasture bans: Rural decline and a new wave of forced migration
content:
Security-driven policies pursued for decades in Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) are gradually dismantling livestock farming, the main source of livelihood for the rural population. Restrictions on access to pastures on military grounds, the designation of grazing areas as “special security zones” and measures preventing villagers from taking their animals into the mountains and highland pastures are effectively bringing an end to a way of life that has sustained the people of Kurdistan for thousands of years. This is not accidental, but the result of a deliberate, systematic and political choice.


Small and large livestock farming, the backbone of the rural economy in Kurdistan, has come under an increasingly restrictive regime in recent years. Villagers can no longer freely take their animals to highland pastures. Even where access is permitted, they face narrow corridors imposed on security grounds, constant identity checks and arbitrary entry bans. These restrictions have gone far beyond a question of access. They amount to a deliberate severing of the ties between local people, their land and their economic autonomy.


Highland pasture bans are often imposed without any specific justification, in the middle of the grazing season and without prior notice. For a farmer, even a few weeks without access to pasture can mean losing an entire year’s livestock. Villagers are therefore forced either to sell their animals early at a loss or to abandon livestock farming altogether.


Highland pastures closed on ‘security’ grounds


The roots of today’s pasture and highland bans can be traced back to the village evacuations and state of emergency measures of the 1990s. Thousands of villages and hamlets were evacuated by state forces during that period, uprooting people from their land. The same logic now continues in a more “civilian” form. Villages are no longer being evacuated, but the pastures on which villagers depend for their livelihoods are effectively being made inaccessible. The outcome is the same: people are separated from their land and grazing grounds, reshaping the region’s demographic and economic structure.


Preferential access to some pastures for village guards, while villagers without ties to the state are excluded, further deepens inequality in the region. Pastureland thus ceases to function as a shared natural resource and becomes a privilege distributed on the basis of loyalty and obedience.


Signs of a collapsing economy


Regional chambers of agriculture and professional organisations have repeatedly said in statements to the press that livestock numbers have fallen sharply across the region over the past two decades, with livestock farming almost disappearing in many villages. Villages once known for their herds have become settlements where only an ageing population remains and agricultural production has largely ceased. Younger generations no longer see staying in their villages as a viable option because they have little opportunity to continue their families’ livelihoods.


The collapse of livestock farming means more than a loss of income. It also threatens the disappearance of centuries of knowledge and a deeply rooted way of life. Seasonal migration to highland pastures, herd management and traditions of communal use formed a system of social organisation passed down from one generation to the next. This way of life has rapidly eroded as access to pastures has effectively been eliminated.


A new route of migration from the highlands to the cities


Migration is becoming the only option for rural families who have lost their livelihoods. Unlike the forced mass evacuations of the 1990s, this process may appear more “voluntary”, but it is no less imposed by circumstances. Families are moving to the outskirts of cities such as Diyarbakır (Amed), Van (Wan), Urfa (Riha) and Mardin (Mêrdîn), or to major cities outside Northern Kurdistan, where they often struggle to survive through insecure, low-paid and seasonal work.


This wave of migration is creating new pockets of poverty and marginalisation in urban centres. Families who were producers in the countryside become a source of cheap labour in the cities, while the autonomous relationship they once had with their land, livestock and natural environment is replaced by a precarious struggle for survival in impoverished urban neighbourhoods. The process goes beyond individual impoverishment and amounts to a broader social uprooting.

title: Suspected death in Eskişehir prison
content:
According to information provided by Çiçek’s family, Şiyar Çiçek, who was being held in Eskişehir Prison, died under suspicious circumstances. Çiçek had been in prison since 2014, and had been held in Eskişehir Prison for approximately two years. He was allegedly kept in a cell for the past 10 days.


According to a report published by Ajansa Welat, Çiçek’s family said that his health was good and that he only had diabetes. Çiçek’s father, Menduh Çiçek, said that his son had died in prison, and added: “On Monday they called us and said ‘Your son is sick, we are taking him to the hospital.’ My son only had diabetes, he was in very good condition, but he died.”


We don't know what happened to my son


Çiçek's father said that he had seen his son’s body and found no signs of torture, but that they had suspicions about the cause of death. He added: “We think they poisoned my son or did something else to him.”


Çiçek said that his son had spoken to his mother by phone about a week before his death and told her that he had been placed in a cell. He continued: “My son had been in a cell for 10 days. If he had been in the ward, we could have found out what happened. But because he was in a cell, we don’t know what happened to him.”


Çiçek said that his son had wanted to go to the hospital with his brother but was not allowed to do so, and added: “They had blindfolded my son. The prosecutor’s office knew that my son had died. But they did this to shift the responsibility onto the hospital. They recorded my son’s death as having occurred at the hospital, whereas he died in prison.”

title: Öztürk: Commission should not limit Öcalan’s role
content:
The Monitoring and Evaluation Board, established in line with the framework law adopted by Parliament as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, formed four subcommissions following its first meeting on 24 August. The inclusion of Abdullah Öcalan in one of these bodies, the “Disarmament and Strategic Coordination Subcommission,” has brought his role in advancing the process to the fore.


Öcalan’s involvement in the commission’s work is regarded as a critical step towards a democratic solution to the Kurdish question and the establishment of lasting peace.


Raziye Öztürk, a lawyer from the Asrın Law Office, spoke to ANF about the current stage of the process and Öcalan’s status.


Mr. Öcalan’s direct participation is valuable


Raziye Öztürk described the establishment of commissions within Parliament as an important threshold at the current stage and said the way should be opened for Mr. Öcalan to participate in the process directly and officially.


Öztürk said: “Undoubtedly, the establishment of commissions within Parliament and the institutional character this gives to the process can be regarded as an important threshold at the stage we have reached. At the same time, we consider every step that enables Mr. Öcalan to participate in the process directly and officially and to effectively fulfil his role to be valuable for advancing the process.


Unfortunately, however, the very name ‘Disarmament and Strategic Coordination Subcommission’ draws a framework that restricts both the commission’s scope of work and Mr. Öcalan’s role. Unfortunately, developments to date have also confirmed this assessment.


The process began with statements and assessments drawing attention to the historical nature of Kurdish-Turkish relations, the partnership in the founding of the Republic and the damage caused to society by many years of conflict. From the outset, there was, of course, an approach that reduced the Kurdish question solely to disarmament and insisted on this. Nevertheless, it could be said that a broader perspective addressing the issue in its historical, political and social dimensions prevailed in the process.”


Security-centred approach has not produced a solution


Raziye Öztürk said the Kurdish question has repeatedly been addressed through security-centred policies in the past and that this approach has failed to produce a lasting solution.


Öztürk also said: “This is precisely why we believe there should be no return to the security-centred approach that has been tried repeatedly in the past. As we have seen with the approach that defines the Kurdish question solely under the heading of ‘terrorism’ and seeks to resolve it through unilateral security policies, this understanding has not produced a solution to date. It is clear that an approach focused solely on ‘disarmament’ will lead to the same outcome.


The mechanisms established today must therefore avoid reproducing the same approach and instead make it possible to address the issue in all its dimensions and develop solutions on the basis of democratic politics. What is decisive here is the approach with which the commission will work and the task it sets itself.”


Disarmament is not the process itself


Öztürk said disarmament is one of the important stages of the process but should not be seen as the process in its entirety, adding that the transition from armed conflict to democratic politics also involves political, social and legal transformations.


Öztürk continued: “We do not disregard the fact that disarmament is one of the important stages of this process. But disarmament is not the process itself; it is one stage in the transition from armed conflict to democratic politics and a lasting solution. What is at stake, therefore, is not merely coordinating the removal of weapons from the equation, but how to achieve the political, social and legal transformation this requires. Mr. Öcalan is the key actor who has defined the strategy and method for precisely this transformation.


The perspective he has put forward has a broader framework that is based not only on ending armed conflict, but also on strengthening democratic politics, resolving the issue on political and legal grounds, and building social peace.


Mr. Öcalan’s direct participation in the process will therefore ensure that this perspective is also reflected in the negotiations and the mechanisms that have been established. There is no doubt that such participation would …

title: Alparslan: Ministry’s decision to separate Zazaki from Kurdish aims to create division
content:
The 2026–2027 academic year began on 14 September. One week before the start of the new school year, the Ministry of National Education (MEB) introduced a separate curriculum for Zazaki (Kirmanckî), which it had previously treated alongside Kurmancî as a dialect of Kurdish.


The new programme, prepared under the “Century of Turkey Education Model”, places Zazaki within the education system as a separate curriculum. It was also decided that Zazaki textbooks would be revised and that the field would be designated as a separate branch for teacher appointments.


As the first week of the new academic year came to an end, Istanbul Kurdish Institute Co-Chair Remziye Alparslan spoke to ANF about the impact of mother-tongue education on children’s development and the Ministry’s decision to treat Zazaki as a subject separate from Kurdish.


Alparslan said mother-tongue education is important not only for the individual development of children beginning their education, but also for preserving cultural identity. 


Alparslan said: “Education in the mother tongue is extremely important for children to begin school in the language that shapes their identity, culture and roots, without becoming alienated from themselves or disconnected from their families and roots, and with a sense of self-confidence. It is equally vital for the transmission, preservation and development of the mother tongue and, consequently of Kurdish culture and identity. Educational scientists and pedagogues are better placed to assess its impact on children’s education. However, education in the mother tongue is crucial so that children raised in their mother tongue do not suddenly find themselves in an unfamiliar environment, can acquire other languages with greater ease, feel that they are a natural part of the society around them, and grow into confident, multilingual and multicultural individuals without being subjected to discrimination or exclusion.”


Mother-tongue education is a democratic demand of all peoples


Remziye Alparslan said the right to education in the mother tongue is a democratic demand shared by all peoples who form part of society and drew attention to the history of the struggle. 


Alparslan also said: “The demand for mother-tongue education, which has come to the fore through the struggle of the Kurdish people, is fundamentally a longstanding democratic demand that seeks to include all peoples and cultures rather than exclude them on the basis of belonging, identity or difference. This struggle has been waged in many different ways over the years, through petitions, boycotts, marches and press statements. For years, there have been demands to remove the barriers to mother-tongue education and, in the case of Kurds, to education in Kurdish, and for Kurdish to be used at every level of education, from preschool to university.”


Policies based on denial must be abandoned


Alparslan said policies based on the denial of mother tongues are not sustainable if societies are to live together freely, voluntarily and in peace.


Alparslan contunied: “Kurds have rights arising from their existence as a people. Regardless of the official language of the country in which they live, they have the right to preserve and develop their own culture, language and existence as a people. As in other contemporary countries, there is no reason for this to be obstructed. There are dozens of examples around the world and in Europe. Turkey must therefore find the courage to break free from this cycle of suppression, denial and disregard, and recognise that doing so is a prerequisite for all communities to live together freely, voluntarily and in peace. The current situation is no longer sustainable and will inevitably encounter the same familiar problems again. As long as the Kurdish people exist, they will continue their struggle for their mother tongue, culture and rights, and sooner or later they will achieve them.”


Criticism of Ministry’s Zazaki decision: ‘The timing is no coincidence’


Alparslan said the timing of the Ministry of National Education’s decision in the first week of September to separate Zazaki from Kurdish and introduce a separate curriculum appeared to have been deliberately chosen to provoke controversy. She stated that Kurdish was being deliberately reduced to one of its varieties, Kurmancî.


Alparslan said: “I believe that the attempt to create a dichotomy between Kurdish and Zazaki, to equate Kurmancî with Kurdish and then …

title: Mobilisation for the Kurdish language
content:
The demand for mother-tongue education has long been one of the central issues in discussions surrounding the Kurdish question and democratisation in Turkey. As the Peace and Democratic Society Process is being debated, the right to mother-tongue education and official status for Kurdish are seen not only as matters of education policy but also as fundamental conditions for social peace.


Heval Dilbahar, Co-Spokesperson of the Language, Culture and Arts Commission of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), said Kurdish-language education from preschool to university is possible and that, if the state demonstrates the necessary political will, existing shortcomings could be addressed within two to three years and Kurdish-language education introduced in schools.


In a report by Lütfi Pala of Mezopotamya Agency, Dilbahar said the republic was founded on a monist understanding: “A century ago, the Republic was established on a monist understanding. As a result, many languages, particularly Kurdish, were banned. The Kurdish language was subjected to severe pressure, coercion and restrictions. However, as a result of the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom, policies of denial, assimilation, prohibition and eradication were broken. In other words, it is no longer possible to deny or completely eradicate the Kurdish language through conventional methods.”


Kurdish remains under siege


Dilbahar said it would be wrong to assume that the pressure and restrictions imposed on Kurdish have been substantially lifted in recent years, stressing that the language remains under siege. Dilbahar also said: “Kurdish is still under siege and remains restricted in many areas. Kurdish still has no official or legal status, while its exclusion from the constitution and official institutions continues. In practice, pressure, obstruction and restrictions continue against many institutions, organisations and groups working on the Kurdish language. The aim is to gradually erode the Kurdish language under these conditions and distance it from society. Consider that today there are thousands of schools providing education in Turkish across Northern Kurdistan (Bakur), yet there is not a single school providing education entirely in Kurdish. Kurdish-language education remains prohibited. There is no right to education in Kurdish from primary school through university. Turkish-language schools and institutions are being opened in cities, districts, neighbourhoods, streets, villages and even hamlets, with the aim of extending and entrenching the dominance of Turkish throughout Kurdistan. Although the Kurdish people are struggling to protect, develop and expand the use of their language, under these conditions the existing efforts are unfortunately insufficient.”


Why should it not be possible?


Asked whether Kurdish-language education from preschool to university is possible and how it could be implemented, Dilbahar replied: “Education is provided in more than one language in many countries around the world. Multilingual education models are implemented from primary school through university in countries such as Switzerland and Sweden. If this is possible in those countries, why should it not be possible in Northern Kurdistan and Turkey? If the state demonstrates the necessary will and intent, the infrastructure for Kurdish-language education could easily be established within two to three years. It is not accurate to claim that this is technically impossible or that the necessary resources do not exist. What matters is establishing the political will and recognising that the Kurdish people have the right to receive education in Kurdish.”


Legal barriers must be removed


Dilbahar added that, in keeping with the spirit of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the state must remove the legal barriers facing the Kurdish language. Dilbahar said:  “The constitution must guarantee freedoms for both Kurdish and all other languages, and Kurdish must be granted a recognised status. The form this status takes can be discussed, but Kurdish, the language of millions of Kurds, must have official status. Kurdish must become a language of education if it is to preserve itself and be carried into the future. All place names and terms that were originally Kurdish and later Turkified must also be restored to Kurdish. title: The red star of Istanbul: Egîd Tolhildan
content:
Throughout history, some cities have been remembered not only as geographical centres but also as symbolic places of resistance and social struggle. Stretching from Havana and Stalingrad to Chiapas and Kobanê, these cities have carved out a distinctive place in the history of peoples’ struggles.


Cities also hold a special place in the history of the Kurdish Freedom Movement in terms of resistance. Some have stood out for mass serhildans, or uprisings, while others have become known for the revolutionaries they nurtured and who took part in the struggle. Istanbul is one of the cities that embodies both.


 


Istanbul has witnessed decades of mass demonstrations and resistance throughout the history of the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Newroz uprisings, university protests, demonstrations against the international conspiracy, resistance in solidarity with Kobanê and Rojava, and actions carried out by the Patriotic Revolutionary Youth Movement (YDG-H), which was active between 2013 and 2016, marked important moments in this history.


Istanbul’s significance for the Kurdish Freedom Movement has not been limited to mass mobilisation. The city has also become associated with the many revolutionaries who joined the ranks of the movement. Around 120 of those included in a list of martyrs recently announced by the People’s Defence Forces (HPG) were revolutionaries who had joined the struggle from Istanbul.


One of them was Egîd Tolhildan (Yoldaş Anık).


A child who grew up amid resistance


Egîd turned towards resistance from an early age. Born into a poor family, he grew up against the backdrop of the 1990s, a period remembered in Kurdish history for major resistance and massacres. His family moved to Istanbul at a time when villages were being burned and forced displacement was intensifying across Kurdistan. Egîd grew up in a poor neighbourhood of Istanbul, where he developed a strong sense of Kurdish patriotism.


Egîd worked to help support his family while also fulfilling what he saw as his patriotic responsibilities, taking part in resistance against the repression and massacres faced by his people. He neither abandoned his family nor stayed away from the resistance.


Egîd became involved in youth organising in Istanbul at a time when attacks described by the Kurdish movement as genocidal were intensifying in Kurdistan and attacks on Rojava were escalating. He took part in resistance against these attacks in both Rojava and Northern Kurdistan (Bakur). As the Self-Government Resistance unfolded and attacks involving massacres intensified in Rojava, Egîd turned towards the mountains.


Resistance was in his very nature


As we make our way to Egîd’s home, we enter the neighbourhood that took shape in the 1990s and still retains its Kurdish and patriotic identity. We soon realise how many people in the neighbourhood knew Egîd when we tell them we are looking for his home. Everyone we speak to says resistance was in his very nature.


H

e was detained, but once released, he would not stop


Egîd began struggling to make a living at a young age, but always placed the party and the guerrillas at the centre of his life. He worked for a time as a shoe shiner before finding a job in a textile workshop. His mother, Suphiye, recounts what followed: “From what I could see, he was not doing much at first. He was going to school. He used to feel embarrassed when I came to the school wearing my headscarf and would say, ‘Don’t come to me.’ We built houses for his cousins, and later we moved here. We built our own home in Karayolları. My children would go out to shine shoes and come back, and with what they earned we would make food for ourselves. Yoldaş loved the struggle; he was with the party. I would wake up in the evenings and see him sitting at the computer watching footage of the party. That was how he eventually joined the party.


He would go to demonstrations. The police raided our home every day. They would ask for Yoldaş; they wanted Yoldaş. I woke him up and told him, ‘My child, don’t be afraid. They will take your statement and release you, and you will come back home.’ Once he was released, his father brought him home. But he still would not stop; he kept going to demonstrations. I would tell him, ‘They will arrest you and they won’t let you go next time.’ He left after the Ankara massacre, and we never saw him again.”

title: Il tempo del riscatto
content:
da

Quarticciolo Ribelle


Con le nostre auto, ormai esenti da bollo, siamo obbligati a guardare un enorme schermo pubblicitario installato su viale Togliatti che mostra Meloni invitata al convegno di Gioventù Nazionale con lo slogan 

“

il 

𝘵𝘦𝘮𝘱𝘰 𝘥𝘦𝘭 𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘨𝘪𝘰

”.


Ci vuole molto coraggio, in effetti, a parlare alla Nazione raccontando di quanto è difficile fare il Presidente del Consiglio. Perché, dal canto nostro, ogni mattina cerchiamo il coraggio di abitare a Quarticciolo, a Rozzano, a Tor Sapienza e, come noi, in tutte quelle periferie del paese abbandonate da decenni.


Perché ci vuole coraggio a camminare per le strade avendo paura di essere aggrediti. Ci vuole coraggio a svegliarsi con le grida di chi è stato accoltellato o peggio gambizzato. Ci vuole coraggio ad andare a scuola tutte le mattine alla Verga o alla Pirotta. Ci vuole coraggio a vivere in case dove ti crolla il soffitto alla prima pioggia. Ci vuole coraggio a non abbandonarle e trasferirsi lontano. Ci vuole coraggio a decidere, nonostante tutto, di restare.


Ci vuole coraggio a crederci ogni giorno, che il cambiamento può avvenire. A non scoraggiarsi quando Del Mastro, un ministro della 𝘯𝘢𝘻𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘦, siede allo stesso tavolo con chi permette che i nostri quartieri siano il centro commerciale del disagio. Ci vuole coraggio a non credere che chiunque occupi le poltrone del Parlamento si dimentichi delle condizioni in cui siamo costretti a vivere.


Ci vuole coraggio a credere e ad affermare che in questo paese possa crescere 𝘶𝘯𝘢 𝘨𝘦𝘯𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘻𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘤𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘧𝘪𝘨𝘨𝘦 𝘭𝘢 𝘱𝘢𝘶𝘳𝘢 𝘥𝘦𝘭 𝘧𝘶𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘰. Il popolo, come ci chiama Meloni, non ha opportunità perché in questi luoghi non c’è niente se non quello che a fatica tentiamo di costruire.


Molti di questi quartieri sono stati commissariati dal dl Caivano bis e oggi, sono passati due interi anni, di quei 180 milioni di euro stanziati complessivamente in tutta Italia, non c’è niente di concreto.


Gli abitanti di Quarticciolo nel 2025 erano riusciti a fare approvare un piano periferie adatto ai bisogni di chi ci vive proprio perché siamo 𝘤𝘪𝘵𝘵𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘪 𝘭𝘪𝘣𝘦𝘳𝘪 𝘥𝘪 𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘵𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘦 𝘲𝘶𝘦𝘭𝘭𝘰 𝘤𝘩𝘦 è 𝘨𝘪𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘰

.


Le risorse stanziate serviranno, prima o poi, per rendere gli spazi abbandonati fruibili con servizi e attività economiche? Serviranno per rendere le nostre case più sicure? Serviranno per assegnare le centinaia di case vuote del nostro quartiere?


Ma mentre Meloni racconta del suo di coraggio, la sicurezza è un tema sempre più importante: aggressioni, rapine, pestaggi, incendi. Basta chiedere a chi abita a Rozzano se il DL emergenze ha migliorato la sicurezza.  Perché nessuno sta facendo niente con le risorse stanziate? E che nessuno dica che sono stati impediti interventi con la forza pubblica. Sono arrivati con i passamontagna, gli elicotteri, i blindati, hanno chiuso strade, perquisito scantinati, arrestato gente in mezzo alla strada. Nulla è cambiato.


Meloni, Presidente del Consiglio, è questo il coraggio di cui si sente orgogliosa?


Ci dispiace che ha bisogno di coraggio per fare il presidente, ma non è il nostro mestiere. Basterebbe dare seguito agli annunci che lei ha fatto, alle promesse della Regione Lazio, dell’Ater e del Comune di Roma.


Noi facciamo quello che possiamo ed è l’unica cosa che esiste: a 10 anni dall’occupazione della Palestra Popolare nasce un Campo da Calcio gestito dalla squadra popolare Borgata Gordiani. Tutto riqualificato con le risorse derivate dall’alleanza tra due quartieri.


Non è tanto, ma è un altro spazio di questo quartiere, tra Quarticciolo e Tor Sapienza, sottratto al degrado, presidiato da chi si allena, reso sicuro da chi lo attraversa.


Noi non abbiamo scelto di 𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘪𝘳𝘦 𝘮𝘢 𝘥𝘪 𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘦𝘯𝘦𝘳𝘦 ad un quartiere, di attraversare queste strade, di rischiare di sbagliare, di ricevere critiche e a volte sostegno. E questo richiede tanto coraggio. Il coraggio di tentare di sottrarre al tempo della politica il tempo del riscatto.

It’s an acronym, so expand on it, and see if you still make sense. “Assigned female at birth people” sounds dumb as hell, but “people who were assigned female at birth” sounds fine, so in acronym form it should be “people who were AMAB” and “people who were AFAB”

title: “La fine del genocidio è la fine del sionismo”. Appello per scendere in piazza per la Palestina il 10 ottobre
content:
Diffondiamo l’appello dei

Giovani Palestinesi d’Italia

 per una mobilitazione nazionale sui territori il 10 ottobre 2026.


Dopo tre anni di genocidio a Gaza, il popolo palestinese continua ad affrontare massacri, assedio, carestia e pulizia etnica, mentre in Cisgiordania si intensificano i raid militari e le violenze dei coloni.


Nonostante il calo dell’attenzione mediatica e le false pacificazioni, i crimini e l’oppressione non si sono fermati.


Il nostro dovere è riportare la centralità della lotta palestinese al centro del movimento politico e popolare in Italia.


La causa palestinese non può essere liquidata come mera emergenza umanitaria, è una lotta politica per la liberazione.


Il 10 ottobre scendiamo in piazza in tutte le città italiane per la fine immediata del genocidio, lo sblocco degli aiuti e il ritiro dell’esercito di occupazione.


Saremo in piazza al fianco di tutti i popoli della regione che resistono all’imperialismo e alle aggressioni sioniste – in Yemen, Libano, Siria, Iraq e Iran – e contro le politiche di guerra che devastano i territori e le popolazioni.


Esprimiamo inoltre piena solidarietà a chi, anche in Italia, subisce la repressione per essersi mobilitato al fianco del popolo palestinese e contro il genocidio.


LE NOSTRE ISTANZE


Stop alla guerra e all’economia di guerra:


Blocco immediato del riarmo, contro l’aumento della spesa militare e l’invio, vendita e transito di armi da e verso l’entità sionista. Rescissione di ogni accordo di cooperazione militare, economica e accademica.


Stop alla criminalizzazione del dissenso:


Ritiro immediato del “DDL Antisemitismo” (che usa la definizione IHRA per equiparare l’antisionismo all’antisemitismo e silenziare la critica politica) e contro i cosiddetti Decreti


“Sicurezza” e tutte le misure repressive contro il movimento di solidarietà.


Libertà per i prigionieri politici in Italia:


Liberazione immediata per Anan Yaeesh, Ahmed Salem, Mohammed Hannoun, Ra’ed Dawoud, Yaser Elasaly, Riyad Albustanji e Abdelnuti Abunada.


Per il diritto del popolo palestinese alla resistenza, in tutte le sue forme, per l’ottenimento del proprio legittimo diritto all’autodeterminazione, alla liberazione e al ritorno, in tutta la Palestina, dal fiume al mare.


Contro la complicità diretta dello Stato italiano, terzo esportatore al mondo di armi verso “Israele” e corresponsabile nel genocidio del popolo palestinese: chiediamo l’immediata cessazione di ogni accordo militare, economico, diplomatico e accademico con l’entita sionista, l’imposizione di sanzioni severe e un embargo totale sulle armi.


Contro le politiche di riarmo europeo e italiano che pretendono di destinare fino al 5% del PIL alle spese militari e all’industria bellica, a scapito dei diritti sociali, sottraendo risorse fondamentali a sanita, istruzione, lavoro e welfare.


VERSO UNA MOBILITAZIONE POPOLARE E DEI LAVORATORI


Invitiamo le comunità, i sindacati, le organizzazioni politiche, i collettivi e le strutture studentesche e dei lavoratori a mobilitarsi per costruire un embargo popolare e pratiche concrete di boicottaggio economico, accademico e militare, intrecciando la lotta contro il genocidio e la guerra con quella contro lo sfruttamento e l’attacco continuo a diritti sociali.


10 OTTOBRE 2026


Da Roma a Milano, da Napoli a Torino, da Bologna a Palermo e in tutte le piazze italiane: Partecipate alle manifestazioni. Alziamo la bandiera della Palestina.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Reserva Natural Laguna de Rocha: verde para los vecinos o negocios para la especulación inmobiliaria
content:
Por Noelia Leiva


A once kilómetros del Aeropuerto Internacional de Ezeiza y 33 del Obelisco porteño, la Reserva Natural Integral y Mixta Laguna de Rocha, en el distrito bonaerense de Esteban Echeverría, genera beneficios ecológicos y sociales propios de un espacio verde en una zona urbanizada: regula la temperatura, es una “esponja” natural frente a inundaciones y aloja a biodiversidad, como el 80 por ciento de las especies de aves de la provincia de Buenos Aires. Sin embargo, su extensión se redujo casi un tercio por una ley provincial. La organización

Colectivo Ecológico Unid@s por la Laguna de Rocha

 denuncia que la modificación obedece a intereses inmobiliarios y que afecta la calidad de vida de las personas del AMBA.


El

artículo 112 de la Ley 15.557

 (Presupuesto 2026), que definió el presupuesto, generó una marcha atrás en Laguna de Rocha que va en contra de las normas ambientales: recortó los metros cuadrados naturales protegidos en el territorio bonaerense y, como consecuencia, redujo el estado de protección del 30 por ciento de la reserva (390 hectáreas).


La decisión de la Legislatura bonaerense insta a adecuar la extensión de Rocha al “Mapa Oficial” de la reserva, lo que la organización socioambiental denuncia como inexistente. En definitiva, implica guiarse por la línea de ribera y excluir el humedal, clave para el funcionamiento ecológico del área.


La modificación, impulsada por el entonces diputado por la UCR Pablo Domenichini, fue aprobada por ambas Cámaras sin un debate específico sobre sus implicancias ambientales. "El artículo 112 fue votado exprés y no tiene nada que ver con la ley de presupuesto. Ignora la función del humedal porque preserva únicamente el espejo de agua y recorta el régimen de preservación. Achica el espacio para proyectos inmobiliarios, y eso es pernicioso sobre un lugar que ofrece efectos positivos totalmente gratuitos", explicó Gabriel Videla, integrante del Colectivo Ecológico Unid@s por la Laguna de Rocha, organización que lleva 18 años en lucha.


Para el Colectivo, la reforma buscaría otorgar valor inmobiliario a los propietarios privados con tierras que ahora estarían disponibles para uso comercial. Tierra Viva se contactó con el Ministerio de Ambiente bonaerense para consultar qué medidas tiene prevista la máxima autoridad en la materia frente a la situación, pero no obtuvo respuesta.


No es la primera vez que Rocha está en peligro. En 2013, la Ley 14.516 le quitó 64 hectáreas a lo establecido por la normativa bonaerense 14.488, que

en 2012 había creado la Reserva Natural Integral y Mixta

. Esa modificación sirvió para ceder terrenos a los clubes Racing y Boca, que planeaban construir polideportivos sobre el humedal. En 2015,

l

a Suprema Corte bonaerense invalidó esa cesión

 por afectar el mismo principio de no regresión ambiental que ahora está siendo vulnerado.


Foto: Colectivo Ecológico “Unid@s por Laguna de Rocha”


Mucha más que un pulmón verde


Rocha es el mayor humedal dentro del área metropolitana y sus beneficios ecológicos exceden el mapa de Esteban Echeverría.

Dentro de las 1.300 hectáreas protegidas se encuentran nueve ambientes distintos

, entre pastizales pampeanos, la zona lagunar, pantanos, talares, bosque nativo y bosque exótico, que sostienen una diversidad poco habitual para la región metropolitana, tras el avance de la industrialización y la urbanización.


"El Club de Observadores de Aves de Esteban Echeverría registró alrededor de 230 especies, el 80 por ciento de las que hay en la provincia", recalcó Juan Correa, también integrante del colectivo ambiental. "Es un gran hotel para aves, para abastecimiento y reposición. También, al ser un valle de inundación, es un regulador hídrico de toda la región", enfatizó. En épocas del

fenómeno climático de


El Niño

, mejora la calidad de vida de vecinas y vecinos de la zona.


El bosque de talares está compuesto por la única especie arbórea que regenera pastizales nativos, y toda la masa verde ayuda a mitigar las islas de calor urbanas, un fenómeno clave en el contexto del aumento global de la temperatura por la

crisis climática

. "En el sudeste del AMBA la laguna mitiga la temperatura, mientras en Capital Federal la masa de cemento eleva la sensación térmica hasta cinco grados", explicó Videla, que sumó un efecto que resuena en todas las viviendas del conurbano bonaerense: al bajar el consumo eléctrico en los días de mayor calor, alivia la demanda sobre Edesur y reduce la …

author: dialogocomospovos
title: Sementes Livres & Rebeldes no 4 Festival de Sementes Crioulas da Bahia
content:
Entre camponeses, guardiões e guardiãs da agrobiodiversidade, pesquisadores e movimentos populares aconteceu a testagem de contaminação transgênica das sementes no 4º Festival de Sementes Crioulas da Bahia, realizado pelo MPA no Assentamento Terra Nossa, em Ponto Novo.


O projeto Laboratório Móvel da UFRB levou até os agricultores a tecnologia para verificar se suas sementes estavam contaminadas por transgênicos. Foram testados 3 tipos de milho produzidos no Assentamento Terra Vista por Mestre Valmir e militantes da rede: milho crioulo vermelho, milho de pipoca azul e milho guarani branco.


A metodologia foi explicada durante o festival: pesam-se 180 gramas de milho para cada 200 ml de água. Depois, a mistura é triturada no liquidificador, o líquido sobrenadante é separado e deixado descansar para ser pipetado. Em seguida, colocam-se 5 ml em cada um dos quatro microtubos e adicionam-se as fitas com anticorpos que reconhecem a proteína transgênica. Quando aparece apenas uma fitinha, o teste indica que o milho está livre de transgênicos. E foi exatamente isso que aconteceu: o milho de Seu Valmir, o grande guardião e mestre de variedades, deu negativo para transgenia.


As amostras se mostraram livres de qualquer contaminação. A universidade reafirmou seu compromisso com os movimentos populares, colocando-se de portas abertas para doar fitas e receber milhos para testagem a cada safra, todos os anos.


Esse resultado é especialmente significativo diante da dificuldade de cultivar milho sem contaminação. A polinização cruzada do milho pode alcançar um raio de mais de 50 km, o que torna a preservação das variedades crioulas um verdadeiro ato de resistência. A equipe reforçou que a contaminação das sementes não é culpa dos agricultores, mas sim do ataque direto do capital e do latifúndio sobre a autonomia e a soberania alimentar dos povos.


A rede agradece a todas e todos que apoiaram e apoiam essa caminhada, especialmente aqueles que contribuem no Apoia-se da rede. E faz um convite para que mais pessoas contribuam, para que aumente a salvaguarda das sementes crioulas e nativas. Afinal, quem tem terra, semeia. Quem não tem, apoia. Ninguém fica para trás.

A ação foi possível graças ao projeto Laboratório Móvel da Universidade Federal do Recôncavo da Bahia (UFRB), que levou até os pequenos agricultores a tecnologia necessária para verificar se suas sementes haviam sido contaminadas por transgênicos do agronegócio. Foram testados quatro tipos de milho produzidos no Assentamento Terra Vista por Mestre Valmir e pelos militantes da rede: milho crioulo vermelho, milho de pipoca azul e milho guarani branco. O resultado foi emocionante: todas as amostras se mostraram livres de qualquer contaminação transgênica.


Esse resultado é especialmente significativo diante da dificuldade de cultivar milho sem contaminação. A polinização cruzada do milho pode alcançar um raio de mais de 50 km, o que torna a preservação das variedades crioulas um verdadeiro ato de resistência. A equipe do laboratório reforçou que a contaminação das sementes não é culpa dos agricultores, mas sim do ataque direto do capital e do latifúndio sobre a autonomia e a soberania alimentar dos povos.

A alegria tomou conta do assentamento. "Viva o milho crioulo! Viva a Teia dos Povos! Viva o Mestre Valmir!", ecoaram as vozes. content:
In this episode Sander Hoogendoorn talks with Eberhard about his experience at iBOOD with AI-supported software development. Why abandon Pull Requests? What does AI-assisted coding review really change? And what happens to collaboration when AI is used?
