title: İçme suyu havzasında 12 noktada jeotermal kuyusu açılacak
content:
Çanakkale -Balıkesir iline içme ve kullanma suyu sağlayan Gönen Barajı su toplama havzası sınırlarında yapılması planlanan jeotermal kuyu sondajı projesine Çevresel Etki Değerlendirmesi (ÇED) Olumlu (Ek 2) kararı verildi. Enther Enerji San. ve Tic. A.Ş. tarafından Çanakkale ili Yenice ilçesine bağlı Hıdırlar ve Akçakoyun köyleri sınırlarında gerçekleştirilmesi öngörülen arama projesi kapsamında 12 adet kuyu açılması hedefleniyor.

Sondaj çalışmalarının yürütüleceği noktalar, Tapu ve Kadastro verilerine göre tarla niteliğindeki arazilerden oluşuyor. Bölge, Balıkesir-Çanakkale Planlama Bölgesi çevre düzeni planında tarım ve turizm alanı olarak tanımlanıyor. Arama ruhsatı sahası içindeki çalışmalarda en yakın yerleşim birimini Hıdırlar köyü oluştururken, bir numaralı kuyu lokasyonunun en yakın konut ile arasındaki mesafe 230 metre olarak ölçülüyor. Proje Tanıtım Dosyası (PTD)’da proje sahasında herhangi bir bina inşaatı yapılmayacağı, sadece geçici şantiye ve çamur havuzlarının kurulacağı ileri sürülüyor.

Proje alanı, Balıkesir'in içme suyu ihtiyacını karşılayan Gönen Barajı ve Kumköy Regülatörü Özel Hükümleri uyarınca uzun mesafeli koruma alanı sınırları içerisinde kalıyor. Yüzeysel suların ve su kaynaklarının korunması amacıyla baraj gölünü besleyen dere yataklarına hiçbir şekilde atıksu, pasa veya hafriyat dökülmeyeceği iddia ediliyor. Sondaj işlemleri sırasında zararlı kimyasallar kullanılmayıp sadece doğal kil olan bentonit ve su tercih edileceği savunuluyor.

PTD’de proje alanının DSİ Pazarköy-Akçakoyunlu Ovaları sulama sahası içerisinde kaldığı, ana boru hattına 25 metre yaklaşma mesafesine dikkat edilmesi gerektiği uyarısına karşı şirketin taahhütte bulunduğu görülüyor. Balıkesir Su ve Kanalizasyon İdaresi (BASKİ) proje sahalarının Gönen Barajı ve Kumköy Regülatörü Uzun Mesafeli Koruma Alanı sınırları içinde kaldığını belirterek, atık sular konusunda bir dizi şartı şirketin önüne koymuş durumda. İl Tarım ve Orman Müdürlüğü ise proje sahalarının henüz tarım dışı kullanım izninin bulunmadığını belirleyerek faaliyete başlanmadan önce Toprak Koruma ve Arazi Kullanımı Kanunu, Zeytincilik Kanunu ve Mera Kanunu kapsamında gerekli izinlerin alınmasını zorunlu kılıyor.

Doğa Koruma ve Milli Parklar (DKMP) ile Orman İşletmesi de alanda Koca Çay, Araplar Deresi ve Kışla Deresi gibi akarsuların bulunduğunu ve Koca Çay'da endemik bir balık türünün yaşadığını kaydederek, akarsu civarındakikıyı alanlara müdahale edilmemesi, akarsulara atık bırakılmaması ve biyolojik çeşitliliğin korunması şartlarını koştu. ÇED Sahasında bazı alanların orman alanı içinde kaldığına dikkat çeken Çanakkale Orman Bölge Müdürlüğü, Orman Kanunu kapsamında gerekli izinlerin alınmasını istedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Tırmanış cennetine siyanür gölgesi
content:
Eskişehir - Eskişehir Sivrihisar bölgesinde faaliyet gösteren Türk Altın İşletmeleri, Kaymaz altın ve gümüş madeni için yeni bir kapasite artış süreci başlatarak çevresel etki değerlendirme başvurusunda bulundu. Madenin açık ocak genişletmesi, flotasyon ünitesi ve ikinci atık depolama tesisinin büyütülmesini içeren proje, Karakaya köyü ile bölgenin en önemli doğa sporları merkezini doğrudan etkileyecek boyutlara ulaştı. Buna karşın hazırlanan ÇED dosyasında, her yıl binlerce sporcuyu ve kampçıyı ağırlayan Karakaya kayalıkları ile kamp alanının adının dahi anılmaması dikkat çekiyor.

Türk Altın İşletmelerinin hazırladığı kapasite artış projesi, bölgedeki maden sahasını devasa boyutlara taşıyor. Şirket, Çanakkale Karapınar ve Alpu Esence sahalarından taşıyacağı milyonlarca tonluk cevheri Kaymaz tesisinde işleyerek siyanürlü atık barajlarını genişletmeyi hedefliyor. Proje alanı Karakaya köyündeki en yakın yerleşim birimine yalnızca 1,2 kilometre mesafede yer alıyor. Maden atık depolama tesislerinin ve siyanürlü işlem sahalarının köye bu kadar yaklaşması, bölgede yaşayan vatandaşlar ile doğaseverler arasında derin bir kaygı yaratıyor.

Karakaya köyü sınırlarında yer alan granit kuleler, Türkiye'nin en popüler spor tırmanış ve kamp alanları arasında bulunuyor. Bölgede 240'tan fazla tırmanış rotası yer alıyor ve her yıl üniversite kulüpleri ile dağcılık dernekleri tarafından eğitimler, şenlikler ve kamplar düzenleniyor. Akasya koruluğuyla bozkırın ortasında doğal bir vaha niteliği taşıyan bu alan, bölgeye ekonomik ve sosyal açıdan büyük canlılık kazandırıyor. Ancak maden şirketinin sunduğu resmi ÇED dosyasında bu ulusal ölçekteki tırmanış bahçesinin, kamp ve mesire alanının varlığı tamamen görmezden geliniyor.

Kayalıkların önemini gizlemek adına perdeleme mi yapılıyor?

ÇED raporundaki bu büyük eksiklik, kamuoyunda ve çevre çevrelerinde bilinçli bir perdeleme şüphesini gündeme getiriyor. Çevre hassasiyet raporlarında alanın herhangi bir özel niteliği yokmuş gibi sunulması, maden ve atık sahalarının kayalıklara vereceği tahribatı gizleme amacı taşıdığı şeklinde yorumlanıyor.

Daha önce üçüncü atık barajı projesine karşı yürütülen hukuki mücadelelerde idare mahkemesi yürütmeyi durdurma ve iptal kararları verirken, süreç Danıştay aşamalarıyla devam ediyor. Siyanür sızıntısı, ağır metal kirliliği, toz ve gürültü tehlikesi altında kalan bölge halkı ve sivil toplum kuruluşları, doğa sporları alanlarını ve yaşam alanlarını korumak için mücadeleyi sürdürüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Okullarda ‘güvenlik’ protokolünün ilk gününde okul saldırısı: Kayıp çocuklar, tehlikeli okullar
content:
Manisa'nın Turgutlu ilçesindeki İnci Üzmez Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesinde 15 yaşındaki 9. sınıf öğrencisi H.O, silahlı saldırı düzenledi. Saldırı sonucunda 2’si ağır 11 kişi yaralandı. Saldırının ardından öğrencinin yanı sıra babası, annesi ve dedesi gözaltına alındı.

Saldırının duyulmasının ardından çok sayıda veli çocuklarına ulaşmak için okulun önüne geldi. Velilerin okula girmek istemesi üzerine okul çevresinde önlem alan kolluk kuvvetleri ile veliler arasında arbede yaşandı. Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı (MEB) tarafından yapılan açıklamada, olayın incelenmesi için üç müfettişinin görevlendirildi, okulda eğitime bir gün ara verildiği duyuruldu. Radyo ve Televizyon Üst Kurulu (RTÜK), olaya ilişkin yayın yasağı getirildiğini açıklarken Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, saldırının ardından konuyla ilişkili bazı sosyal medya paylaşımlarına ilişkin soruşturma başlatıldığını duyurdu.

Manisa’daki olay, Maraş ve Antep’in ardından bu sene gerçekleşen üçüncü okul saldırısı oldu.

Eğitim Sen Manisa Şube Başkanı Mehmet Ramazan, konuya ilişkin gazetemize konuştu. Saldırının gerçekleştiği İnci Üzmez Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi'nin sosyoekonomik açıdan dezavantajlı ve kozmopolit bir bölgede bulunduğunu kaydeden Ramazan, kurumun Turgutlu Mesleki Endüstri Meslek Lisesi ile birleştirilme sürecinde olduğunu aktardı.

Öğretmenlerin itirazlarına rağmen bu adımın atıldığını hatırlatan Ramazan, “Bir araya gelmemesi gereken bu kalabalık kitleyi, yaz tatilinde yeni binalar yapmadan, okullar açılmışken ve taşınma sürerken birleştirdiler. Norm meseleleri ve bu plansız birleştirme adımları şiddet iklimini besleyen yanlış uygulamalardır” dedi.

Silahlı saldırıyı gerçekleştiren çocuğun geçtiğimiz yıl okula gitmediği için sınıf tekrarına kaldığını aktaran Ramazan; okul bünyesinde MESEM programının da bulunduğunu, ancak çocuğun programa kayıtlı olmadığını ifade etti.

Okullarda tırmanan şiddetin toplumsal gerçeklikten ve dışarıdaki koşullardan bağımsız ele alınamayacağını vurgulayan Ramazan, meseleye salt asayiş gözüyle bakılamayacağını belirterek “Şiddetin sosyolojik bir karşılığı var; kadına yönelik şiddet, suça sürüklenen çocuklar, ekonomik krizin sancıları ve psikolojik problemler gibi etkenleri görmezden gelerek sonuç alamazsınız. Meseleyi sadece okulu güvenlik parantezine alarak çözemezsiniz” ifadelerini kullandı.

Saldırıyı gerçekleştiren öğrencinin ikamet ettiği Yiğitler Mahallesi Muhtarı Veysel Çakır ise ailenin ‘kendi halinde’, küçük çaplı tarım işleriyle geçimini sağladığını ve eski bir evde yaşadıklarını aktardı.

Çocuğun okul durumu ve devamsızlık gerekçesi hakkında bilgi sahibi olmadığını dile getiren Çakır, çocuğun dışarıda başka bir işte çalıştığını görmediğini belirterek, “Çocuk 2011 doğumlu; kendisini tanıyorum, biliyorum ama bu tür bir şeyi yapabilecek bir çocuk değildi. Ailesiyle ovaya gidip geliyordu, çalışıyorsa da ailesinin yanında, kendi geçimlerini sağlayacak kadar olan tarım işinde bulunuyordu” ifadelerini kullandı.

Saldırıdan hemen bir gün önce 7 bakanlık arasında okullardaki ‘güvenlik önlemlerine ilişkin’ protokol imzalanmıştı. İçişleri Bakanlığı, Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı, Adalet Bakanlığı, Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı, Gençlik ve Spor Bakanlığı, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı ile Sağlık Bakanlığı arasında imzalanan protokole ilişkin İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, “Biz öğrencilerimizin güvenli bir şekilde okula gelmelerini, okulda huzurlu bir şekilde eğitim öğretim görmelerini ve sağ salim tekrar evlerine dönmelerini istiyoruz” demişti. Üçüncü okul saldırısının ardından ise bu bakanlardan hiçbiri sorumluluk üstlenmedi. Bu 7 sorumlu isim, ‘elem olaya ilişkin üzüntülerini’ dile getirmekle yetindi.

Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanı Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanı Vedat Işıkhan, Gençlik ve Spor Bakanı Osman Aşkın Bak, Sağlık Bakanı Kemal Memişoğlu “acil şifa dilemekle” yetinirken Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek ise 2'si ağır 11 çocuk yaralandıktan sonra “Çocuklarımızın güvenliği söz konusu olduğunda hiçbir ihmalin, hiçbir sorumsuzluğun görmezden gelinmesi mümkün değildir” dedi. İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi ile Milli Eğitim Bakanı Yusuf Tekin de Turgutlu’ya gitti.

Ortaöğretim seviyesinde okullaşma oranı sürekli düşüyor. Çocukların eğitim dışına itilmesi çocukların sosyal durumunu takip etmeyi neredeyse imkansız hâle getirirken Manisa’daki saldırı bunun son örneği oldu. Ortaöğretimdeki öğrenci sayısı 2022’de 1 milyon 789 binken bu sayı 2025’te 5 milyon 328 bine düştü.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: ICE “Disappears” Thousands Ordered to Be Deported From Detainee Locator
content:
This could make it “nearly impossible” for some people to challenge their deportation orders, an attorney said.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is removing the names of its detainees who are facing final deportation orders from its public online database.

The move will disrupt detainees’ legal challenges to deportation and leave their whereabouts unknown to their lawyers and loved ones.

The agency quietly removed thousands of people from its online detainee locator on September 15, the Associated Press reports. Certain detention facilities will not be subject to the new order if judges have ruled that they are required to list detainees in their facilities.

The exact number of names removed is unclear, but judges have issued over 740,000 removal and voluntary departure orders this year, while reports have found that ICE arrested nearly 16,000 people in July who were subject to final removal orders. Experts and advocates have criticized the practice as digitally “disappearing” immigrants, saying that it’s yet another erosion of due process rights.

The agency has also issued a new policy barring immigration officials from sharing the locations of such detainees, two former Department of Homeland Security officials told The Washington Post.

This policy of hiding detainees’ locations will make it far harder or “nearly impossible” for many people to challenge their removals, legal experts said, as the agency rushes to make quotas for its mass deportation campaign.

American Civil Liberties Union Senior Staff Attorney My Khanh Ngo told AP that eight Somali men, her clients, detained at the U.S.’s Guantanamo Bay detention camp are among those whose names were removed. She said that such a move could make it “nearly impossible” to challenge many deportation cases.

“If you can’t find your client, don’t know what’s happening to your client, you can’t get that information to the court to stop their removal,” said Ngo.

“Families are freaking out because they think the person has been deported and they don’t know where the person might be,” said Greg Chen, senior director of government relations for the American Immigration Lawyers Association, per AP. “On the attorney side, this has serious implications for the ability to contact their client. It certainly has implications about how it will interfere with the attorney-client relationship.”

ICE has already faced scrutiny over its practices of quietly transferring detainees to different facilities without notification, often leaving families terrified when they find out that their loved one has been moved thousands of miles away.

Over the past year, the Trump administration has sent over 25,000 people to countries that they had no previous connection with, according to Refugees International. Under the direction of White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, the Trump administration transformed a former refugee bureau within the State Department into the “Office of Remigration,” which has authorized or pledged $410 million in agreements with 31 countries, mostly in Africa and Latin America.

The news of the database deletions comes just days after an ICE agent shot and wounded a Venezuelan man, Wilber Garcés Pérez, in Austin over the weekend. ICE has reportedly transferred Garcés from a local hospital to a detention facility against doctors’ recommendations, as doctors have not removed the bullet from his body because it is too close to his spine. Despite this, a judge has ordered the 28-year-old DoorDash driver to be present for an in-person deportation hearing on September 30.

title: Erdoğan BM'de "Küresel cinsiyetsizleştirme politikalarına karşı" LGBTİ+ operasyonlarını savundu:
content:
⁠Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) 81. Genel Kurulu'ndaki konuşmasında Gazze'deki savaşa son verilmesi, Filistin'in tanınması ve BM Güvenlik Konseyi'nin reformu çağrısında bulundu; Suriye'de Ahmed Şara yönetimine desteğini yineledi, Ukrayna'nın toprak bütünlüğünü savundu ve Kuzey Kıbrıs Türk Cumhuriyeti'nin tanınmasını istedi.


Konuşmanın son bölümünde ise Erdoğan, Türkiye'de son dönemde hükümetin LGBTİ+ politikalarının temel söylemini oluşturan “aile ve çocukların korunması” yaklaşımını BM Genel Kurulu'na taşıdı.


Reuters, Erdoğan'ın konuşmasının bu bölümünü ayrıca haberleştirirken, Türkiye'de LGBTİ+ örgütlerini hedef alan “Ailem Güvende” operasyonundan bir hafta sonra yapıldığına dikkat çekti. Operasyon kapsamında 82 kişinin tutuklandığını, 100'den fazla protestocunun da gözaltına alındığını duyurdu. 


“Kadın ve erkekten oluşan aile”


Erdoğan, konuşmasının bu bölümünde sözlerine Batı ülkelerinde İslam düşmanlığı, Müslüman kadınlara yönelik ayrımcılık ve başörtüsü yasaklarını eleştirerek başladı. Müslüman kadın ve kız çocuklarının ayrımcılığa daha fazla maruz kaldığını söyleyen Erdoğan, bazı ülkelerdeki okul başörtüsü yasaklarını “kadınların en temel haklarına yapılmış bir saldırı” olarak nitelendirdi.


Yabancı düşmanlığı, kültürel ırkçılık ve antisemitizmle mücadele edilmesi gerektiğini söyledikten sonra  “cinsiyetsizleştirme” olarak kodladığı LGBTİ+'lara yönelik uygulamalarına geçti:


“Küresel cinsiyetsizleştirme politikaları, aile kurumuyla birlikte masum çocukları da hedef alan bir kuşatmaya dönüşmüştür. Bu kuşatmayı ancak kadın ve erkekten oluşan aileyi koruyarak kırabiliriz.”


Erdoğan ardından Türkiye'nin izleyeceği politikayı şu sözlerle açıkladı:


“Türkiye, lobilerin saldırılarına rağmen aile ve çocukların korunmasında inisiyatif almayı sürdürecektir.”


Erdoğan, “lobiler” ile kimi kastettiğini açıklamadı ve konuşmasının bu bölümünde LGBTİ+ ifadesini kullanmadı. Ancak sözleri, doğrudan LGBTİ+ örgütlerine yönelik son operasyonlar bağlamında haberleştirildi.


Erdoğan aynı konuşması kapsamında “cinsiyetsizleştirme” olarak nitelediği toplumsal cinsiyetin tanınmasına yönelik saldırılarının ardından sosyal medyadaki "dezenformasyon"a, oradan yapay zekâya geçti:


“Toplumsal barışı dinamitleyen bir diğer tehdit, sosyal medyada yaygınlaşan dezenformasyon faaliyetleridir. Hakikati savunmak, bugün daha önce hiç olmadığı kadar önemli hale gelmiştir.”


Ardından, yapay zekâ için uluslararası ortak bir hukuki çerçeve oluşturulmasını ve bir BM Uluslararası Yapay Zekâ Sözleşmesi hazırlanmasını istedi. Konuşmasının sonunda dile getirdiği görüşlerin “birilerini rahatsız edeceğini” söyleyen Erdoğan, “sesimizi kısmak için her türlü algı operasyonuna başvuracaklar" iddiasında bulundu. 


BM ve Avrupa Konseyi operasyonları eleştirmişti


Erdoğan'ın bugünkü sözlerine, Türkiye'de LGBTİ+'lara yönelik operasyonlar sırasında uygulananlara yöneltilen eleştiriler çerçevesinde bir yanıt ortaya çıkmamıştı. Ancak konuşmada kullanılan “aile ve çocukların korunması” gerekçesi, Türkiye hükümetinin geçen hafta LGBTİ+ örgütlerine yönelik operasyonları savunurken kullandığı gerekçeyle örtüşüyor. Operasyonların başlamasının ardından uluslararası insan hakları mekanizmalarından tepkiler gelmişti. 


Salı günü de 65 ülkenin hak kuruluşlarından bir ortak açıklama yayımlandı:


65 ülkeden Türkiye'ye çağrı: LGBTİ+ hareketini kriminalize etmekten vazgeçin


22 Eylül 2026


BM insan hakları mekanizması Türkiye'den LGBTİ+ hak savunucularına yönelik gözaltı ve tutuklamalara son vermesini ve insan hakları faaliyetleri nedeniyle özgürlüğünden yoksun bırakılanların serbest bırakılmasını istemişti.

author: Julia Conley
title: Judge Blocks Deportation of ICE Shooting Victim Wilber Rafael Garces Perez
content:
Garces Perez was transferred back to the Texas ICE jail as the bullet reportedly remains lodged in his back.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The attorney representing Wilber Rafael Garces Perez said Tuesday that a federal judge had granted her emergency request to block the Trump administration from deporting the 28-year-old delivery driver, who was shot by an immigration agent Sunday and has since been transferred multiple times between hospitals and a detention center — all while the officer’s bullet reportedly remains lodged in his back.

“We have filed a federal lawsuit, and the judge has ordered that he be present at the first hearing, which is scheduled for Wednesday, September 30,” said Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch. “And that means he won’t be deported in the meantime.”

Lincoln-Goldfinch applauded the rare piece of “good news” that has come out of Garces Perez’s case since he was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent while making DoorDash deliveries in his car Sunday afternoon.

As Common Dreams reported, Garces Perez was transferred from an ICE detention center in Pearsall, Texas to a hospital late Monday after reporting that he had lost feeling in the left side of his body, likely as a result of the bullet that remained close to his spine.

But Lincoln-Goldfinch and Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-Texas) said Tuesday that Garces Perez had again been taken back to the detention center.

Castro said he and Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas) plan to visit Garces Perez at South Texas ICE Processing Center on Wednesday, to “check on his condition and demand his release.”

“It is nothing more than a prison,” said Castro. “Wilber came to the United States legally. He had work permits and was an asylum seeker. None of this should have ever happened.”

Garces Perez arrived in the US in 2024 from Venezuela, using a government program for asylum seekers and the CBP One app that was introduced by the Biden administration to make an appointment for approval from immigration agents. He received a work permit and applied for asylum.

He mistakenly missed an immigration hearing after a notice was sent to an old address, The New York Times reported, which led to his deportation order. He has no criminal history.

Lincoln-Goldfinch had been planning to visit her client in the hospital Tuesday, where he was taken after he called in to a press conference the lawyer was holding Monday and said that he had not received medical treatment for his gunshot wound.

After speaking to Garces Perez via a video call Tuesday morning, Lincoln-Goldfinch reported on social media:

Wilber tells me that after he spoke publicly, guards at the Pearsall detention center forcibly took the tablet from his hands, revoked his communication privileges, and moved him out of the infirmary into an isolated room with a flat bed that cannot be adjusted like a medical bed.

At the hospital, Wilber says doctors finally spoke directly to him about his care and gave him IV morphine for his pain. We now understand that the gunshot fractured his clavicle and that he has significant swelling and is wearing a sling. We still do not have clarity about the cause or extent of the loss of movement he experienced.

He was discharged back to Pearsall around midnight. Today, he tells me he is receiving only Tylenol and ibuprofen for pain. He remains in isolation, on a flat bed, and without the tablet he previously used to communicate. We are asking for his communication privileges to be immediately restored and for him to be provided an appropriate medical bed and adequate medical care. Most importantly, we are continuing to advocate for Wilber’s IMMEDIATE release.

Also on Tuesday, it was revealed that the ICE agent who shot Garces Perez was not wearing a body camera at the time of the shooting — similar to the case of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, who was fatally shot by an ICE agent in Maine in July.

We had a massive debate about this, and ICE assured everyone it would get the cameras working for accountability, but it instead only uses cameras for surveillance.

“Before we hear anything from ICE about, ‘We pulled him over, or he was fleeing, or he was aggressive,’ our response to any statements like that is, ‘We won’t believe you until you show us,’” said Goldfinch-Lincoln. “Show us your body cam footage, show us your dash cam footage.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: Denuncian que el INTA censura a una investigadora que estudió los efectos de los agroquímicos en el campo
content:
Virginia Aparicio coordinó una investigación internacional en la que detectó presencia de plaguicidas en muestras humanas y ambientales en Argentina, pero el organismo le prohibió difundir los resultados.


Virginia Aparicio, ingeniera agrónoma, doctora en Ciencias Agrarias e investigadora del INTA.  


La Asociación del Personal del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (APINTA) difundió un comunicado en el que expresó “preocupación” por la situación de la investigadora del organismo, Virginia Aparicio, científica de la Estación Experimental Agropecuaria (EEA) Balcarce, y denunció que atraviesa una situación de “persecución, censura y silenciamiento” dentro del organismo.


Aparicio fue coordinadora en Argentina del proyecto internacional SPRINT, financiado por la Unión Europea, que en 2023 le permitió estudiar la presencia de plaguicidas en muestras humanas y ambientales en Argentina y que formó parte de un trabajo de alcance internacional.


Denuncian censura en el INTA


En ese momento, cuando intentó divulgar los resultados, a fines de 2023, el director nacional del organismo le escribió un correo electrónico en el que explícitamente le prohibió hacerlo como investigadora del INTA.


Pues bien, a pesar del tiempo transcurrido, y de las disculpas ofrecidas por el INTA, el asedio y la censura no sé habrían reducido, sino más bien se incrementaron.


Es que Aparicio fue sumariada por llevar a analizar al exterior las muestras tomadas en la investigación porque en el organismo no lo realizan.


NO 2026 90714427 APN EEAAMBAINTA


Salida del Proyecto Sprint


Desde APINTA señalaron que la presentación pública de los resultados fue suspendida en 2023 y que posteriormente el INTA decidió finalizar la participación argentina en el proyecto.


“La investigación científica debe poder desarrollarse con libertad, transparencia y respaldo institucional”, sostuvo la organización gremial, que planteó que los investigadores deben poder desarrollar sus trabajos, comunicar sus resultados y aportar conocimiento a la sociedad.


En otra pieza difundido bajo el título “Basta de persecución en el INTA”, APINTA volvió a referirse a Aparicio y sostuvo que los resultados del proyecto SPRINT fueron adversos en relación con la salud pública, particularmente para el sector productivo.


Defensa a Virginia Aparicio


El gremio cuestionó así la situación de la investigadora y reclamó garantías para el desarrollo de la actividad científica dentro del organismo.


“No hay desarrollo productivo sin ciencia. No hay ciencia sin libertad para investigar”, expresó APINTA, que además advirtió sobre la importancia de contar con un INTA que pueda producir y comunicar conocimiento.


“Desde APINTA levantamos la voz en defensa de la ciencia y de quienes investigan en el INTA”, apuntaron.


Sprint


El proyecto internacional SPRINT permitió estudiar la presencia de plaguicidas en muestras humanas y ambientales en Argentina, como parte de una investigación internacional. Sin embargo, la presentación pública de resultados fue suspendida en 2023 y posteriormente el INTA decidió finalizar la participación argentina en el proyecto.


“Desde APINTA defendemos el derecho de las y los investigadores a desarrollar su trabajo, comunicar sus resultados y aportar conocimiento a la sociedad”, señalaron.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Admin Boots 760K Individuals From ACA Exchanges, Citing Alleged Fraud
content:
One critic decried the move as “a political stunt designed to throw even more people off their coverage.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Vice President J.D. Vance and Mehmet Oz, the head of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, jointly announced on Tuesday a plan by the Trump administration to cancel coverage for hundreds of thousands of individuals and families currently enrolled in insurance exchanges within the Affordable Care Act (ACA).

The administration will cancel around 315,000 ACA health plans, which provide health insurance coverage for approximately 760,000 people in the U.S. Both Vance and Oz allege that the plan targets people whose applications neglected to include required information on their applications. Some enrollees may have been added to the ACA — sometimes known as Obamacare — without their knowledge, the pair also alleged.

Yet, many people may face removal simply because their insurance brokers, who helped them enroll, mistakenly did not place their Social Security numbers on submitted documents when they applied.

In response to that action, Vance and Oz announced that over 500 brokers have been warned they could be blocked from taking part in enrolling future participants. CMS also announced a moratorium on new brokers helping people to enroll.

“A blanket moratorium on new agent and broker registrations would punish legitimate professionals instead of targeting the bad actors responsible for fraud,” said Mychal Walker, president of the National Association of Benefits ​and Insurance Professionals.

The bulk removal of individuals enrolled in the ACA exchanges is part of a so-called anti-fraud task force that Vance is leading.

“This is what the fraud task force is all about,” the vice president said at a press conference for the plan, claiming that billions of dollars will be saved by removing these individuals.

“If you care about the ACA, then you’ll want us to take the fraud out,” Oz also stated.

Asked by a reporter whether some eligible individuals could be removed from the ACA rolls, Vance dismissed those concerns, claiming the White House had attempted to reach out to people by mail to prevent that outcome, stating that, “we send them FedEx letters, we go to their house.”

But the flippant attitude of the duo may cause some to question whether they are sincere. At one point, the image of a person alleged to have engaged in fraud was displayed during the presser. “He’s got a very punchable face,” Oz said.

In addition to the 760,000 who were announced to be removed from the ACA health coverage, the duo also said they were examining an additional 400,000 individuals they suspect are part of a larger fraud scheme.

The advocates of social programs have criticized the administration’s purported focus on rooting out fraud as a ruse for cutting benefits and programs that help Americans with lower incomes.

“Families need coverage they can afford and count on when they get sick. Vance’s task force won’t accomplish that,” said Brad Woodhouse, president of Protect Our Care, adding that the vice president’s actions are “nothing more than a bullshit distraction — a political stunt designed to throw even more people off their coverage while pretending to save taxpayers’ money.”

In an op-ed for Truthout in May, Amy K. Matsui, vice president for child care and income security at the National Women’s Law Center, wrote, “These efforts are less about ensuring that public dollars are spent for their intended purpose and more about cutting basic needs programs altogether”:

It’s hard to seriously argue that this administration is concerned with rooting out fraud, considering the president has pardoned wealthy donors convicted of tax fraud, forgoing millions of dollars in restitution. So, I repeat: This is not really about responsible stewardship of public resources or making life more affordable for struggling families.

The announcement of the plan by the Trump administration on Tuesday comes as over 5 million Americans have already dropped their ACA enrollment this year after being unable to afford coverage. Prices have soared after the White House refused to renew subsidies for the program that were introduced during the coronavirus pandemic to help more people gain access to health care.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Threatens Iran With Genocide in Address to UN General Assembly
content:
“Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he said.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump made his most openly genocidal threat yet to Iran on Tuesday, threatening to “annihilate” the country and its 92 million people with “no hope of survival.”

In his opening address to the UN General Assembly in New York City, Trump asserted again that he is facing a choice on Iran about whether to make a deal “that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country.”

“Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” Trump said in his UN speech.

Trump has repeatedly made genocidal threats against Iran, prompting calls for impeachment and war crimes inquiries. These arresting remarks are especially alarming considering that Trump felt emboldened to make them at the highest-level gathering of world leaders, under the flag of an organization created after World War II with the mission of preventing global atrocities.

Human rights experts have previously said that Trump’s threats to wipe out Iran are genocidal. The UN’s Genocide Convention defines genocide as acts carried out “with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.”

Over the nearly seven months of his war on Iran, Trump’s genocidal threats have become commonplace. He has previously said that “a whole civilization will die tonight”; claimed numerous times that there “won’t be anything left” after he strikes the country; and, most recently, pontificated about “if and when do I blow the entire nation up?”

During his remarks at the UN, Trump said that Iran’s air force, navy, nuclear program, and defense equipment have been totally destroyed by the U.S – a dubious claim that he’s made since the first week of the war. He said that Iran’s government “slaughtered 72,000 of its citizens this year,” adding that “recently 10,000 were killed for protesting.”

It’s unclear what events Trump is referencing. Iranian human rights activists have recorded roughly 6,500 protesters killed in mass protests in December and January, far lower than Trump’s 72,000 figure. Many mass gatherings in Iran since then have cheered the government against the U.S. and Israel’s war of aggression.

A UN fact-finding mission also recently found that two U.S. strikes on Iran during the first day of the war were likely war crimes in violation of international laws of civilian protection.

After making his genocidal threat at the UN, Trump claimed “we will make a deal right after the election. It doesn’t make sense for them not to. They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election, what they don’t realize is I am not running.” He said that, once the war is over, oil prices “will come plummeting down even lower than they were at the start of the conflict.”

Analysts have said this claim attempts to manipulate voters amid the president’s record low approval ratings, driven in large part by the war and the affordability crisis that it’s worsened.

In his speech, Trump also threatened Cuba, saying that his administration is “seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba,” where he said left-wing leaders have “spent decades coordinating with the left-wing radicals and communist networks here in the United States.”

author: Renée Feltz
title: Tennessee Is Days Away From Executing a Sexual Assault Victim
content:
Christa Pike’s lethal injection is booked for September 30. She may be the first woman Tennessee executes in 200 years.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Christa Pike was sexually abused and raped from the time when she was a toddler until almost a year to the day before she was arrested in 1995 at age 18 for murdering fellow teenager Colleen Slemmer when the two attended a job training program for troubled youth in Knoxville.

Tennessee officials do not dispute these facts. “I think everybody in this courtroom wishes that those things had never happened to Ms. Pike,” Tennessee Attorney General’s Office lawyer Will Ayers acknowledged in his closing argument to a grueling three-day hearing last month about challenges to Pike’s execution scheduled for September 30. “I think we all wish that we were not here today and that she was not on death row.”

In a new approach, the state’s Supreme Court appointed Shelby County Senior Judge Mark Ward as a “special master” to hear the arguments by Pike’s defense team, including that lethal injection would be cruel and unusual because it could trigger traumatic memories, among other reasons.

“We’ve all heard of flashbacks,” said clinical psychologist Dr. Bethany Brand, who testified that such memories can “intrude so intensively that the person loses all awareness of where they actually are, and what’s happening, and they instead are reliving what they lived through already.” Brand interviewed Pike in 2023 and found the “level of trauma she was subjected to … is almost impossible to grasp because it is so severe.”

Experts in the field of trauma and sexual violence filed an amicus brief in the case arguing there is “substantial risk” that the execution would cause Pike to re-experience what she endured as a girl and teenager and “it will be as horrific for her now as it was then.”

“Once she is restrained and immobilized, a man will try to find a vein in Ms. Pike’s arm through which he will inject the poison that will kill her,” notes the brief. “If he cannot find a vein in her arm, the expectation is that he will attempt to inject the poison near her groin.”

But a week after the hearing, Ward concluded Pike’s team had “failed” to prove she would face “needless suffering,” or could “avoid mental suffering” if the state used any other method besides lethal injection.

If the justices agree with Ward’s “findings,” then Pike’s lawyers say they will appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court. They have also submitted a clemency petition to Republican Gov. Bill Lee, asking him to commute her sentence to life in prison without parole, noting that Pike’s life of abuse went unad­dressed by the adults and state sys­tems meant to pro­tect her, and she has accepted responsibility for her crime and expressed deep remorse. Otherwise, she will be the first woman Tennessee executes in over 200 years, and the last person sentenced to death in the state for a crime committed at such a young age, the petition states.

“There is an inability to hold simultaneously in our minds that this person not only inflicted suffering but is someone who is herself suffering, and that is what we really need to do to understand this case,” Sandra Babcock, faculty director and founder of the Cornell Center on the Death Penalty Worldwide, told Truthout. “It’s not to erase the suffering of either Colleen Slemmer or Christa Pike. It is to recognize that Christa, in addition to being a perpetrator, was herself a victim.”

Authorities in West Virginia first failed to help Pike after being alerted to her suffering as an elementary school student when a teacher called her parents but failed to alert authorities when she drew a man with a “huge penis and demon face.” At age 11, she was raped by a man who pled “no contest” to a reduced charge, then faced abuse from her mother’s boyfriends in her own home. After lashing out and abusing drugs, she was sent to juvenile detention centers in North Carolina where her former attorney Matthew Martin, now a judge, testified he and others “failed her” when she should have instead “had services wrapped around her.” Not long after she returned home, she was raped at age 17.

To find a new start, Pike attended a job training program in Knoxville, Tennessee, but she fell into a relationship with 17-year-old Tadaryl Shipp, who had a history of violence and abusive behavior. Pike thought Slemmer was trying to “steal” …

author: Kourosh Ziabari
title: No English Test for You: Trump’s Campaign Against Iran Now Targets Education
content:
By restricting access to standardized tests, the US is effectively blocking Iranians from applying to schools abroad.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

As U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration tightens its repressive measures against Iran, Iranian students and applicants of English proficiency tests have become the latest targets of a campaign by the White House to severely constrain Iran’s connections with the rest of the world.

With the war on Iran nearing the end of its seventh month, the U.S.-Israeli bombing operations have been supplanted by new tactics, including a package of sweeping sanctions rolled out on August 24, which the Department of the Treasury has labeled as “Economic D-Day,” calling it an “unprecedented, whole-of-government, economic campaign” that will continue until “Tehran stands alone.”

As part of this economic offensive, the Office of Foreign Assets Control has revoked several sanctions regulations licenses, including Iran General License G, which previously allowed academic exchanges and authorized certain educational services in Iran, such as tests of English proficiency that are administered worldwide.

Now, young Iranians seeking educational opportunities overseas are saying their prospects are being undermined: International companies conducting credentialed tests in Iran have ceased their local operations, and third countries where Iranian students could travel to take the tests are also turning them away.

The Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), Pearson Test of English (PTE), and International English Language Testing System (IELTS) are among the standardized tests that academic institutions in English-speaking and some other countries expect international applicants to pass as a requirement of enrollment in their programs.

Other additional tests are often required by higher education institutions during the admission process, including the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE). For years, these tests have enabled cohorts of young Iranians to follow their educational aspirations in places like the U.K., Canada, and the United States, where they remain some of the largest populations of international students despite stringent visa policies.

This slow but steady trickle of opportunity may now be halted as the U.S. blocks Iranians from satisfying the basic conditions of applying to schools. There are also concerns that overcompliance may add arbitrary prohibitions to the existing rules, worsening discrimination against people of Iranian heritage based on their country of origin or perceived nationality, even if they’re residents of other countries.

“I had one student who had taken the PTE exam in Van and wanted to retake two skill sections, but unfortunately, she was told that because of the new restrictions, she couldn’t participate using an Iranian passport,” said Mona Poorverdi, a 41-year-old English teacher in northern Iran, referring to an applicant she knew who was barred from sitting for the exam in Turkey earlier this summer.

Administered by the London-based Pearson plc, the test includes multiple modules, including PTE Academic, which is accepted by universities in Britain, Australia, and New Zealand. The multinational company, whose chair is the Iranian American businessman and Google’s former Chief Business Officer Omid Kordestani, has now announced that it will comply with the U.S. sanctions and will not schedule or deliver exams for candidates who are residents of Iran.

Shortly after the Treasury’s campaign was set in motion, the New Jersey-headquartered Educational Testing Service (ETS) announced the indefinite suspension of TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran. The private educational assessment organization, which administers a range of language proficiency and certification exams, said the action was “required to comply with U.S. sanctions law.”

Pearson plc and ETS didn’t respond to Truthout’s request for comment.

Other private companies have also joined the U.S. government’s economic warfare targeting everyday life in Iran. Starting September, the Pennsylvania-headquartered educational technology company Duolingo has placed a moratorium on Iranian citizens taking its Duolingo English Test, citing the Trump administration’s sanctions.

author: FMF Staff
title: Five Years Later, Girls in Afghanistan Are Still Waiting For School Doors To Open
content:
For five years, girls above sixth grade have been barred from classrooms, making Afghanistan the only country in the world where girls are banned from secondary and higher education.

The ban was initially said to be a temporary measure but has now defined half a decade of life for millions of Afghan girls. For them, these years were supposed to be spent in classrooms, preparing for university, building careers, and planning their futures. Instead, they have been spending time waiting.

According to United Nations data, 2.6 million girls have been denied their right to education since the ban began, a policy that experts warn will have long-term consequences not only for girls, but for Afghanistan’s economy, health system, and future development. UNICEF has warned that if the ban continues, millions more girls will be deprived of education by the end of the decade. The ban has already dismantled the pipeline for female doctors and midwives. The maternal and infant mortality rate has already gone up and is only expected to go higher.

When looking beyond the statistics, we see the actual lives that have been put on pause for 5 years.

Many girls who were in sixth grade when the ban began should now be graduating from high school or attending university. Instead, they remain at home, trying to continue their education through informal or online means, knowing that nothing can replace a classroom. One student explained that she would have been preparing for her final year of school by now, but after years of waiting, she has begun to lose hope in the future she once planned.

Others describe the psychological toll of being excluded from education for years. One student said that being away from school for so long had caused depression and a deep sense of uncertainty about the future, adding that five years is “a lifetime” to be kept from education.

Afghan women who shared their testimonies describe losing both their jobs and their ability to continue their education, leaving them feeling that their role and identity in society had been taken away.

“The deeper pain is the loss of security and freedom, waking up every day with the thought that your future is uncertain,” one Afghan woman said in testimony collected from inside the country.

“Watching the sisters and daughters of this land be deprived of their right to education… These changes have not only altered our personal lives; they have wounded the soul of our society.”

Many women also warned that the longer the ban continues, the more dangerous its effects become. There are growing concerns about forced marriages, poverty, mental health, and the normalization of a system in which girls are excluded from public life and education.

Afghan women say their lives have changed in ways they never could have imagined. Before the restrictions, many were studying, working, and building careers. Today, many are confined to their homes, unable to work, unable to study, unable to laugh and visit relatives, unable to walk around their neighborhoods and parks and connect with their community, and unable to feel secure about their children’s future.

Despite 5 years of compounding restrictions, many Afghan women and girls continue to resist in quiet ways: teaching children at home, studying online, starting small businesses, and continuing to learn wherever and however they can. They have shared time and time again that these small acts are their way of keeping hope alive and tightening their grasp on their stalled dreams.

The question many Afghan girls are asking remains the same: How many more years must pass before they are allowed to return to school?

For millions of Afghan girls, the loss of education has not only taken away classrooms and careers, but more crucially it has taken away valuable time, opportunity, and the ability to plan a future. The longer this ban continues, the more it threatens not only the lives of Afghan women and girls, but the future of Afghanistan itself.

As one Afghan woman wrote in a testimony from inside the country: “We are not just statistics or headlines. We are human beings, with dreams, talents, and hearts that still beat for the future. Please do not forget the voices of Afghan women.”

author: Unknown
title: Doğan: We expect important developments in the coming days
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan spoke on current developments following her party’s first Central Executive Board (MYK) meeting after its 5th Ordinary Congress.


According to Doğan, the meeting addressed the party’s work for the new period, the new legislative term, the Peace and Democratic Society Process, as well as economic and social developments.


‘We expect important developments’


Commenting on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Ayşegül Doğan said they viewed the framework law adopted by Parliament as the first step in the process.


She said efforts regarding disarmament were continuing through contacts between state officials, Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK leadership, adding that reciprocal efforts were also underway on the ground.


“We expect important developments regarding disarmament in the coming days,” Ayşegül Doğan said.


She added that an announcement would be made when there were concrete developments arising from these efforts that could be shared with the public, noting that no definite date had been set.


Öcalan’s role


Ayşegül Doğan said that Abdullah Öcalan’s role in the process should not be considered solely from a single perspective.


Disarmament on the one hand, political transition on the other


Ayşegül Doğan further stated the following:

His formal involvement in the work as coordinator for disarmament and political transition would have an extremely positive impact. That is why we consider this important.


There will also be a need for certain working groups that can contribute to the efforts on disarmament and political transition. These developments will be important for identifying and establishing those groups and for enabling the work to move swiftly toward a conclusion.


Therefore, Mr. Öcalan’s role needs to be discussed not from a single perspective, but in all its various dimensions: disarmament on the one hand and political transition on the other. Because this process is about making a lasting transition from conflict to democratic politics. All mechanisms must operate accordingly.


Committees must work effectively and in coordination


Following the establishment of the Monitoring and Evaluation Committee after the law was enacted, we are now able to hold these discussions. The Monitoring and Evaluation Committee, as stipulated by the law, held its first meeting on August 24. At a press conference we held afterward, following discussions within our Central Executive Board, we emphasized the importance of the fact that this committee had been established quickly, had convened, had begun its work, and was carrying out activities on the ground.


A committee was established and subcommittees were formed. However, no public statement has yet been made regarding who will serve on these four subcommittees or how they will operate. Nor has any information been provided on the matter.


As the DEM Party, we have previously stated that it is very important for these committees to work effectively, in coordination and in close cooperation with one another. We reiterate this.


The new term beginning on October 1 will be very important


We emphasize that the new term beginning on October 1 will be a very important period for peace and democracy. Parliament has major responsibilities in permanently ending the conflict, strengthening democratic politics, and removing obstacles to political participation. All political parties, and of course the Speaker of Parliament in particular, have crucial roles to play. Parliament Speaker Mr. Kurtulmuş periodically informs the public about this issue and makes statements regarding the steps that need to be taken.


Fair representation must be ensured

title: PJAK member remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after arrest by Iranian intelligence
content:
Sirwan Habibi, a member of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him in Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that Habibi’s family has repeatedly visited Ministry of Intelligence offices and courts in Kamyaran and Sanandaj in recent days, seeking information about his situation. However, the authorities have continued to deny any knowledge of his arrest.


Habibi, from Sanandaj, is known within PJAK by the organisational name Aram Sine. The continued lack of information about his fate, together with the absence of any judicial case registered in his name at the courts in either city, has heightened concerns about his condition and whereabouts.


KHRN has spoken to several residents of Kamyaran’s Besat neighbourhood who witnessed his arrest, obtaining further details about the circumstances.


According to witnesses, dozens of civilian vehicles with tinted windows used by the Ministry of Intelligence agents surrounded several streets in the neighbourhood on the evening of 8 September. At about 01:00 local time on 9 September, agents began pursuing Habibi as he rode a motorcycle.


Witnesses said one of the vehicles struck his motorcycle at high speed, causing it to overturn, before agents used violence to arrest him.


Bystanders called the police emergency number, 110, and approached to help him after the motorcycle overturned. Plainclothes forces fired into the air to disperse them.


One witness said: “A few minutes later, a police patrol responding to the 110 call arrived, unaware of what was happening. But security forces blocked its path, said it was a security matter and forced the officers to leave.”


The witnesses said Habibi resisted arrest, but agents beat him, covered his face with a cloth and put him in a Samand car before taking him away.


In a statement issued on 14 September, PJAK said Habibi had been carrying out an organisational mission and was unarmed when Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him. The party said his fate remained unknown.


KHRN’s findings show that, before the US-Israeli war with Iran, most people arrested by the Ministry of Intelligence and the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Kurdistan Province were taken to the two agencies’ detention facilities in Sanandaj, where they were held and interrogated.


Following US and Israeli air strikes on those facilities, security agents have been holding detainees in secret detention facilities operated by the Ministry of Intelligence and in solitary confinement in prisons in the cities concerned.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Compares AI Warnings to Past Climate Fears He Wrongly Says Were a “Hoax”
content:
Millions of people have died as a direct result of the climate crisis.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump has dismissed legitimate concerns about the growth of artificial intelligence (AI), comparing them to the “hoax” of the climate crisis.

“The same people that said, ‘We’ll all be dead in twelve years because of Global Warming’ … are the people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us, that robots are going to attack us, and everything is a DISASTER,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

The president’s comments came a week after reports about the U.S. military nearly starting a war with China after relying on false information from AI, and after the world experienced its hottest month on record in August.

Trump also claimed that “nobody was dead” due to climate change, and compared AI concerns to the investigation into election interference by Russia during his first term in office, and his impeachment over withholding aid from Ukraine in order to get political “dirt” on Joe Biden, wrongly describing both of those situations as “a Hoax.”

In dismissing worries over the expansion of AI — which tech experts and developers themselves have said should be slowed down until proper safeguards are instituted — Trump made a false claim about the climate crisis: that no one has died from it.

In fact, millions of people around the world have lost their lives due to its impacts.

According to a Lancet Countdown report published last fall, which was authored by 128 experts from 71 different academic institutions, 546,000 deaths have occurred from heat exposure on average each year over the past decade. It also found that 84 percent of heatwave days in the past five years of data wouldn’t have happened without the effects of the climate crisis, and that droughts induced by the climate crisis have also led to 123.7 million more people experiencing food insecurity around the world than observed between 1981 and 2010.

“We’re seeing millions of deaths that are occurring needlessly every year because of our persistent fossil fuel dependence, because of our delay in mitigating climate change, and our delays in adaptation to the climate change that cannot be avoided,” said Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown at University College London.

Extreme weather events, which are becoming more numerous and severe due to climate change, have caused at least hundreds of thousands of deaths over the past 20 years.

“From 1995 to 2024, more than 832,000 lives were lost … driven by more than 9,700 extreme weather events,” reads an explainer from GermanWatch’s Climate Risk Index. “The frequency and intensity of climate-related disasters continue to rise, and these figures underscore the urgent need for climate action.”

A University of Wisconsin-Madison study published in 2022 found that eliminating air pollution from energy-related activities could reduce premature deaths in the U.S. by more than 53,000 annually. Put another way, by ending the country’s dependence on fossil fuels and shifting to renewable energy sources, the U.S. could save a number of lives nearly equivalent to the population of Madison every five years.

AI data centers will also worsen the climate crisis.

According to a 2015 analysis from Cornell University researchers, by 2030, the current rate of AI growth will add 24 to 44 million metric tons of carbon dioxide to the atmosphere every year. That amount is equal to 5 to 10 million cars added to U.S. roads annually. Water usage to cool these data centers would also equal the annual household usage of 6 to 10 million Americans per year.

author: Daron Letts
title: From ‘Fore!’ to ‘Play ball!’: Golf event makes Iqaluit minor softball league reality
content:
Minor league softball is coming to Iqaluit in summer 2027, thanks to more than $220,000 raised by the Iqaluit Charity Golf Tournament in Gatineau, Que.


“This support will give more young people a chance to be active, learn new skills and take part in organized recreation,” said Iqaluit Mayor Solomon Awa Monday in a news release.


Organized by Outcrop Communications, more than 130 golfers took part in the Sept. 17 event, which also attracted approximately 30 corporate sponsors.


The donations are destined for the Ikajuqtiit Community Association, a non profit, Iqaluit-based organization that enhances recreational opportunities for local youth, including improvements to the Iqaluit ball diamond.


The funds will cover uniforms and equipment for the new league, said association chair Tom Fitzgerald Tuesday in a phone interview.

The money will also pay for the installation of artificial turf in the outfield.


Those materials are scheduled to arrive next July on the first sealift of 2026, at no charge by Nunavut Sealink and Supply Inc., he said.


It is the first time the association has been the beneficiary in the charitable event’s 19-year history.


 Habitat for Humanity Iqaluit usually receives the funds that the event raises.


However, because Habitat for Humanity had no projects planned for Iqaluit this year, organizers chose to support Ikajuqtiit, said Outcrop Communications CEO Jen Hayward Monday in a phone interview.


The city’s recreation department will organize and administer the league, Fitzgerald said.

title: COMPRENDRE ET AGIR DANS LA COMPLEXITÉ : pour une théorie de la situation
content:
Le séminaire réunit des praticiens, chercheurs et militants de France, Argentine et Italie qui refusent la résignation. Depuis 1995, nous produisons des outils théoriques pour comprendre le monde tel qu'il est — et agir dedans.

É


Le Collectif Malgré Tout, en partenariat avecle Cedetim et Rencontres et Débat Autrement, relance son cycle de séminaires mensuels.


Reprise du séminaire «

 

Comprendre et agir dans la complexité : pour une théorie de la situation

 

»


 |&nbsp7 septembre 2025


Le séminaire du collectif Malgré Tout « Penser et agir dans la complexité » fait sa rentrée pour nouvelle saison 2025/26 ! L' objectif de ce séminaire peut se résumer ainsi : chercher une nouvelle « terre ferme » (…)


Nous poursuivrons cette année notre étude théorique et pratique de la situation, comprise comme socle organique minimal de l'agir.


Premier séminaire de cette année :


Séminaire


Présentation des axes de la saison 2026/2027


Avec la fin de l'époque de l'homme - sujet autoproclamé face à un monde réduit au statut d'objet - se pose une question centrale : quelle instance multiple peut encore penser, sentir et agir dans le chaos contemporain

 

?


La crise actuelle produit un vécu quotidien marqué par la dispersion, l'impuissance et l'angoisse devant un monde qui échappe à nos grilles de lecture. Le travail que nous proposons repose sur un pari : faire de la situation le dispositif à partir duquel il devient possible d'affronter cette dispersion sans céder à la tentation d'un nouvel ordre disciplinaire.


autres dates


Une telle exigence suppose de rompre avec l'imaginaire occidental de la fixité, qui n'a cessé de chercher l'être du côté de ce qui demeure, se conserve et résiste au devenir. Notre époque appelle au contraire une réconciliation avec le devenir, non comme abandon à la dispersion, mais comme condition d'une éthique situationnelle du présent.


Comme nous l'avons précédemment montré, la complexité ne relève ni d'une théorie ni d'une simple interprétation. Elle constitue un mode objectif et concret du monde qui exige un changement de paradigme, capable de renouer avec la puissance d'agir.

author: Luan Matheus Santana
title: “Usem muito Gemini”: Educação vira porta de entrada das Big Techs no Piauí
content:
Zona leste de Teresina. A sala de aula de uma escola estadual tem estrutura similar às demais instituições de ensino do Piauí: é ampla, tem paredes claras e as mesas estão organizadas para atividades em grupo. Alguns elementos, porém, chamam atenção. A sala é equipada com Chromebooks. No centro, uma poltrona reproduz as cores e o formato do logotipo do Google. As mesas e cadeiras também seguem a paleta da multinacional: azul, vermelho, amarelo e verde. Ao fundo, ocupando praticamente toda a parede, um grande painel visual exibe a outra logomarca, a do Google for Education. 


“Gostaram dessa sala? Mais uma sala tecnológica, de inovação, padrão Google, viu?”, disse o então secretário estadual de educação do Piauí, Washington Bandeira, em vídeo compartilhado nas redes sociais na época. Depois, ele conta aos alunos com orgulho que o pessoal do Liceu paraibano visitou a sede do Google nos Estados Unidos.

“Usem muito o Gemini, porque o Google é nosso parceiro no ensino de IA”, completou, referindo-se à inteligência artificial.  


Publicação de Washington Bandeira sobre a parceria do estado do Piauí com o Google na área da educação


A “sala Google” no Centro de Educação Tecnológica Professor Darcy Ribeiro foi a primeira inaugurada pelo governo estadual, em 20 de março de 2025. À época, o espaço foi apresentado como um marco da modernização da educação pública. Além de Teresina, outras duas cidades do Piauí, Regeneração e Amarante, também instalaram “salas Google” em escolas da rede pública. Estes ambientes coloridos, porém, são apenas um símbolo da proximidade do governo do Piauí com o Google e demais Big Techs.


Pelo menos desde 2022, o governo do Piauí tem firmado contratos milionários com multinacionais de tecnologia. O governador do estado, Rafael Fontelles (PT), é candidato à reeleição e tem aparecido como favorito nas pesquisas de intenção de voto. 


Um levantamento realizado pela

Agência Pública

 identificou R$ 93,7 milhões em acordos diretos e indiretos firmados pelo governo do Piauí nos últimos quatro anos com empresas como Google, Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon Web Services (AWS), além de empresas locais que atuam como integradoras de serviços das multinacionais.

A maior parte destes contratos se referem a recursos para a área de educação. Foram R$ 36,4 milhões, mais de um terço do total. 


Os contratos destinam-se à compra de plataformas digitais, infraestrutura em nuvem, licenças de software, equipamentos, soluções de inteligência artificial e, em muitos casos, para contratação de revendedores e integradores nacionais. 


Parte desses recursos estão sendo investidos em tecnologia para o ensino de inteligência artificial nas escolas da rede pública. O estado foi o primeiro no Brasil a incluir a IA como disciplina obrigatória em 2024 – em algumas instituições, a ferramenta usada para o ensino de IA é a Teachable Machine, do Google. Em junho de 2026, o governo lançou um novo programa para levar o ensino de IA também às escolas municipais. Inicialmente, o projeto será implantado em 50 municípios, com previsão de alcançar todas as 224 cidades do Piauí até 2027. 


Pesquisadores, especialistas em educação digital e organizações de defesa de direitos digitais questionam o modelo adotado no Piauí e em outros estados da federação. Eles alertam para o risco de dependência tecnológica e para a ausência de mecanismos transparentes de governança, proteção de dados e avaliação do impacto dessas tecnologias. 


Inauguração da ‘sala Google’ em Teresina


“É evidente que tem uma assimetria de poder, um acúmulo de saberes e de tecnologia bastante desigual entre os países do Norte e do Sul global”, afirma Rodrigo Nejm, doutor em psicologia e especialista em direitos digitais e educação digital no Instituto Alana. Para ele, é completamente possível reconhecer as assimetrias de capacidade tecnológica sem, para isso, “legitimar uma dependência de submissão”. 


“O problema não é fazer uso de plataformas internacionais, mas é permitir que elas abusem e violem direitos dos estudantes no Brasil”, completa. Para Nejm, parte dos milhões de reais destinados à transformação digital da educação deveria ser utilizada para desenvolver “soluções livres, nacionais, se possível, mas que fossem auditáveis, transparentes, para que, por exemplo, o Tribunal de Contas ou um profissional da imprensa pudesse ter acesso integral a informações sobre o critério de funcionamento, ou as evidências das ciências da aprendizagem que fundamentam”, explica …

author: Katja Diehl
title: 2,5 Milliarden. Verbrennen.
content:
Es ist leider gar nicht so schwer, DIE Stimme zur intersektionalen Mobilitätstransformation zu sein, wenn Gesellschaft und Politik bis heute bei Mobilität Auto und am liebsten auch Verbrenner denken.


2,5 Milliarden Euro für fossile Kraftstoffe – was wäre damit möglich?


Bund und Länder haben sich auf einen erneuten Tankrabatt ab dem 1. Oktober 2026 geeinigt. Es ist bereits der dritte Versuch innerhalb weniger Jahre, steigende Spritpreise durch kurzfristige Steuersenkungen zu kompensieren. Während massiv in die Subventionierung von Benzin und Diesel investiert wird, bleiben die strukturellen Defizite im öffentlichen Nahverkehr ungelöst.


Aus Sicht der Mobilitätsgerechtigkeit stellt sich mir die Frage:


Wie lange wollen wir noch mit der Gießkanne Milliarden ausschütten, während für jede Wahlfreiheit in der Mobilität durch Busse, Bahnen, Radwege angeblich kein Geld da ist?


Menschen in Armut, die auf das Auto angewiesen sind, ein geringes Einkommen haben und oft in ländlichen Regionen leben, wo Alternativen fehlen.


Mit denselben 2,5 Milliarden Euro ließen sich Hunderte Kilometer neuer Radwege bauen, On-Demand-Rufbus-Systeme im ländlichen Raum etablieren oder kindgerechte, sichere Räume schaffen. Selbst ein flächendeckendes Sozialticket wäre finanzierbar.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Trump Administration Aims to “Asphyxiate” Cuba Into Submission, Diplomat Says
content:

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

As the United Nations General Assembly opens in New York, we speak with senior Cuban diplomat Carlos Fernández de Cossío, who says the Trump administration is seeking to “asphyxiate the people of Cuba into submission.” On Friday, millions in Cuba lost power in what was at least the sixth major blackout since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. “We will do all we can to stop any nation, the U.S. or any nation, from taking over Cuba,” says Fernández de Cossío, who has served as deputy Cuban foreign minister since 2022.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman in New York. Juan González is in Chicago.

As world leaders gather for the United Nations General Assembly here in New York, we turn now to look at Cuba, which is facing a growing humanitarian crisis amidst an escalating economic war waged by the Trump administration. AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, the CIA recently formed a new secret Cuba task force as part of a widening U.S. effort to pressure Cuba. The U.S. has made many attempts to overthrow the Cuban government over the past 65 years, hundreds of attempts. CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: It is an honor.

AMY GOODMAN: Thanks so much for being with us. I’m glad we’re within the 25-mile zone that you’re allowed to travel in in New York. Right? Twenty-five miles from Columbus Circle?

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: Columbus Circle, yes.

AMY GOODMAN: Number one, if you can talk about what is — as the foreign minister addresses the United Nations, what’s the Cuban government’s message to the Trump administration as it tightens the economic sanctions and embargo?

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: We will be speaking to the international community at the U.N., not necessarily to the U.S. government, but the U.S. belongs to the international community. We live in a world which has become very dangerous, where expansionism, the ambition of domination, the attempts to take over the natural resources of developing countries has come back to the stage. The U.N. was created precisely for that not to happen, and has developed precisely for not that to happen, yet as reality today as a result of a foreign policy that is conceptualized as peace through force, which implies imposing the will of the U.S. through intimidation, aggression, coercion and so on. So, that’s one point that we need to talk.

We need to talk about the plight of the people of Cuba, because the aggression of the United States against Cuba today has a very serious human face …

author: Corey Larocque
title: Kivalliq Trade Show gets underway in Rankin Inlet
content:
News Sep 22, 2026 – 1:30 pm EDT

Rankin Inlet Mayor Harry Towtongie welcomes exhibitors to the Kivalliq Trade Show during a meet-and-greet reception for about 150 people Monday night in the hamlet’s community hall. The theme of the three-day business event is “Naalagit: Listen.” Speeches from Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. president Gloria Uluqsi and Nunavut Senator Nancy Karetak-Lindell are on Tuesday’s agenda, as well as the start of exhibits from regional businesses. The trade show runs until Wednesday. (Photo by Corey Larocque)

author: Roaa Reda
title: Three months on, citizens await answers after appealing disqualification from subsidies
content:
During an evening visit this week to a

subsidized grocery store

in Giza, Mada Masr asked the employee at the counter about how customers have been affected since the government began cancelling citizens’ ration cards three months ago.


The store employee said around 200 people who used to get their subsidized goods from his shop have had their cards suspended.


He believed many of those customers had been wrongly disqualified from the system.

They include families whose children are enrolled in private schools charging well below

LE20,000 per year and

 people who once owned cars, but sold them long ago.


Yet, none of these customers have had their subsidies reinstated since the window for grievances

opened July 14, he said. 


The government began in June to suspend ration cards for hundreds of thousands of citizens under its new “social justice” eligibility criteria. But three months on, official state bodies have yet to give a definitive answer on when these appeals will be resolved.


This month, when Mada Masr tried to understand whether the grievance system was working, we heard a similar story repeated in conversations with people who work in or with the subsidy system, from the street level to municipal supply offices and governorate authorities. All of them said they had no idea when or how the government would start reviewing grievances and reinstating subsidies for those proven eligible. And most said that none of the citizens who had filed grievances had received a response, with one source citing “seven or eight” restorations at most.


The lack of response leaves the thousands who have filed grievances in limbo, prompting MPs to press the government not only for a clear decision, but also to ask whether there will be compensation for the monthslong wrongful suspensions that have left card holders without access to subsidies.


The confusion in the supply system exposes many families to mounting price pressures, especially as inflation spikes, leaving many uncertain about the future as the government transitions the entire commodities subsidy system to a cash assistance model that relies on digital credit allocations. 


***


To verify whether any

complainants

 have regained access to their subsidies, a Mada Masr correspondent went to a ration office in Giza and asked about the fate of appeals.

 Staff there said that, so far, not a single person who had filed a grievance has been reinstated into the system. The office could only check the status of a ration card and see how far it is in the appeal process.


Another ration office employee in Sohag, Zain al-Abideen, reiterated the same, saying that of the citizens he had helped to file grievances, not a single one was reinstated. 


Mada Masr also spoke to Badawy Dabour, who works independently to support people submitting subsidy appeals in Qalyubiya. Dabour said he had helped a large number of people file grievances, but only seven or eight have had their cards restored.


Dabour also mentioned other cases of wrongful disqualification: people with old cars, or whose children aren’t enrolled in private schools.


While citizens wait for the results of their appeals, no government body has disclosed when they can expect a response. 


In televised statements, Supply Minister Spokesperson Ahmed Kamal

said

 in August that the grievance process happens in two stages, with citizens required to submit data first via the Digital Egypt platform or via post office branches that have been dedicated to supporting grievance requests.


The second stage is going to a

ration office

with a statement confirming that they don’t own the assets for which they have been wrongfully disqualified.

 


Once cards are reactivated, he said, beneficiaries would get a text message notification. He said people would be returned to the system starting August 1, but did not say how long the review process would take. 


But this has not happened in the majority of cases, and when Mada Masr directed the question to Supply Ministry spokesperson Ahmed Kamal, asking whether the ministry has set a specific date for reactivating the cards of citizens whose eligibility has been proven, he said the work of examining and reviewing the grievances was ongoing.


Several MPs

have


directed


the

 same question to ministers via Parliament.
